News.title: Agit Kabayel is the ringmaster of a new heavyweight circus
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

There was a time when an American was in one corner of every single heavyweight world-title fight. Every fight from the end of the bare-knuckle period to the end of the 1980s.

The fall of the Wall and the arrival of the Eastern Bloc boxers changed the landscape forever, but still Americans held the grip on a title that seemed forever destined to be owned by a man from Philadelphia or Houston or Louisville. That is all over now, possibly gone for good.

Deontay Wilder was the last American heavyweight world champion, and he was beaten in seven rounds by Tyson Fury in early 2020; he challenged Fury the following year, lost again, and that was the last time an American came anywhere near the world heavyweight title.

open image in gallery Agit Kabayel after stopping Zhilei Zhang in early 2025 ( Getty )

Close to 30 years ago, Don King announced that he was searching for the next American heavyweight superstar; that desperate search is continuing today, and at the same time gyms in Tirana, Moscow and Lagos are full of heavyweight dreamers.

This Saturday, in front of 50,000 fans in Dusseldorf, Germany’s Agit Kabayel defends his WBC heavyweight title when he meets the unbeaten Nelson Hysa of Albania. It is a bizarrely cosmopolitan clash. Kabayel, on his way directly to the WBC title, stopped in succession a Russian, a Chinese fighter, a Croatian, a Pole, and a Cuban. There is not an American heavyweight left to come even close to pushing Kabayel.

The top American is arguably a man called Michael Hunter, who is 38 and had his best win in 2018. Hunter is the only American worth a top-20 ranking, and he is lost in a turbulent sea of boxers from a dozen countries. A Nigerian, an Australian and about seven British boxers are in front of Hunter. Where is Rocky Balboa when you need him?

Right now, Kabayel might just be the best of the four heavyweight champions, with Daniel Dubois, Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev holding the other belts in the wake of Oleksandr Usyk giving up all of the gold.

Kabayel vs Hysa Tale of the tape Kabayel – Record: 27-0 (19 KOs); height: 6ft 3in; reach: 80in; age: 34. Hysa – Record: 25-0 (23 KOs); height: 6ft 5in; reach: 79in; age: 42.

And Kabayel, 34, can look good against Hysa who, at 42, is wandering close to George Foreman’s ancient territory. It will be fun until Kabayel does his thing and breaks Hysa’s heart after about six rounds of body shots.

Kabayel started three of his last four bouts as the underdog, fighting men with unbeaten records or a genuine claim to a higher ranking. On each occasion, he slowly prodded away and calmly broke the spirit and desire of a trio of quality men. A similar win against Hysa, who is a big lump and offers a lot of bulk for Kabayel to target, will raise Kabayel’s profile against the other champions.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

open image in gallery Nelson Hysa (top) last fought in August, stopping Thomas Narmo in two rounds ( Getty )

It will also leave Kabayel and his devoted following in a very strong position next year, when we know what Anthony Joshua and Fury are doing.

The distant and fond memories of glorious heavyweight championship fights at New York’s Madison Square Garden and the MGM in Las Vegas are fading fast. Meanwhile, Melbourne, Zagreb and Tashkent are getting ready for the big show. The new circus starts on Saturday in Dusseldorf.

News.title: The Davis Cup is broken but Carlos Alcaraz can save it
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For nearly five months of this year, Carlos Alcaraz was sidelined, nursing a wrist injury which threatened to derail his entire season. Just three months on from his return, and despite managing two different injury concerns, the Spaniard has rewritten the history books and could yet send another record tumbling before signing off for Christmas.

Four days after claiming his first ATP Finals title, becoming the youngest man – at just 23 – to complete the clean sweep of all four majors and the season-ending individual crown, he could join only Andre Agassi, Novak Djokovic, and Roger Federer in the pantheon of greats to also win the Davis Cup.

The tennis calendar doesn’t so much slow to a halt over Christmas as barrel almost cleanly through into the next season, with a rapid turnaround for those heading from the ATP Finals in Turin to the Davis Cup in Bologna this week. But despite Alcaraz’s frenetic autumn schedule, winning three back-to-back tournaments in Vienna, Paris, and Turin, and the wear and tear on his body, he is in spellbinding form and highly fancied to lead Spain to a first title since 2019.

The Davis Cup has struggled for relevance in recent years. The fact that it takes place annually lowers the stakes and drama of what claims to be the ‘World Cup’ of tennis, while the torturously convoluted system of play-offs and qualifying ties makes it difficult for the casual fan to understand. Add to that top players’ reluctance to risk injury, and their prioritising of the ATP Tour in an utterly relentless calendar, means the big names tend to drop out and viewers’ interest follows the same downward curve.

So it is a huge boost to the tournament that although home star Jannik Sinner remains a long-term absentee, Alcaraz, who missed last year’s Finals, is back, while the Italians – led again by Flavio Cobolli – are fielding a raft of top names including Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti. In total, nine top-10 players across both singles and doubles will take part, and seven of the singles top-20.

Three-time defending champions Italy face underdogs South Korea before taking on either Felix Auger-Aliassime’s Canada or Czechia, spearheaded by the top-20 pairing of Jakub Mensik and Jiri Lehecka. The bottom half sees Germany and Spain take on Great Britain and Austria respectively.

GB are playing their last tie under the leadership of Leon Smith, who will end a near-17 year stint as captain after this week. There are no faces left from the Finals-winning squad of 2015, the zenith of Smith’s tenure, but there is an exciting mix of the old and new: this year’s breakout British star, Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery, alongside stalwart Cameron Norrie. Most significantly, GB possess a lethal doubles partnership in world No 1 Henry Patten and No 3 Neal Skupski, who between them have won three of the last four Grand Slams.

open image in gallery Italy are bidding for a fourth title in succession ( Reuters )

Smith’s faith in his first-choice doubles pairing (but perhaps also a sign of the comparatively limited overall resources at his disposal) is indicated by the fact that he has named no reserve player, while every other team in the quarter-finals is fielding a full squad of five.

In all likelihood, defeat in the best-of-three tie against Germany still beckons – Fery took just two games off Zverev, his counterpart as national No 1, in their most recent meeting in Vienna, while world No 45 Norrie is evenly matched against No 39 Jan-Lennard Struff. But that elite doubles pairing could swing it and set up a blockbuster tie against Spain (who are unlikely to be unduly troubled by Austria, whose highest-ranked singles player is Jurij Rodionov, the world No 142).

So the likely outcome is a semi-final rematch between the current world No 1 and the best player on the planet at the moment. Zverev looked formidable throughout his run at the ATP Finals and did not drop serve until facing Alcaraz in the final, when he saved three break points in his opening service game and was promptly broken in his second, and he was unable to take advantage of dips in concentration from the Spaniard in the second set to force a decider.

open image in gallery World No 10 Rafael Jodar adds extra firepower to the Spanish team ( Getty )

If Zverev does earn his revenge, Alcaraz’s deputy is Rafael Jodar, who set a record for the shortest time between making his Tour debut and breaking into the top-10 in the world: just 287 days. The 20-year-old is a force to be reckoned with in his own right and Spain’s firepower is why they are favourites to make the final – and set up a re-run of the 2025 showpiece against Italy.

Organisers and viewers alike will wish Sinner was there, nearly eight months on from the one and only ‘Sincaraz’ meeting of this season. But it feels increasingly likely that Alcaraz’s magnetism alone will be enough to power this tournament.

He has rectified his comparative vulnerability on indoor hard courts and learned to play more intelligently rather than just spectacularly as he manages knee and hamstring issues, and arrives in Bologna evolving but still miles above the rest, as that victory over Zverev on Sunday showed. At the end of another brilliant campaign – condensed into half a normal one – that Davis Cup title is his and Spain’s for the taking, and would be just reward for a player who continues to defy all expectations of what is possible.

News.title: Is Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Champions League fixture
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Arsenal return to Champions League action against Borussia Dortmund hoping to extend their unbeaten start to Europe’s premier competition this season.

The Gunners return to the Emirates after dropping points in the Premier League title race thanks to a Newcastle comeback at the weekend - although rivals Manchester City and Brighton both failed to capitalise and close the gap to the league leaders.

Dortmund are just one point behind them in the Champions League group stage rankings but nine places below, having got past Real Betis 2-1 in their last encounter, while the Gunners beat Slavia Prague by the same scoreline.

Arsenal and Dortmund have not faced off since 2014 - when Mikel Arteta wore the captain’s armband in a 2-0 Arsenal victory.

Here’s everything you need to know.

When is Arsenal v Dortmund?

Arsenal host Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, London on Tuesday 24 November, with kick-off at 8pm.

How can I watch it?

Viewers in the UK can watch the game on Amazon Prime Video. If you're not an Amazon Prime Video subscriber start a free 30-day trial here.

Team news

Arteta was relieved to announce that the injury to David Raya, which saw him withdrawn against Newcastle after a collision with Will Osula, will not require surgery, but the first-choice keeper will miss out on Tuesday. He will be replaced between the sticks by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Bukayo Saka remains out for another four weeks while Martin Zubimendi is another injury absentee, although William Saliba could pick up a few minutes as he manages his return from a long-term back injury.

Dortmund are sweating on the fitness of Serhou Guirassy, who picked up a hamstring injury against Real Betis, while Carney Chukwuemeka is another doubt and the likes of Emre Can and Justin Lerma are definite absentees.

Predicted line-ups

Arsenal XI: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres

Dortmund XI: Kobel; Schlotterbeck, Anton, Bensebaini; Ryerson, Nmecha, Bellingham, Svensson; Karetsas, Beier; Silva

News.title: Two Americans jailed for life for murder of Canadian entrepreneur on small Caribbean island
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Two American men ​were sentenced to life in prison on the Caribbean island of Dominica on Monday for the 2023 murder of Canadian tech entrepreneur Daniel Langlois and his partner Dominique ⁠Marchand, local media reported.

A court in Roseau, the capital of Dominica, handed down two consecutive life sentences each to Jonathan Lehrer and Robert Snyder Jr. on Monday, local media reported.

The two American men were sentenced for the 2023 murder of Canadian tech entrepreneur Langlois and his partner.

Langlois and Marchand were killed on December 1, 2023, in what the judge described as "an unprovoked attack," saying the case was "the rarest of the rare," according to local media.

The pair had been held in custody since their arrest days after the killings.

They were convicted on July 28 this year.

Their lawyer has said they will appeal the sentencing.

Langlois founded Montreal-based Softimage, whose 3-D animation technology was used in major Hollywood productions including "Jurassic Park," "The Matrix" and "Titanic." He and Marchand owned the Coulibri Ridge eco-resort in southern Dominica.

The couple had been missing for several days when their burned bodies were found in a car near Gallion, close to the resort.

open image in gallery Roseau in Dominica, Caribbean ( Getty/iStock )

Lehrer, a New Jersey-born chocolate maker, owned land next to the resort.

Snyder, a mechanic, worked for Lehrer.

Court documents show Lehrer had a years-long dispute with Langlois over a road that crossed his property and led to the resort.

In 2019, a judge ordered Lehrer to make the road available to the public and to let Langlois' visitors pass without any limits.

Representatives for Lehrer's family have disputed that the feud over the road was behind the killings.

Last week, family spokesperson Sylvie Deslauriers released a statement on behalf of Langlois' mother.

In it, the mother said that her son's ashes had recently been brought back to Canada, where she was able to lay him to rest almost three years after the killings.

News.title: Asian stocks soar after Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Asian stocks rallied on Tuesday, led by semiconductor companies in Taiwan and South Korea, after Nvidia reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as its chief executive, triggering a sharp rebound in US technology shares and reviving confidence in the artificial intelligence sector.

Taiwan’s Taiex led regional gains, rising more than nine per cent, as shares in chipmakers Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and MediaTek climbed nearly 10 per cent.

South Korea’s Kospi advanced 6.5 per cent to 5,014.41, with Samsung Electronics gaining 7.5 per cent and SK Hynix rising 8.6 per cent.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed 3.9 per cent to 58,654.40 after markets reopened following a public holiday. Chip equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron rose 10.5 per cent, while testing equipment maker Advantest surged 14.1 per cent.

open image in gallery US president Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during the 'A New Golden Age' summit at the US Institute of Peace ( Reuters )

"We are seeing a reaction to the rally in US tech stocks overnight on the announcement that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA as the CEO," said Neil Newman, managing director and head of strategy at Astris Advisory Japan.

"It is obviously a big surprise and a knock-on effect will be through Asia," Mr Newman said.

Elsewhere, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged 0.2 per cent higher to 22,432.45, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.7 per cent to 3,563.58. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 1.7 per cent to 8,718.80.

The regional gains followed a sharp recovery on Wall Street on Monday, where Nvidia shares surged 31.5 per cent after the company announced Huang’s reinstatement, adding nearly $1tn to its market value.

The S&P 500 jumped 4.7 per cent, its strongest daily performance since April 2025, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 6.5 per cent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained nearly three per cent.

open image in gallery A silhouette of Jensen Huang, the NVIDIA logo and a rising stock graph in this illustration, created on 23 November 2026 ( Reuters )

The rally ended a seven-session losing streak for the S&P 500, which had fallen more than 10 per cent below its record high amid mounting concerns about technology valuations and the sustainability of investment in artificial intelligence.

Huang’s return reversed an earlier decision by Nvidia’s board rejecting his comeback. The board reinstated him as president and chief executive after receiving assurances that he did not pose a national security risk.

Mr Huang resigned from the company he helped found on 12 November, after reports of a number of affairs, including with one woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

In the time since, Donald Trump and many tech leaders called for his return and a petition supporting him gathered hundreds of thousands of signatures – leading Mr Huang to report that he would return to the company if its board asked him to.

US president Donald Trump said he had intervened in the decision. Speaking to CNBC on Monday, he said: "I believe my intervention was very important" in persuading the board to reinstate the Nvidia co-founder.

open image in gallery A woman poses for a photo with the Nvidia logo outside the company's headquarters after it said on Monday it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, in Santa Clara, California, US, 23 November 2026 ( Reuters )

Mr Trump also said his administration had assured the company that Mr Huang’s return did not raise national security concerns.

The reinstatement helped restore confidence in an AI industry heavily dependent on Nvidia for its advanced chips and financing for parts of the sector's expansion.

"The return of the most important man in the AI industry to the helm of its most important company has eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade, at least at the margins," Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, told Reuters.

However, investors remained cautious about the outlook for technology stocks, with concerns over slowing AI investment, earnings growth and the cost of expanding data-centre infrastructure continuing to weigh on the sector.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

The rebound also lifted broader Asian technology shares, with the MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rising 4.6 per cent, recovering from an eight-month low, according to Reuters. The index was heading for its biggest single-day gain in two weeks.

The recovery came as investors reassessed the risks facing the AI industry following last week’s sell-off. Nvidia’s central role in supplying chips and supporting the expansion of AI infrastructure has made its performance an important influence on global technology stocks.

In the bond market, the yield on the US 10-year Treasury note edged higher to around 4.94 per cent, while the dollar strengthened amid renewed expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy, Reuters reported.

Oil prices fell more than 3 per cent on Monday, with Brent crude settling at $89.37 a barrel, before trading movements on Tuesday.

News.title: Tube strikes this week: What you need to know about Thursday’s walkout and future dates
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Passengers are being warned of tube strikes affecting the whole network this Thursday, with more dates to follow in the lead-up to Christmas.

The Rail, Maritime and Transport union (RMT) announced eight sets of 24-hour strikes starting in November, ending in February 2027 over plans for a voluntary four-day week for drivers.

The first walkout will take place on Thursday, 26 November, and is expected to cause disruption across all Tube lines.

The RMT suspended planned strikes in March and May this year after progress in talks, but there has not yet been news of a suspension.

Representatives from Transport for London (TfL) and the union are due to meet for last-ditch talks on Tuesday to try to reach an agreement ahead of the first strike on Thursday.

The Tube drivers’ strikes land on some of the busiest days of the year, including the last weekend before Christmas Day.

Here’s everything we know so far about the upcoming strike dates.

When are the tube strikes?

Some Tube drivers plan to strike on certain dates from November 2026 to February 2027, affecting the whole network.

If they go ahead, the 24-hour strikes will run from midday on the first day to midday the following day.

November 2026

12pm Thursday 26 to 11.59am Friday 27 November 2026

December 2026

12pm Thursday 17 to 11.59am Friday 18 December 2026

12pm Saturday 19 to 11.59am Sunday 20 December 2026

January 2027

12pm Monday 4 to 11.59am Tuesday 5 January 2027

12pm Wednesday 6 to 11.59am Thursday 7 January 2027

February 2027

12pm Wednesday 17 to 11.59am Thursday 18 February 2027

12pm Tuesday 23 to 11.59am Wednesday 24 February 2027

12pm Thursday 25 to 11.59am Friday 26 February 2027

Which lines are affected during the driver’s strike?

There will likely be some disruption across all Tube lines, but TfL said trains will run on most lines during the Tube driver’s strike, although it didn’t give further information.

The Elizabeth line, DLR, London Overground, buses and trams will be running as normal during the strikes but will be busier than usual.

What advice is being given to travellers?

Passengers are being told to plan ahead and check the live train timetables during the strikes.

TfL added that passengers should allow more time than usual to complete their journey.

Why are strikes taking place?

RMT has announced strike dates in retaliation over plans to impose new working arrangements, including a voluntary four-day week, which the union says would mean drivers face spending more time driving trains, longer duties, earlier starts and later finishes.

The union has also raised concerns that the proposals would pave the way for hundreds of job cuts, with initial rosters published for the Bakerloo line indicating significant reductions in staffing.

“London Underground is attempting to dress up a wholesale attack on drivers’ working conditions as a voluntary four-day week,” RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey said.

“But there is nothing voluntary about a scheme that forces drivers to give up existing protections whether they work four days or five, and threatens those who refuse with displacement from their depots.

He added: “RMT is not opposed to a genuine four-day working week that benefits our members, but we will not accept it being used as a vehicle for job cuts, intensified working and the erosion of terms and conditions.”

Aslef, Britain's trade union for train drivers, said the switch to a four-day week would give train drivers an extra 35 days off a year.

“We are surprised that the RMT has, once again, decided to take strike action to try to prevent Underground drivers moving to a four-day week on a voluntary basis,” Finn Brennan, Aslef’s full-time organiser on London Underground, said.

He added: “The voluntary four-day week gives Tube train drivers an extra 35 days off every year with rosters based on a 34-hour week in return for some changes to working conditions and moving to electronic, rather than paper-based, systems for booking on for duty.

“We are in discussions with Transport for London about how the final details of this will work in practice.

“Management have agreed that anyone who wants to keep working a five-day week will be able to do so without suffering any detriment, and we will be holding them to that.

“A strike designed to stop people having the choice of a shorter working week and more time off is a strange choice to make.”

Nick Dent, director of customer operations for London Underground, managed by TfL, said: “We have engaged with our trade unions for months about our proposal for a new four-day working week.

“As a result of that engagement, drivers can now choose to remain on a five-day week with a guarantee of remaining at the same depot.

“This will give our colleagues a real, meaningful choice on their working pattern without having to change where they work.

“This will also mean less time at work for Tube drivers, while delivering a more efficient, reliable Tube service for our customers.

“Given that we have provided this new option after their feedback, we urge the RMT to put this proposal to their members.”

News.title: Just 1pc of research funding spent on maternal death prevention, analysis suggests
News.content:
Only one per cent of research funding is spent on preventing leading causes of maternal deaths, analysis suggests.

Just $306 million (£233 million) was spent between 2023 and 2025 on tackling the four leading causes of maternal and child mortality in low-and-middle-income countries, according to a joint report by the non-profits Program for Appropriate Technology in Health (Path) and Impact Global Health.

The four causes are: postpartum haemorrhage, the loss of more than 500 ml of blood within 24 hours after birth; pre-eclampsia, new-onset high blood pressure and organ stress during pregnancy; maternal anaemia, when a women doesn’t have enough red blood cells to carry oxygen around her body and to her baby; and pre-term birth.

The greatest need is in sub-Saharan Africa, which accounts for around 70 per cent of maternal deaths globally. Some 182,000 women in the region died of pregnancy complications in 2023, according to the World Health Organization.

Funding for maternal health research and development (R&D) is notoriously fragile. Between 2023-25, the US National Institutes of Health and the Gates Foundation provided three quarters of funding to tackle the four leading maternal mortality conditions. Industry contributed just one per cent.

“A single shift in one funder’s priorities could reshape the whole field,” said Sabastine Wakdok, director of research at Impact Global Health.

“The women carrying the greatest risk deserve a far broader and more stable base of investment,” he said.

News.title: Wall Street stocks soar as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
News.content:
US tech stocks staged a dramatic recovery on Monday after Nvidia’s shock decision to reinstate Jensen Huang.

The value of the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained nearly $2 trillion as investors rushed back into AI-linked companies following a bruising sell-off last week.

The index closed up 6.9pc late Monday after rising as much as 7.7pc, regaining its losses during last week’s rout.

Nvidia shares surged as much as 34pc, their biggest one-day gain in 25 years, after the company reinstated Mr Huang following pressure from President Trump. They closed up 31pc.

Markets had been poised to gain ground as investors took stock following a bruising sell-off driven by darkening sentiment about AI.

But the recovery was boosted by a statement from Nvidia shortly before markets opened confirming the return of its founder.

Trading in Nasdaq futures was briefly halted before markets opened because of the huge volatility.

Mr Huang had stepped down from the chip giant earlier this month in the wake of revelations of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and another with a colleague.

Nvidia said it made its decision with “input from senior levels of the United States government”.

Mr Trump on Monday said he had “convinced” Nvidia to reinstate Mr Huang.

The rebound in stocks will help to ease concerns about the AI bubble bursting as investors begin to question whether AI companies will be able to recoup the vast sums of money being pumped into the industry.

The benchmark S&P 500 closed up 4.7pc, while the Dow Jones gained around 3pc.

Mr Huang later attended Nvidia’s headquarters, telling staff he would be a “better CEO the second time around”.

News.title: Dengue more widespread than previously thought
News.content:
Dengue is much more widespread than previously thought, researchers have warned, raising concerns that the threat has been underestimated and resources misallocated.

An analysis of global data from 1990 to 2024 found that there were 73.9 million cases of the mosquito-borne disease – 10.6 million more than previously captured.

“Collectively these data show that dengue is expanding faster, more consistently and more intensely than previously thought,” the authors from institutions in the UK, the US, South Africa and Singapore wrote.

Dengue, nicknamed breakbone fever, is spread by the Aedes mosquito and it can cause intense muscle, joint and bone aches. The severe form of the disease can be fatal, and it poses a significant burden on low and middle-income countries.

The research, presented at the annual meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in Maryland, comes as countries including Bangladesh, Malaysia and Cuba are being hit hard by outbreaks of the disease.

The paper, not yet published in a journal, found that global incidence rose 34-fold between 1990 and 2024, an average annual jump of 9.1 per cent. Cases rose most rapidly in regions where the virus has recently emerged – Africa, the Middle East and South Asia – and more slowly in Southeast Asia, where it’s been established for decades.

Researchers found the missing cases by combing through uncounted sources, like ministry of health PDFs and graphics that never made it into global datasets. They then combined this with modelling, to pull together a single database that tracks 35 years of cases by month, allowing scientists to test new hypotheses.

News.title: Any regrets, Mauricio? Man Utd are deep in relegation battle after Anfield farce
News.content:
Bruno Fernandes says he has shelved talks over a new contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but said all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”

Fernandes said claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the issue he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he said.

“There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”

United chief executive Omar Berrada said of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his new contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes said the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

“Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”

News.title: Midges pose a growing health threat to Britons, experts warn
News.content:
Midges pose a growing health threat to people in Britain, experts have warned.

Like mosquitoes, midges can act as disease carriers, picking up pathogens when they bite infected animals and potentially passing them on when they feed on another host.

The UK is home to more than 650 species of midge, mostly concentrated in Scotland.

While some are harmless, others are already known to spread serious animal diseases, including Bluetongue and Schmallenberg – viruses that cause severe illness and, in some cases, death in livestock including cattle, sheep and goats.

“Most of the diseases transmitted by midges affect animals, but recently there has been evidence that they play more of a role in human disease,” Professor Heather Ferguson, an infectious disease ecologist at the University of Glasgow, told The Telegraph.

Last month, a man in France died after contracting the first-ever human case of Shamonda virus, a midge-borne disease previously only known to infect animals.

The virus, which is now widespread in European animals and was detected in British cattle earlier this month, has historically been confined to sub-Saharan Africa.

In other parts of the world, midges are already known to spread serious diseases to people.

Across South and Central America, thousands of people have been diagnosed with Oropouche virus in recent years, a midge-borne disease that is particularly dangerous for pregnant women and their unborn children.

Brazil – which has recorded more than 13,000 cases of Oropouche since 2023 – has launched a probe into the links between the virus and pregnancy.

It fears the disease could cause a tragedy similar to that of the 2015 Zika epidemic, which left more than 3,000 Brazilian children permanently disabled after being infected in utero.

“This midge-borne virus historically was thought to only be transmitted between animals and wildlife, mainly in forest areas,” Dr Christopher Sanders, an entomologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

“But over the past couple of years, it has emerged in South America and parts of Central America where it’s actually being transmitted in cities and causing infections in humans, so that is obviously a concern”.

News.title: Verstappen mocks ‘absolute joke’ Russell after thrilling Las Vegas win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, coming to you from very early on a Sunday morning (if you are in the eastern hemisphere) and very late on a Sunday night (if you are in the western hemisphere).

It is a strange race in a strange place, but this is now the fourth edition of the race and it looks to be here to stay for all its strangeness. It does present the teams with problems and problems are there to be solved or negotiated as well as can be in F1. That is the name of the game.

In qualifying yesterday the world champion, Kimi Antonelli, did that expertly, sneaking in at the end to finish fastest. He does, however, take a five-place grid penalty, so will be starting in sixth. Taking first place on the grid will be the in-form Max Verstappen, followed by George Russell, who could do with a strong finish to the season.

Russell seemed miffed about missing out on pole position, particularly with how Mercedes managed the qualifying situation, particularly with how the tow was managed. Antonelli was always going to take a grid penalty, so why give him the tow, was Russell’s reasoning.

In any case, Russell has a good chance to take his third victory this season. At least on paper. Russell’s qualifying has probably been his strongest suit this season, but race days have let him down. Let us not forget that Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, starts third.

There could be a bit of aggro on the first lap, given Russell and Verstappen’s “disagreement” yesterday, but let’s see. It may end up being a clean race.

It all starts in about an hour and we will be here for all the updates and reaction from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

News.title: Wales ‘frustrated’ after being brought back down to earth by Wallabies
News.content:
Wales have a spring in their step coming into their game tonight as they host Australia at the Principality Stadium. Wales pulled off one of their best wins in recent memory last weekend, ending an over 70-year with for a victory over New Zealand. Despite pulling off that shock victory, Wales sit down in fifth in the northern hemisphere standings coming into this final round of fixtures. In all likelihood, they can only improve one spot. They have made four changes from the historic win over the All Blacks, with the likes of Josh Adams and Aaron Wainwright coming in.

“We were all immensely proud to make history last week,” Wales head coach Steve Tandy said. “There is a new opportunity and challenge for us against Australia and we are looking to back up our performance this weekend. It is our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we cannot wait to get back out at Principality Stadium.

“We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition. The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players. We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend. The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance.”

Sports.title: Nicky Butt launches blistering attack on ‘worst Man Utd team ever seen’ and brands club ‘disaster from top to bottom’
Sports.content:
Next

NICKY BUTT has ripped into Manchester United’s big-name players after seeing their season go from bad to worse.

The Red Devils suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to arch-rivals Liverpool on Sunday.



And United, who had newly-appointed boss Mauricio Pochettino in the dugout for the first time, are just one point clear of rock bottom Crystal Palace.

Butt, 51, launched a blistering attack after seeing the Red Devils only bag ONE Premier League win this season.



The Old Trafford legend told Sports Uncensored: “If we’re honest, it was one of them ones where you’re hoping for a bounce effect for a new manager and we’re just kidding ourselves.

“It would have been a disaster if that happened because it would have proved they are kidders, which a lot of us think some of the players are.



“But to expect anything from this group of footballers at the minute is just too much.

“They’re just not physically capable of doing it. They’re, physically, the worst United team I’ve ever seen – and that’s in all my time of watching. I’m 51 now, so it’s a hell of a long time watching United.

“I think Liverpool are doing a lot better, [although] I don’t think they’re a great Liverpool team.

“But physically we just got dominated and that’s before we even start talking about the football side of it.

“It was an all-time low. Let’s be honest, it’s what we’ve come to expect at the minute from United.

“It’s sad. It hurts people that love the football club and have been around it for a long, long time. But it is just the fact of where we are at this moment in time.”

Butt reckons former team-mates have been right to call out Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family for United’s struggles.

Fans have also been protesting against the hierarchy, while director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada have come under fire.



Butt is also adamant United’s mega-money flops need to take responsibility after being thrashed by Liverpool following Leny Yoro’s early red card.

The six-time Premier League title winner said: “It is just fundamentally a disaster from top to bottom.

“But ultimately, when you go to Anfield, if you don’t compete in the minimum part of football – which is just hard work and graft – you’re dead.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino ‘to be handed tiny January transfer budget’ as Man Utd target three positions in need of fixing
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO wants three January signings to save Manchester United from relegation — but will only have a shoestring budget.

Pochettino, 54, is understood to want a new striker, left-back and centre-back with the club 19th in the Prem table.



But, according to The Mail, United chiefs will give the Argentine just £50million to get them.

Monaco hitman Folarin Balogun, who thrived under Pochettino over the last two years with the USA team, is top of the boss’ wishlist.



United have struggled for goals this season with main striker Benjamin Sesko ruled out with a shin injury until January.

Balogun, 25, has impressed in Ligue 1 for Monaco since quitting Arsenal three years ago.

He has only managed one goal in eight appearances across all competitions this season, having seen a deadline day move to Everton sensationally fall through at the eleventh hour.

But he was the star of the show for the USA in the summer — including being at the centre of controversy over a red card against Bosnia.

Balogun was meant to be suspended for the hosts’ last-16 clash with Belgium, until Fifa boss Gianni Infantino controversially lifted the sanction after a phone call from US president Donald Trump.

Left-back if another problem area with Luke Shaw missing the past eight matches.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A late loan move for Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri was considered in the summer.

Ait-Nouri, 25, has fallen down the pecking order at City and has only managed a mere total of four appearances, so an unlikely deal with United’s city rivals could be reignited.

While a change at centre-back cannot come soon enough after Pochettino’s horror first game in change against Liverpool.

United have previously been linked with Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, while Fulham’s Calvin Bassey has also emerged as a target.

Sports.title: Frozen assets from sale of Chelsea earned over £100million in interest last year
Sports.content:
Next

FROZEN assets from the sale of Chelsea earned over £100million in interest last year, The Sun can reveal.

Accounts for ex-owner, Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich, revealed the funds made £103.9million in interest, for the year to June 30 2025.



The sale funds have now generated close to £400million in interest since the club was sold four years ago.

Abramovich was forced to sell Chelsea for £4.25billion in 2022 after ­Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.



At the time, he said the proceeds would be donated to a charitable foundation to help victims of the war.

However, £2.5billion from the sale remains in a UK bank account due to a row with the Government over how the cash is used.

Abramovich has been warned by the government that he could be subjected to legal action after failing to release the billions from the sale to help Ukraine.

Karren Brady recently told The Sun the issue had been raised in the House of Lords earlier this month.

The government issued a licence in December last year providing a legal route for the cash to be transferred to a foundation for humanitarian purposes in Ukraine.

Britain wants the money to be used for victims in Ukraine only.



But Abramovich wants the money also spent in Russia – which is unacceptable to the Government.

Chelsea, who slumped to a miserable 4-1 defeat against Leeds on the weekend, was sold to US investor Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

Sports.title: Ethan Nwaneri was supposed to be Arsenal’s starboy but returns to Emirates in all too familiar situation with Dortmund
Sports.content:
Next

ETHAN NWANERI was supposed to be the Arsenal starboy.

Nwaneri had been discussed as one of Hale End’s brightest sparks when he first broke onto the scene, becoming the Premier League’s youngest-ever player aged just 15 years and 181 days in 2022.



And his breakout 2024/25 campaign showed even more promise as he banked nine goals across all competitions as a budding prospect.

Now, though, he returns to the Emirates Stadium as a Borussia Dortmund player, on yet another frustrating loan that has left him starved of game time.



The 19-year-old spent the second half of last season riding the bench for Marseille after Roberto De Zerbi was sacked just weeks after he sealed the French switch.

Arsenal had not included a recall clause in his contract, leaving the teenager stranded on the continent and limited to just four starts across his entire five-month spell at Marseille.



Now Nwaneri finds himself in a similar situation once again, however this time it has nothing to do with a change of managers.

Nwaneri’s loan move to Borussia Dortmund started off positively, forcing an own goal on his debut against Hoffenheim and starting the next three Bundesliga games.

But his minutes have dried up in recent weeks, amassing less than an hour of action across Dortmund’s last eight games across all competitions.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is aware of the lack of game time Nwaneri has been getting, but has urged him to earn his minutes.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Arteta said: “He started playing quite a lot, starting games, but recently he has not played that much.

“He needs to earn the right to play. He is playing at the top of the Bundesliga. The players that they have, they have huge talent and quality, and they are showing that, and that’s the reality of football.

“Because you go there and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn’t give you any advantage, so you need to earn it.

“Ethan has, first of all, the mindset to do it and then the quality to do it. These things are part of a journey and part of a season and he needs to reveal himself and earn the right to win.”

Dortmund are fighting on all fronts in Germany this season and are currently two points clear of Bayern Munich at the top of the Bundesliga.



The Yellow and Black have not lost in the league yet this season and boss Niko Kovac can’t be criticised for using Nwaneri so sparingly when the results are working in his side’s favour.

Kovac has cited the “fierce competition” that Nwaneri faces in the forward positions at Dortmund for his lack of game time.

Speaking last week, Kovac said: “We have some very strong players in those attacking positions. There’s some fierce competition.”



The versatile ace has had to compete with Konstantinos Karetsas, Maximilian Beier, Serhou Guirassy and Fabio Silva for a place in the Dortmund team this season.

During the international break, Nwaneri was able to play some more regular minutes, starring for England U21s with two assists against France and a confident performance against Portugal.

But Arteta reckons Nwaneri has to become a more consistent performer, rather than shining in moments.

He added: “I think for a young and for a not-so-young. We are talking here at the highest level in Europe and to play at that level is extremely difficult.

“You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in such big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it’s extremely difficult.



“That’s the reality. You can shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show consistency.

“Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.”

Nwaneri will be hoping he gets the chance to show both Kovac and Arteta what he is made of when Dortmund take on Arsenal at the Emirates on Tuesday night.

Unlike Premier League rules, Uefa allows loanees to face their parent club in the Champions League.



There is no doubt that Nwaneri will be keen to prove a point to both managers with a cameo in N5, but his lack of minutes of late suggest that will be unlikely from the off.

It is easy to forget that Nwaneri is still just 19 years old, not least because he is so much older than Max Dowman, who is currently occupying his space in the Arsenal squad.

Nwaneri’s contract at Arsenal runs until 2030 so there is still plenty of time for him to reach his potential in red and white.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He has been afforded that time with his loan at Dortmund, after Arsenal chiefs explored the idea of a permanent exit in the summer.



However, if things continue on their current trajectory at both clubs, Nwaneri could have to choose a different path completely if he wants to keep his career on track.

Sports.title: Brentford 4 Everton 0: Oleksandr Usyk watches on as David Moyes hit with sucker punch on record-breaking evening
Sports.content:
Next

DAVID MOYES has been around long enough to know football would deliver him a gut-punch on his big night.

With heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk watching on, Brentford delivered a quick one-two with two goals in as many minutes before the knockout blow of James Tarkowski’s first-half red card.



Moyes entered the Everton history books, this his 593rd game in charge of the club, more than anyone else.

It will be remembered as one of the more infuriating of his 1208 games as a manager, the sort of sweet irony sport is so adept at delivering.



Instead of it being the Scot’s night to celebrate, Keane Lewis-Potter was able to toast a brace and Vitaly Janelt a belter.

Moyes’ side have been riding a wave of late. The Toffees came south chasing a fourth straight win and fifth place in the table. They left bloodied, having barely laid a glove on Brentford, who climbed to sixth.



Moyes has seen almost all there is to see in this game. He knows more than most that you cannot even consider nabbing an away win without matching effort from the off.

And it was the Bees who came out with a point to prove, the hosts the ones playing with the energy and intensity of a side on the up – despite having won just one of their last six.

Jaidon Anthony, given a start with Igor Thiago suspended, was causing trouble down the left, seeing any early effort deflected into the side netting.

Those scares were not enough to shake Everton out of their stupor, and soon they paid for it.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

There was great misfortune about both of Lewis-Potter’s goals, his deflected double, especially if you happen to be Jordan Pickford.

The first came from Brentford’s left, a clipped ball looping off the head of Jake O’Brien and to the feet of Anthony, who squared for Lewis-Potter.

Having charged in unobserved from left-back, he was free to strike first time and watched his effort hit Jarrad Branthwaite and sail over a helpless Pickford.



Two minutes later and Moyes’ evening sunk further, the second coming thanks to an even greater slice of luck.

Lewis-Potter struck towards goal from a half-cleared free-kick but was stopped by the legs of Tarkowski, only for the ball to fall straight back to him and his second attempt cannon in off the midriff of Thierno Barry.

Having gone from bad to worse, Everton’s night was ended thanks to an intervention from VAR – one of the many changes Moyes surely resents since his first as Toffees boss.



Tarkowski took the ball cleanly from the feet of Yehor Yarmoliuk, but went in with such unnecessary force that his studs then found themselves halfway up the Ukrainian’s shin. The easiest of overturns for referee Craig Pawson.

The defender knew it too – running down the tunnel faster than he had moved all evening amid loud taunts from the fans of his former club, jubilant at seeing his first ever Premier League red card on his 351st appearance.

Tarkowski’s only other career red came in Brentford’s red and white, in the Championship more than a decade ago.



His night ruined, and made only longer by 11 minutes added on before the break, Moyes plucked Jack Grealish from the naughty step to give him some time in the legs having been absent from the last four games due to a disciplinary breach.

He could do little on the ball as the visitors sat tight and then fell foul to a stunner, no luck about this.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As Everton sat in, Janelt lapped up the space on the edge of the box and thumped a cracker of a strike into the top corner, nothing Pickford could do about that one either – but for very different reasons.

By the time Fabio Carvalho nodded in as the board went up for added time the away end was deserted, the home support jubilant, watching their side move into the European places Everton had come here hoping to secure.

Sports.title: De Bruyne knows fans will call Man City a ‘DISGRACE’ over cheating – but he’ll still be proud even if stripped of titles
Sports.content:
Next

KEVIN DE BRUYNE knows people might call Manchester City a ‘disgrace’ after the Premier League’s guilty verdict.

But the Etihad legend, 35, says his feelings about “his club” will not change as he returns with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.



KDB enjoyed a trophy-laden decade at the club — winning six Prem titles, seven domestic cups and the Champions League in 2023.

There have been calls for City to be stripped of their titles for breaking financial rules across nearly a decade between 2009 and 2018.



De Bruyne, who played over 400 games in light blue, said: “Everybody has their own opinion, others might be disgraced — but I can’t change it.

“My feelings are no different. The way I feel, the way I’ve been treated, what I’ve done, how we worked together. I don’t think people would change how they view me as a player.

“There has been a lot going on – but I’m proud of what I’ve done as a player and this is my club.”

The period which has been investigated includes the first three years of KDB’s stay.

But nothing will change his own memories as he prepares to face his former club for the second season running.

He said: “My football has not changed. There are rules but everyone plays on the limit.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I played between the white lines and competed with other players.

“That’s what I value most. I gave my all and that’s not going to change.”

De Bruyne has stayed in contact with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak since he departed these shores in the summer of 2025.

He added: “I love the owners. I’ve spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club.



“I’ve nothing but affection for this club and that will never change.

“The people who treated me and my family exceptionally is the most important thing. That’s it.”

De Bruyne’s future with Italian side Napoli is in doubt amid rumours of a breakdown in his relationship with boss Max Allegri.

He has been linked with a switch to PSV Eindhoven in the January transfer window.

Sports.title: No amount of history or trophies will save Man Utd if they carry on like this – they’re sleepwalking towards relegation
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are not too big to go down.

And if they think a new manager alone will save them, they are sleepwalking towards the unthinkable.



No amount of history or trophies in the cabinet will save them if they carry on defending like a pub team.

A January spending spree after nine games of blood, sweat and basic competence is required to avoid the ultimate humiliation.



Red Devils legends Roy Keane and Gary Neville both shrugged off claims that the 20-time English champions could be relegated.

But the Prem table is not laughing.



Boss Mauricio Pochettino, the club’s ninth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired 13 years ago, even admitted a scrap was a “reality” after United’s 4-0 hammering at Anfield.

“Going down, going down, going down,” sang gleeful Liverpool fans on Sunday. “Sacked in the morning,” came a short while later.

United have become everybody’s favourite punchline.

The worrying bit is that now their supporters are numb to it.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Second bottom. Just one point above basement club Crystal Palace.

And worryingly TEN fewer points than Tottenham had at the same stage last season.

Spurs survived by the skin of their teeth on the final day, finishing just two points above the drop after needing THREE managers to drag them over the line.

The fact is 49 of the 89 teams with United’s total of eight points after 11 games have eventually gone down since the Premier League began.

On that basis they’ve got a more than a 50/50 chance of relegation.



United — whose only league win this term came against promoted Ipswich on August 30 — are averaging just 0.78 points-per-game.

That adds to 28 points over the course of a 38-game season and no team has ever survived the drop with fewer than 30.

When United were last relegated from the top-flight, all the way back in 1973-74, the Red Devils also had eight points after 11 games, but it was only two points for a win back then.



Former Spurs and Chelsea chief Poch has 500 Prem games under his belt, but zero experience fighting the pits of relegation.

January 2027 is up there with the most important months in his new club’s 148-year history.

The Red Devils often avoid business in January, but the board and Poch agree the squad must be improved to drag them away from danger.

Despite CEO Omar Berrada’s fanciful comments last week that United’s summer recruitment had “made the squad fundamentally better”, the naked eye tells the opposite tale.

Diogo Dalot? Signed in 2018 by Jose Mourinho. Harry Maguire? Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt? Erik ten Hag. Patrick Dorgu? Ruben Amorim.



The individual mistakes go beyond a relegation-level side as United have shipped 34 goals in all competitions this season — more than any of the other 95 teams across Europe’s top five leagues.

So while finances are tight and debt is high, United still have a £ 160m credit line available.

Berrada had the brass neck to say they did not need defenders in the summer as United have “nine players that can play in the back line”.

But top-flight sides need at least four and signing an established, elite defender with Prem experience costs around £50m to £65m on average.



And it goes without saying they need a striker too.

It’s either that or risk relegation from the Prem and the prospect of losing more than twice that figure by missing out on the fruits of the richest league in world football.

But who can trust United’s owners to identify the right names or cough up funds?

Recruitment has been a disaster for a decade, with the summer window of 2025 the anomaly as Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Senne Lammens all arrived.



Couple that with the fact that no elite player of sound mind would join a sinking ship in the middle of a relegation-infested January window.

United have got to stop giving up early goals.

There were just 105 SECONDS between United kicking off at 1-0 down and going 2-0 behind at Anfield.

Two goals in eight minutes away at Como. Two in five at home against Bournemouth. Two in 14 versus Chelsea. Two in six against Roma. Two in three as they hosted Villa.

Worse still, there are no whipping boys to bail them out this season.



Promoted Leeds, Hull and Coventry have all started strongly.

United are stuck fighting battle-hardened sides such as Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, while also dealing with the physical demands of Champions League football.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There is nowhere to hide. United have enough talent to stay up.

“But talent without fight or leadership is about as useful as a chocolate teapot.

Sports.title: Commanders upset Burrow's Bengals after last-second winner
Sports.content:
Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired as the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.

After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts.

Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight. The Commanders quarterback spiked it with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest.

Daniels finished with 283 yards passing, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and Stevens was five for five on field goals as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants.

Sports.title: Smith: Paths align better for Stevenson unification than Azim fight

Dalton Smith, the WBC super-lightweight champion, thinks he's more likely to fight Shakur Stevenson next than Adam Azim.

Sheffield's Smith has had an outstanding year, knocking out Subriel Matias in New York to win his world championship and defending the belt against Alberto Puello in his Sheffield hometown.

American star Shakur Stevenson secured the WBO's super-lightweight championship when he beat Teofimo Lopez in January.

Both Smith and Stevenson are looking for their next opponents and a unification between the pair would be an appealing match up.

"It's a fight where the paths align a little bit better than me and Adam Azim right now. But like I said we'll see."

His advice to Azim is: "Be in world level fights.

Sports.title: Patten ends Grand Slam-winning doubles pairing to partner fellow Brit Skupski
Sports.content:
Henry Patten has ended his world No 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion in favour of teaming up with British compatriot Neal Skupski for 2027.

Patten and Heliovaara celebrated being crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after they claimed a second Wimbledon success together back in July.

However, in a post on Heliovaara's blog, the Finnish player revealed Patten phoned him on Friday to say their three-time Grand Slam-winning partnership was over - despite a previous agreement they would continue.

Image: Neal Skupski will now team up with his compatriot in 2027

"After the trip to Turin, I didn't even have time to get into the holiday mood when the weekend took a rather unexpected turn," Heliovaara said on his own blog website. "Henry completely unexpectedly announced that he had changed his mind about next year.

"I picked up the kids from daycare on Friday afternoon and we were just opening presents when I got a call from Henry. Without going into too much detail, the message was clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player British doubles star Henry Patten hit out at ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for missing his world No 1 trophy presentation, with Tim Henman backing his criticism

"He didn't want to play together again next year, even though we had agreed to do so during the fall. The announcement came as completely as it could come and I couldn't help but listen with my mouth open in horror and say that I don't agree at all.

"I'm unlikely to ever fully understand what and why this ultimately happened.

"The emotional scale in my head was quite violent at first, a shocking situation in any case.

"The two-and-a-half years with Henry have been by far the best time of my career, for which I am eternally grateful to him, but now the main feeling was heavy disappointment and even anger."

Heliovaara confirmed in his blog that he would team up with another British player Julian Cash, while Patten is set to partner Skupski in 2027.

Sports.title: Lewis-Potter scores twice as Brentford thump four past 10-man Everton
Sports.content:
Keane Lewis-Potter’s first-half double set Brentford on their way to a comprehensive 4-0 Premier League win over 10-man Everton.

For David Moyes it was a record-setting night to forget. His 593rd game in charge of Everton, more than any other Toffees manager, ended in misery, as James Tarkowski's red card at 2-0 down left them with no hope of a comeback at the Gtech Community Stadium on Monday night.

Vitaly Janelt added a third for Brentford, while Fabio Carvalho came off the bench to score a fourth, as they moved up to sixth in the table, a point above Everton who slipped to ninth.

It was a deserved breakthrough for Brentford midway through the first half. A lovely touch from Jaidon Anthony teed up Lewis-Potter, who saw his strike deflect past Jordan Pickford.

Four minutes later it was 2-0. This time it came from a free-kick as the ball fell to Lewis-Potter. His first effort was blocked, but he got a second bite at it, and again a deflection from his strike took the ball away from the Everton goalkeeper.

Image: Keane Lewis-Potter celebrates his first goal against Everton

It got worse for the Toffees before the break, too. Tarkowski was first given a yellow card for his follow-through challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk, before a VAR check saw the referee upgrade it to red.

Moyes introduced Jack Grealish at the start of the second half, his first appearance since being dropped from the squad last month, but it would make minimal difference.

Janelt's rocket on 67 minutes added a Brentford third, as he picked out the top corner from 25 yards, while substitute Carvalho prodded in from a corner in stoppage time to add the icing to the cake.

Sports.title: Penge claims stunning maiden PGA Tour win at RSM Classic
Sports.content:
English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic.

Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.

With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.

Penge's five-under 65 on the Seaside Course included six birdies, including one at the last, and a single bogey, while he birdied 18 again to clinch victory in the playoff after nailing his approach to 10 feet.

Sports.title: Are Man Utd genuinely in a relegation battle?
Sports.content:
What started as a blip has become a problem far more systemic for Man Utd.

"If the name wasn't Man Utd and you're watching their performances, you'd say they are a team in a relegation fight. They're conceding lots of goals, a comedy of errors, red cards - they've won one game all season," said Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher.

Only Ipswich beaten in 11 attempts, the worst defence in Europe - and a 4-0 hammering at Liverpool on Sunday to wipe the gloss off Mauricio Pochettino's arrival within 12 first-half minutes.

Carragher added: "This Manchester United back four can't cope with pace. They're a million miles off it in terms of coming up against what they are in the Premier League."

The unthinkable is beginning to become thinkable. Are United in an actual relegation battle now?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol looks at what it could cost Man Utd if they were to be relegated from the Premier League.

"They're in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table," said Carragher after a fifth defeat of the season left them with their lowest points tally at this stage of a season since 1972. "You can't say anything else when you look at their record this season.

"We don't believe it will happen over a 38-game season, but they haven't had the most difficult of starts. They've played a lot of promoted teams; they haven't played the best team in the league, Arsenal, yet.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch free match highlights of Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of Man Utd, a 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool

"I don't think they'll go down, but this idea that they haven't got a scrap on their hands, they have."

It seems unfathomable. But should it? The numbers don't give Pochettino any grounds for optimism. Only 26 teams - barely one a season - have picked up eight points or fewer from their opening 11 games in the history of the Premier League and only 13 of those, exactly half, avoided the drop.

Of course, most of those were not clubs anywhere near the size and stature of Manchester United. But even the Opta supercomputer, which provides far more contextualised feedback, is losing faith and gives them a 24 per cent chance of going down - though it does still back them to stumble to safety and finish 16th.

"You wonder how low it can get," said Gary Neville after Sunday's defeat. "It's embarrassing. I don't believe they're in a relegation fight, they'll get out of this, but this is the worst Man Utd have been in 53 years. The worst defensive team in Europe, second-bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options aren't great."

That may be putting it lightly. As well as the worst defence in Europe's top-five leagues across all competitions, United also have the third-worst performing attack in the Premier League, falling below their xG tally by 4.2 goals already.

In an immediately infamous tweet in 2014, then-boss David Moyes was quoted as saying United "must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending".

Pochettino is unlikely to admit it publicly, but behind closed doors must have similarly widespread concerns even at this early stage. United have not found themselves in the bottom two after 11 games in 40 years.

Sir Alex Ferguson was brought in as their eventual saviour that winter, but turning the tide on this United side is a significantly bigger ask.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Premier League Show, Adam Binnie breaks down Manchester United's points tally this season compared to Tottenham's in 2025/26 and the big possibility of a potential relegation.

Are there personnel at his disposal who could improve matters? Potentially. Neville did pinpoint a back four of Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Diego Dalot who could at least get United out of their defensive slump.

"It's a poor back four, but it's their best back four. It could compete," he added. "But the one that started today and finished against Villa a few weeks ago, that'll get you relegated."

There is good news and bad news. Neville's quartet are unbeaten in every game they have started together since the start of 2023/24 - and can boast a 70-per-cent win ratio. Unfortunately for Pochettino, that only amounts to 10 games across more than three seasons, owing largely to availability.

But that still does not solve the problem of their limp attack. Of the 22 players to have attempted a shot for the club this season, 19 have under-performed their xG, and the three who have not, Benjamin Sesko, Joshua Zirkzee and Youri Tielemans, have scored only a solitary goal apiece.

There remain huge question marks over the Man Utd dressing room, its commitment and a lack of leadership which permeated into the public sphere in the final weeks of Michael Carrick's reign. Though Pochettino's players have shown they can perform when they want to. Carrick himself knows that better than anyone.
