Sports.title: Herta replaced at Hitech to end F2 season early
Sports.content:
Colton Herta will end his torrid time in Formula 2 early by not returning for the final two rounds of the 2026 season following a “mutual agreement” with Hitech.

The nine-time IndyCar race winner made the transition to European single-seaters this year as part of his bid to gain an FIA Superlicence that is required to compete in Formula 1.

But F2 has not gone as planned for Herta, who is 19th in the standings with only 26 points from 12 rounds, achieving a best result of fifth at Barcelona from third on a reversed grid.

The 26-year-old American is not returning for the final race weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi and will be replaced by Roman Bilinski - who was already set to take Herta’s seat in 2027.

Jan Sumann, Hitech's F2 head of race engineering said: “We're delighted to welcome Roman to Hitech for the final two rounds of the season.

“These two weekends will give us an opportunity to start building important relationships before the winter.

“I would also like to thank Colton for his commitment and determination throughout his time with Hitech, despite a challenging season. We wish him the very best for the future.”

Roman Bilinski, Monza in F3 2025 Photo by: Formula Motorsport Ltd

Herta was not quoted in the team statement and it is not yet known what his plans for next year are because, despite a poor season, he was still in the frame for an F1 promotion.

That was via his role as Cadillac’s reserve driver and thanks to six FP1 appearances in 2026, he has now obtained a superlicence but days after doing so, Valtteri Bottas was confirmed for next year alongside Sergio Perez.

As for his replacement at Hitech, Bilinski also contested his rookie F2 campaign this year but didn’t fare much better, sitting 16th in the standings with 36 points for DAMS.

“I'm really excited to be joining Hitech for the final two rounds of the season. Having the opportunity to work with the team ahead of 2027 is a real bonus,” said the 22-year-old Polish-Briton, who finished 11th in F3 in 2025.

“It means we can start working together straight away, get to know each other and build a strong foundation ahead of next year. Of course, I’ll be hoping for some strong results to close out the current season.”

Sports.title: Why Bearman’s expected 2027 Haas F1 deal remains unsigned
Sports.content:
Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman remains the only driver on the F1 grid without a contract for 2027. It is a situation that would have been hard to imagine just a few weeks ago, given that his retention at Haas had been taken for granted since last summer.

The announcement of Rafael Camara as Bearman's 2027 team-mate, which came ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, was expected to be swiftly followed by that of his British team-mate. Instead, the silence has dragged on to the point of becoming a talking point, even prompting rumours of Bearman driving elsewhere next year. The paradox is that Bearman and Haas have strong reasons to reach an agreement.

Bearman has ruled out racing elsewhere in 2027, while Haas has long been expected to retain him, yet the negotiations have dragged on far longer than initially anticipated.

In recent weeks, there has been speculation about the reasons for the deadlock, some linked to the contractual relationship between Bearman and Ferrari and to the future prospects of the 21-year-old Briton.

According to information obtained by Autosport, however, the issue holding up the signing does not concern the driver’s long-term future, but rather the financial terms of the deal with Haas.

Ferrari has already exercised the option allowing it to retain Bearman within its driver programme. Given that Maranello has invested financial resources in the young Briton ever since he joined the Driver Academy in 2021, allowing Bearman to leave on a free transfer would be a big waste of all those efforts.

Rafael Camara will finish the 2026 season for Haas as he prepares for his full 2027 debut alongside Oliver Bearman. Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Bearman could be in a position to leave Ferrari at the end of 2027 if he has not received a call-up to join the works team, but this scenario does not represent an obstacle to renewing with Haas, and there is no need to finalise his relationship with Ferrari in the short term – especially given that Lewis Hamilton is in the twilight of his career. The Scuderia has not ruled out any of its longer-term options.

The immediate negotiations therefore centre on two parties: Haas and Bearman’s entourage. The sticking point is the salary offered by the American team, a figure that the driver and his staff do not consider commensurate with their expectations.

This has led to a prolonged deadlock, despite both sides being aware of the need to reach an agreement. On the eve of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman made no secret of his disappointment at a situation that has now been dragging on for months. “There’s nothing new to say. To be honest, I’m rather disappointed to find myself here, at the twentieth round of the season, without a signed contract for next year. It’s a strange situation, but we’re getting there.”

The Briton admitted that the uncertainty is becoming difficult to cope with, especially after a season in which he believes he has proved his worth as the team's lead driver.

Bearman categorically ruled out the possibility of moving to another team in 2027, though. When asked if there was even the slightest chance of racing elsewhere, with no more seats up for real discussion, his answer was unequivocal: "No, zero chance."

He added: "My goal for 2027 is very clear. I think we have unfinished business here. Then looking further into the future, it's not really in my hands, let's say it like that."

Bearman has been open about his ambition to make it to Maranello, but he is aware that decisions regarding the Scuderia’s future do not depend solely on his performance.

"Of course I'm under contract with Ferrari. Ferrari have given me this incredible opportunity to step into F1 with them for the first time," he acknowledged. "I'm still a Ferrari junior driver and my ultimate dream is to race for Ferrari. First of all, they're the most iconic team and they're the first team that believed in me as a kid.

Oliver Bearman, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

"It's still my ultimate dream, but there's no doubt that looking into the future, there may be some challenges there. There's no denying that, it's very clear. I don't really have much say in the matter. We just need to see how things develop over time."

The immediate contract situation is more straightforward. Ferrari has already clarified its contractual position and is not the party holding up Bearman’s confirmation. The ongoing negotiations concern only the terms of the agreement between the driver and Haas. Autosport understands the matter is expected to be resolved before the final weekend in Abu Dhabi, in all likelihood through an inevitable compromise on the financial front.

That doesn't make the lack of a deal by the end of November any less frustrating for Bearman. "It's not a good feeling to be sitting here with two races to go without things sorted out," he said. "Even though I know that we're pretty much there, the fact is that we're not. There's no excuse for being here without a contract signed, quite honestly."



Those comments show just how much this whole tug-of-war has weighed on the driver. Barring an unexpected breakdown in negotiations, Bearman is expected to remain with Haas in 2027 as well, forming one of the youngest driver pairings on the grid alongside Camara.

Sports.title: F1 plans two-team engine supply limit under 2030 V8 rules
Sports.content:
Formula 1 is planning a shift to just two power unit supplies per manufacturer in 2030, Autosport has learned, raising questions over the status of Mercedes' three current customers.

Over the Las Vegas weekend the FIA announced there was unanimous support to bring the next generation of power unit regulations forward to 2030. That includes a move to 2.1-litre V8 engines, including a turbocharger, a maximum of 200 kilowatts of electric power and the use of sustainable fuels.

That move satisfies the demand for cheaper and less complex engines, which FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 chief Stefano Domenicali had been pursuing in unison. Meanwhile, adding a turbo was a key requirement for the likes of Audi and also ensures engine noise remains at a suitable level for some of F1's urban venues.

What was also part of a wide-ranging document the FIA produced on the 2030 framework, but wasn't part of the public announcement, is an agreement between the six 2030 power unit manufacturers to supply just two teams each. This also includes their works team, leaving just one single engine supply available for external customer teams.

Autosport understands that one aim of the move is to reduce the political influence of manufacturers supplying a large share of the grid, in this case Mercedes and Ferrari, while the manufacturers in question had also been willing to downsize as supplying F1 engines is a loss-making operation, with supplies capped at just $18m per season.

Ferrari is currently supplying the works team, Haas and Cadillac, but the latter will be moving to in-house engines from 2030, meaning the question of Ferrari's supply is solving itself. Red Bull Powertrains will also be taking care of two teams, Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, while at present Audi, Aston Martin partner Honda and Cadillac's shareholder General Motors will all have their own works teams as their one and only confirmed customer.

Photo by: Manuel Eletto

The Mercedes question

That leaves the question of what will happen to Mercedes and the customers of Mercedes High Performance Powertrains. Alongside the works team in Brackley, the Brixworth operation is currently supplying McLaren, Williams as well as Alpine, whose parent company Renault recently abandoned and sold its in-house engine operation.

Per the 2030 framework, two of those three teams would be looking for a new engine supply if the FIA World Motor Sport Council approves the proposal in Shanghai next month. That seismic shift will set up months of political intrigue in the F1 paddock as teams scramble to secure what has been F1's most reliable and performant power unit supplier ever since F1 moved to hybrid engines in 2014, or conclude deals with currently less desirable options.

Autosport understands that both McLaren and Williams are fancying their chances of remaining with Mercedes. And while McLaren at least explored the idea of becoming its own power unit manufacturer when a move to a cheaper formula would make that more feasible than it is now, CEO Zak Brown indicated that ship has sailed for 2030 as he aims to remain a Mercedes customer.

"It's something we've looked at in the past, but we're very happy with HPP," Brown said in Las Vegas on Thursday. "I think we've proven that we can win championships with them, so we don't have any intention to have anything in the back of our car other than a Mercedes."

Mercedes' intentions about what its ideal customer team would look like are less clear right now. Having been beaten by McLaren in 2024 and 2025, CEO Toto Wolff maintained that a win for a customer is still a feather in the cap for HPP and the Mercedes brand as a whole, while a strong customer team also provides a valuable chassis benchmark for the works operation.

And while Brown hailed HPP as an "awesome partner", it's no secret that the relationship between HPP and McLaren has at least come under some strain at the start of this year amid a knowledge gap between the works team and its customer over how to exploit and deploy the complex new power units.

Photo by: Alex Pantling / Getty Images

Whether Mercedes will continue to lease engines to its most formidable rival or whether a deal with a midfield team is the preferred option will likely become the subject of plenty of intrigue in the coming months.

Why FIA engine is dead

What is certain is that the FIA's proposed third-party engine plan is now dead in the water. With F1 power units becoming less complex and expensive in 2030, FIA president Ben Sulayem had floated the idea of sourcing a supply of off-the-shelf, white-label engines to further alleviate concerns over team independence.

However, that plan never seemed economically viable for any prospective engine builder, and with all six PUMs at the table now unanimously agreeing to 2030's key infrastructure, a cap of two supplies would mean there are at least 12 power unit supplies available for 11 teams.

The FIA did include a safety net in case one of the six manufacturers decides to drop out, adding a clause under which a departing manufacturer’s F1 power unit intellectual property would transfer to the FIA, which could then assign it to a new manufacturer coming in.

As is the case today, there will also be an "obligation to supply", meaning the FIA could force one of the manufacturers to supply an additional, third team with an engine if that outfit can't arrange a deal to find one, which may well end up becoming a key clause.

What has also been agreed is the basis for the power unit cost cap for the 2030-2034 period. The cap will remain at today's figure of $190m for 2030 before falling by $7.5m per year, ending at $160m for the 2034 season.

Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

That sliding scale helps manufacturers with the initial development cost of the new power units. A development freeze of the current engines from 2028, as well as a ban on V8 dyno testing until the summer of that year, is expected to help F1's current manufacturers manage their resources between the two projects. Existing manufacturers will also receive more cost-cap headroom than newcomer General Motors, which can now abandon its V6 plans and just focus on the V8 programme in Charlotte. GM is understood to be signing up to a budget cap of $170m for the first couple of years.

Why early deal is so crucial for F1

There are still several important topics to be fleshed out further by the manufacturers, such as the exact nature of the electric push-to-pass system as it would need to work in conjunction with the chassis design to promote close racing.

But by defining the overarching framework and key engine architecture, which will be rubber-stamped by the FIA World Motor Sport Council, both the manufacturers and the FIA can now get to work on the next rules cycle on a reasonable timeline.

That should help the governing body come up with chassis regulations which are tuned to work well with the new power units and deliver a more pure and exciting set of rules, without facing the prospect of having to adapt to late U-turns by OEMs, which led to 2026's compromised and criticised formula to begin with.

Sports.title: Camara to finish F1 season with Haas, ending F2 title bid
Sports.content:
Haas rookie Rafael Camara will see out the season with Haas in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, effectively ending his F2 championship challenge.

Camara was confirmed in October as a full-time replacement for Esteban Ocon in 2027, and was fast-tracked into the seat after Ocon's relationship with the US-owned team deteriorated.

After test driver Ryo Hirakawa took over Ocon's car midway through the Mexico Grand Prix weekend, Camara made his F1 debut on home soil in Brazil and was also in the VF-26 at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The final two rounds presented a bigger decision to make, though, because the 21-year-old is leading the F2 championship by seven points over Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov. Drivers are unable to take part in both F1 and F2 on the same weekend.

Haas has now decided to keep the Brazilian in the seat to finish the season, rather than bringing back Hirakawa, to give Camara as much experience as possible ahead of his 2027 rookie campaign.

"We’re excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," said Haas F1 Team boss Ayao Komatsu.

"I’m delighted that Rafa’s embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway."

Rafael Camara, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

Camara finished 20th after a difficult maiden race in Interlagos in the wet, and took 16th in Las Vegas.

While Tsolov now just needs seven points to match Camara, Camara’s absence also boosts third-placed Alex Dunne’s title chances, who trails the Brazilian by 18 points.

Sports.title: Andy Hiraoka Is the Right Test for Richardson Hitchins
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he is returning in February, though he still has no opponent. Zuffa Boxing should give him Andy Hiraoka. More than two years will have passed by then since Hitchins edged Liam Paro by split decision for the IBF light welterweight title. Zuffa paid for an unbeaten former champion. It needs to put him in with someone who can actually beat him.

“FEBUARY I’m Back !!!!” Hitchins posted on X without naming an opponent or a city. Dan Rafael reported in October that Zuffa was mapping out early 2027 dates for Hitchins after talks for a Keyshawn Davis bout stalled. Both Hitchins and Hiraoka used to campaign at light welterweight before moving up to 147 pounds. Hitchins already made his welterweight debut on July 26 against Ricardo Salas, while new Zuffa signee Hiraoka will be fighting at 147 for the first time in his promotional debut.

What Hiraoka Brings at 147

Hitchins stopped George Kambosos Jr. in eight rounds at 140 and swept every round on all three scorecards against Salas in New York. Those shutout scores against Salas show how cleanly Hitchins worked from the outside. They also skip over how frequently he clinched once Salas closed the gap. Hitchins grabbed, waited on the referee to break them, and went right back to his jab without taking much back.

Hiraoka (24-1, 19 KOs) makes those clinches harder to pull off. The southpaw works behind a sharp right jab and digs to the body on the way in. If Hiraoka keeps a hand free when Hitchins reaches to tie him up, Hitchins will spend the night resetting his feet instead of dictating the pace. Hiraoka will have to earn his entry, too. He is coming off a decision loss to Gary Antuanne Russell down at light welterweight in February, so a February 2027 date would show whether his power holds up in his welterweight debut.

Zuffa Needs a Real Answer

If Zuffa wants to book fights the way the UFC does, this matchup is sitting right in front of it. It has two welterweights under contract whose styles clash cleanly. Nobody outside the camp knows how much say Hitchins and his manager, Keith Connolly, have over opponents. If Hitchins has approval rights, passing on Hiraoka makes business sense for him. Keyshawn Davis brings a bigger name and a bigger payday for the risk. Hiraoka offers plenty of trouble inside the ropes without bringing half the attention.

Hitchins (21-0, 8 KOs) and the Salas fight already showed what happens when an opponent lets him stand on the outside and jab all night. Hiraoka won’t give him that kind of space. Putting them together in February is the quickest way for Zuffa to learn what happens when Hitchins gets pushed onto his heels for twelve rounds.

If Zuffa wants to know what Hitchins is really worth at 147, matching him against Hiraoka will give them an answer. Better to get that read now than waste another year protecting him.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Waited Ten Years To Share Schizophrenia Diagnosis
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says doctors diagnosed him with schizophrenia after he beat Wladimir Klitschko in November 2015. He waited nearly ten years to mention it, saving the reveal for a Netflix documentary timed to his fight with Anthony Joshua. The film drops November 27, two weeks before Netflix streams Fury vs. Joshua live from Cardiff on December 11.

“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said Fury in excerpts published by BBC Sport. Netflix tied the documentary directly to the Joshua bout in its October 29 announcement, putting the fight right in the headline. You don’t need to guess why the film is dropping now. Fury, 38, hasn’t explained publicly why he waited a full decade until the biggest fight and biggest purse of his career to share a diagnosis he skipped in earlier accounts.

What Fury Said About His 2016 Crisis

Fury was talking publicly about his mental health back in October 2016, less than a year after taking the unified heavyweight titles from Klitschko. He told Rolling Stone he was dealing with depression, drinking heavily and using cocaine. He also said he had been told he had a form of bipolar disorder.

He revisited that breakdown in his book Gloves Off. Fury wrote that doctors told him he had bipolar disorder, paranoia and anxiety. Schizophrenia never appeared in that version. In the Netflix film, Fury says he heard voices threatening him and his family, thought the radio was talking to him, and begged his wife Paris to get him out of a hospital in June 2016 because “the Illuminati” wanted him.

Fury went into that hospital with a suspected heart attack, which doctors diagnosed as an anxiety attack. He says a London psychiatrist later confirmed schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. According to the Los Angeles Times, Paris remembers the psychiatrist telling them Fury was “a mild schizophrenic.”

Fury says a 2017 Halloween night out in a skeleton costume served as his turning point before he returned to the ring and stopped Deontay Wilder in 2020. Everything in these excerpts still comes down to what Fury and his wife say happened, with no word from the doctor who saw him.

Netflix gets a fresh promotional hook heading into a December 11 heavyweight main event it is carrying live. The streamer already owns footage of Fury’s comeback and title runs. He left that diagnosis out of Rolling Stone and his own book for ten years, then brought it out right before the biggest payday of his career. None of that helps him with Joshua’s right hand in Cardiff.

Sports.title: Rayo Calls Shakur Stevenson ‘Not a Real Fighter’
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela had plenty to say about Shakur Stevenson leaving Zuffa Boxing without ever fighting him. In an interview with The Ring, the former 140-pound titleholder accused Stevenson of chasing safer paydays while ignoring a dangerous opponent who had already beaten two of Stevenson’s common reference points.

Stevenson spent his time pushing for a bout with Manny Pacquiao and hoping Lamont Roach would get past William Zepeda so he could fight Roach next, according to Valenzuela. His own name barely came up.

“Honestly, I was kind of pissed,” said Valenzuela to Ring Magazine when asked about Stevenson’s departure. “I was like, ‘What a pussy. You’re not a real fighter.’ He just wants to make money and cash out, big fights.”

What Valenzuela’s Resume Showed

A split decision win over Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz gave Valenzuela the WBA super lightweight title and took out a fighter Stevenson had gone back and forth with on social media. Valenzuela also pointed to his knockout claim over Edwin De Los Santos, a puncher who gave Stevenson twelve difficult rounds in November 2023.

“I beat Pit Bull Cruz. I knocked out Edwin De Los Santos, the guy who gave him his toughest fight. So, why not fight me?” said Valenzuela.

Pacquiao still draws a crowd and a large purse even in his forties, which makes the business appeal obvious. Roach had far less commercial traction, especially after Zepeda dominated him. Watching Stevenson openly root for Roach to win while saying almost nothing about a fight with him left Valenzuela convinced Stevenson was looking for the path of least resistance.

“He just wants to box comfortably. He doesn’t want to feel no pressure,” said Valenzuela. “That’s what I do. I bring the pressure, and I bring stress.”

Negotiating Habits and What Comes Next

Ashton Sylve was another name mentioned for Stevenson. Valenzuela questioned what fighting an unproven prospect would say about Stevenson’s willingness to take real risks. Stevenson’s negotiating habits drew criticism too, from weight terms for Devin Haney to wanting Raymond Muratalla at 135 pounds after Stevenson had already moved up to 140.

“He’s not up for a gamble. You know, you got to bet on yourself in a tough fight,” said Valenzuela.

Attention now turns to Floyd Schofield and a chance to become a two-time world champion. Stevenson walked away from Zuffa without ever finding out how his defense holds up against a taller southpaw willing to press him for twelve rounds.

Sports.title: Aaron McKenna Likely To Drop Belt To Avoid Amari Jones
Sports.content:
Aaron McKenna will likely drop his IBF middleweight title rather than defend it against Amari Jones if the sanctioning body orders the bout, according to Chris Mannix.

Right now, that belt looks like a hot potato McKenna is just keeping warm until his December check clears in Saudi Arabia. I can understand why. A negotiation with former WBO champion Denzel Bentley pays better and gives McKenna a cleaner style, assuming both camps revisit the fight that fell apart in September.

Mannix said on his podcast with Sergio Mora that people close to the situation, including on McKenna’s side, expect the champion to pass on Jones. The IBF is expected to order the mandatory after McKenna’s scheduled December defense in Saudi Arabia. Mora didn’t sugarcoat the matchup. “We’ll get a new champion at 160 if that happens,” said Mora.

The Denzel Bentley Alternative

McKenna and Bentley had already agreed to a unification bout before the WBO ordered Bentley to face Yoenli Hernandez. The WBO stripped Bentley in October when he skipped that obligation. Bentley went through with his London fight against Shane Mosley Jr. this month instead, dropping him in the second round on the way to a unanimous decision. Zuffa Boxing promotes both McKenna and Bentley, giving them a fight they already know how to make.

Bentley still poses real danger. He carries enough power to make McKenna think twice before trading, and the Mosley win proved he can bank rounds after an early knockdown without chasing a stoppage. McKenna still gets his own shots off much easier against Bentley than against Jones. Both men also have a real following in Britain and Ireland, which makes the gate work.

What Jones Brings To The Ring

Jones creates a completely different set of problems. He works behind a long jab from both stances. When DeAndre Pettis shelled up upstairs, Jones went to the body until the openings appeared. Mannix noted that Jones told him a cut on the bridge of his nose cost him his final few weeks of sparring before that bout. He still became the first fighter to stop Pettis. McKenna wants to trade in the pocket. Jones has the reach and power to punish him on the way in and keep hitting him once he gets there.

Mannix expects McKenna to move up in weight if he vacates. That leaves Jones fighting for the vacant belt. Jahi Tucker sits next in the rankings, though Mannix heard George Liddard could jump to the No. 2 spot with a win in December. Mannix called Jones against Liddard in early 2027 his “educated guess.”

Bentley already proved he will take a fight without a title on the line. Once the Riyadh purse clears, McKenna can drop the strap and cash in against Bentley rather than walk into Jones’s jab.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Warns Liam Paro Over VADA Testing Dispute
Sports.content:
Bill Haney brought up the possibility of a contract breach on Monday if Liam Paro walks away from his December 19 welterweight unification fight with Devin Haney over VADA testing. Speaking on Instagram Live, Bill mentioned lawyers and asked whether Paro’s side is looking for an exit from the Chase Center main event in San Francisco.

“I think it looks like you might be finding reasons to breach outside of the agreement,” said Bill Haney. He said lawyers handle those disputes and noted that the Haneys would face consequences too if they failed to meet what they signed up for. Bill stopped short of threatening a lawsuit, adding that Devin is already in camp and preparing to fight.

What Bill Says Happened In Negotiations

Bill claims Paro’s team never raised VADA testing during negotiations and only brought it up publicly after the contract was signed. Paro and his promoter, Matt Rose of No Limit Boxing, say VADA was agreed to during talks. Paro has publicly pressed Devin to enroll, though whether Paro himself has entered the pool remains unconfirmed.

Bill pointed to Devin’s bout against Brian Norman Jr. to show how he handles testing when it is part of a deal. VADA was written into that contract before Norman signed, and the disagreement then was over when Norman would enroll. With Paro, Bill said the bout came together on roughly four or five weeks’ notice, and he considers 12 weeks the minimum for VADA.

“Had it been a longer time where we would have had to negotiate, then I would have put it in the agreement,” said Bill.

The contract may say one thing. Devin still has nearly four weeks to volunteer for the program he spent years promoting. Bill said he stopped pushing Devin to enroll after leaving year-round testing because they took ridicule while few other fighters joined. That is a tough sell when the opponent is asking for the exact testing the Haneys used to champion.

What Paro Faces If He Walks

Paro is unlikely to pull out. A welterweight unification and the purse that comes with it would be difficult for him and No Limit Boxing to replace. If he stays in the fight, the Norman bout shows what he has to solve. Haney builds rounds behind his jab and quick combinations, then backs out behind an extended lead hand or ties up his opponent the moment the distance closes. He held Norman repeatedly. Paro has to punch as Haney reaches to clinch, before the referee breaks them and resets Paro at the end of the jab.

Bill says the testing already in place is enough for him. That gets harder to defend if Paro pulls the upset on December 19. You cannot turn down VADA when your opponent asks for it in November and then complain about the rules in January.

Sports.title: Devin Haney’s VADA Dispute Puts Liam Paro Fight at Risk
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s December 19 welterweight unification against Liam Paro in San Francisco is running into conflicting reports over whether Haney has enrolled in Voluntary Anti-Doping Association testing. Chris Mannix reported Haney had not signed up, and Paro’s side was ready to walk.

“The Devin Haney-Liam Paro fight is in real jeopardy, sources say,” Mannix wrote on X. He said Paro wanted full VADA testing and summed up the camp’s position in four words. “No testing, no fight.”

The VADA Enrollment Deadline

Paro’s promoter, No Limit Boxing, told Nine it gave Haney’s team 24 hours to enroll. According to the promoter, VADA testing was agreed upon during the original talks. Paro later said he was told the Haneys wanted to rely on athletic commission testing alone.

Paro’s camp can take the IBF belt out of the December 19 main event by pulling him from the fight. Haney could still defend his WBO title against a replacement if the promoters found one, but that would cost him the chance to leave San Francisco with two belts.

The Missing VADA Start Date

VADA has yet to publicly confirm Haney’s enrollment or say when random testing will begin. Even if Haney has signed the paperwork, Paro’s camp still has to decide whether the testing arrangements are enough for him to fight on December 19.

We all heard Bill’s ridiculous excuse. What a farce.

The Haney’s, while Conte was around, argued that everyone should do VADA. Obviously as everyone knows, VADA’s testing substance panel is much more extensive than any commission. (We Verified this fact with VADA) VADA checks for blood doping, hGH, peptides and synthetic testosterone, and more. Even after everything that I went through, I have been willing to test for all that and more to prove i am clean . In fact, we hired the State of California Commission to do simultaneous testing in addition to VADA. — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) November 23, 2026

A late start date shrinks how much of the final camp gets covered before both men step on the scale in San Francisco. Haney, 33-0 (15 KOs), is bringing his WBO welterweight belt into the bout against Paro, 27-1 (16 KOs), who holds the IBF title. Neither side has pulled out, though Paro’s team has made clear it will not box under commission testing alone. Until VADA puts Haney’s name on an official enrollment list, Paro’s side has no reason to back off its threat.

Paro’s camp might be doing Haney a favor if it walks away over VADA. Haney is also a promoter, and the Paro fight hasn’t generated much buzz for a pay-per-view main event. If he already has an opponent in mind who could sell more buys, Paro’s withdrawal would give him an opening to make that fight and keep December 19.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Gets Martin Bakole in Cardiff
Sports.content:
Martin Bakole has less than three weeks to prove he actually trained for his original December 11 bout before stepping in against Deontay Wilder. Turki Alalshikh named Bakole to replace injured cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia in the co-main event of Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

On paper, Bakole is not getting dragged off the couch this time. He was already scheduled to fight Solomon Adebayo on the same Netflix card. That sounds fine until you look at what Bakole weighed the last two times he stepped into the ring.

Bakole’s Weight Was Already Slipping

Bakole weighed 284 pounds when he walked down Jared Anderson in August 2024. He dropped the unbeaten American three times, doing much of his damage with uppercuts, and stopped him in the fifth. Six months later, Bakole took the Joseph Parker fight on 48 hours’ notice, weighed 310 pounds, and was stopped in the second round.

The late call helped explain the 310 pounds against Parker. Bakole had a full camp for Efe Ajagba in May 2025 and still came in at 299. He looked sluggish over 10 rounds and came away with a majority draw. Trainer Billy Nelson said the weigh-in caught him by surprise and brought in a nutritionist after the fight.

Bakole has not fought in the 19 months since that night against Ajagba. Coming into a routine undercard bout against Adebayo, nobody knows if he took the scale seriously or showed up around 305 pounds expecting an easy night. If his legs are heavy in Cardiff, Wilder will have all the space he needs to set his feet and fire the right hand.

Bakole Still Threatens Wilder’s Chin

Wilder, 41, holds a 45-4-1 record with 43 knockouts, though he had to grind through twelve rough rounds to edge Derek Chisora by split decision in April. His punch resistance is no longer what it was during his title reign.

Even at 300 pounds, Bakole has a heavy jab and can hurt Wilder with short uppercuts if he backs him to the ropes. If Bakole gets through the first three rounds and starts making Wilder fight with his back to the ropes, the extra weight may be less of a concern. The danger is getting there. If Bakole plods straight in, Wilder can drop him with a right hand before Bakole gets close enough to throw those uppercuts.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Calls Haney’s VADA Delay “Shady”
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia called Devin Haney’s VADA testing delay “shady” on Monday, questioning why one of boxing’s loudest advocates for the program still has no publicly confirmed enrollment for his December 19 welterweight unification fight against Liam Paro.

Garcia pointed to Haney’s history with the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association and urged boxing reporters to cover the holdup. He was responding to a post from Paro, who claimed Haney’s camp wanted to rely solely on athletic commission drug testing. Paro’s claim about commission-only testing has yet to be independently confirmed.

It’s quite obvious Devin Haney is hiding he has advocating for Vada testing for years now. This hold up is shady and I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again you can’t trust the haneys The little brother knowing things before anyone knows And now this Where is all the boxing reporters BIASED Report on this. He has a long track record of using Vada. Fights 5 weeks away — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) November 23, 2026

Haney said Friday that the Paro bout would be his 14th straight fight using VADA and that he had returned more than 65 clean tests. That statement came before Paro’s claim that Haney’s camp wanted commission testing alone.

Garcia has firsthand experience with the program he is now urging Haney to enter. VADA collected the samples in which Garcia tested positive for ostarine around their April 2024 fight. The New York State Athletic Commission changed Garcia’s decision win to a no contest and suspended him for a year. Haney spent two years preaching clean boxing after that night. Seeing his own enrollment missing inside four weeks of fight night gives Garcia an easy target.

Paro’s promoter, Matt Rose, told Fox Sports Australia that VADA testing was one of the first terms agreed during negotiations. Rose said his team gave Haney’s side 24 hours to enroll and that Paro was prepared to walk away. Standard commission testing on fight week does not match random out-of-competition blood and urine collection. Their WBO and IBF title fight is scheduled to headline a DAZN pay-per-view at Chase Center in San Francisco.

The Irony could not be more shocking. So Bill and Devin claim to be “clean” from PED’s, yet they are very knowledgeable about “cycling” etc. Very versed in this area. I didn’t even know what that ment. Now we learn that they “clean guys” are refusing to enroll in VADA testing. Suddenly, they have some issues with VADA, it turns out. Only change lately is that Victor Conte is not here. Can’t make this up. — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) November 23, 2026

Haney says he intends to enroll with VADA for a 14th straight bout. Nothing has been filed yet. With December 19 less than four weeks off, every wasted day shrinks the window for out-of-competition testing in San Francisco.

Ghana News.title: Black Challenge to arrive in Ghana on Thursday with historic World Cup trophy
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s Black Challenge are expected to arrive in Accra on Thursday, November 26, with the country’s first Amputee Football World Cup trophy.

The National Paralympic Committee of Ghana (NPC Ghana) confirmed the team’s return following their historic triumph in Mexico, where they defeated Morocco 1-0 in Sunday’s final in San Juan de los Lagos.

Captain Richard Arthur Opentil scored the decisive goal to hand Ghana the title and complete a remarkable campaign.

NPC Ghana also confirmed that Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams held a virtual meeting with the players and technical team on Monday evening to congratulate them on their achievement.

During the interaction, the minister announced a US$10,000 bonus for each player, in addition to their agreed allowances.

He further disclosed that the Ministry of Sports and Recreation was working with its partners to organise a national heroes’ welcome for the returning champions.

The committee also expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama for his support, recalling that he presented the team with US$10,000 when they handed him their African title in 2024.

Ghana arrived in Mexico as two-time African champions, having won the continental title in 2021 and 2024, as well as gold at the 2023 African Para Games in Accra.

Their World Cup campaign began with a 2-0 defeat to Angola and a 1-1 draw against Colombia before they bounced back with a commanding 6-0 victory over Iraq to finish second in Group D.

The Black Challenge subsequently defeated the United States 3-1 in the round of 16 before overcoming Egypt 2-0 in the quarter-finals.

They secured their place in the final after edging defending champions Türkiye 4-3 on penalties in the semi-finals, following a 1-1 draw after extra time.

Forward Mubarik Mohammed was one of Ghana’s standout performers, finishing the tournament as the Golden Boot winner with seven goals.

The victory marks a historic milestone for Ghanaian para sports, with the Black Challenge adding the world title to their impressive collection of continental honours.

NPC Ghana has paid tribute to the players, head coach Stephen Richard Obeng, the technical and medical teams, its staff and the media for their contributions to the team's successful campaign.

Ghana News.title: Kofi Adams pledges $10,000 bonus for each Black Challenge player after Amputee World Cup triumph
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams has pledged an additional US$10,000 bonus for each player of Ghana’s Black Challenge following their triumph at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup.

Ghana defeated Morocco 1-0 in Sunday’s final to lift the trophy and become world champions, with an own goal in the second half proving decisive.

As part of efforts to celebrate the team’s achievement, the Sports Minister sent a delegation to the team’s hotel in Mexico, comprising the Ministry’s Sports Protocol Officer, Dinah Boateng, and Chief Director, Fati Lily Soale, to engage with the players.

Adams joined the meeting virtually via Zoom to congratulate the team on their historic achievement before announcing the additional financial package.

“Aside from all the bonuses and other monies that have been paid to the team, we as a ministry are also adding an extra US$10,000 for each player of the team,” he said.

The Black Challenge are expected to arrive in Ghana on Thursday at 1:00pm, with their return scheduled at the Kotoka International Airport following their historic World Cup success in Mexico.

Ghana News.title: Banks poised to drive New Economy, says ADB MD
Ghana News.content:
The Managing Director of Agricultural Development Bank PLC (ADB), Edward Ato Sarpong, has highlighted the critical role of Ghana’s banking sector in driving the country’s new economy.

He described banks as strategic partners poised to mobilise capital, finance productive sectors, support enterprise development, and accelerate sustainable economic growth.

The new economic transformation agenda, recently outlined by the Ministry of Finance, seeks to transform Ghana’s economic landscape through targeted investments in eight strategic pillars, with approximately US$10 billion earmarked for priority sectors to stimulate industrialisation, expand employment opportunities, and strengthen the country's productive capacity.

According to the ADB MD, strong collaboration among government, financial institutions, investors, businesses, and development partners will facilitate the successful implementation of the new economic transformation agenda.

He emphasised the importance of positioning the banking industry as a catalyst for productive investment, particularly in sectors that can create sustainable jobs, expand exports, promote local value addition, and strengthen Ghana's economic resilience.

Banking Sector as a Catalyst for Economic Transformation

The Finance Minister’s proposed New Economy agenda identifies eight strategic pillars comprising economic stability, agriculture, energy, minerals, tourism, textiles, medicines, and technology.

Under the proposed investment framework, agriculture receives US$3 billion, followed by energy at US$2.2 billion and minerals at US$1.5 billion.

Tourism, textiles, and medicines each receive US$1 billion, while technology receives US$300 million.

The sectoral allocations underscore the scale of financing required to translate the new economic programme into tangible investments, productive enterprises, and sustainable employment opportunities.

Mr Ato Sarpong highlighted that the programme presents great opportunities to deepen financial intermediation, mobilise domestic savings, facilitate investment flows, and develop innovative financing solutions tailored to the needs of businesses operating across the priority sectors.

“Banks will be essential in supporting trade finance, working capital, infrastructure-related investments, payment systems, and financial advisory services required to strengthen the competitiveness of businesses,” the ADB MD said.

Agriculture and Agribusiness at the Heart of the New Economy

With agriculture receiving the largest proposed sectoral allocation of US$3 billion, Mr Ato Sarpong noted that the New Economy agenda presents a significant opportunity to accelerate agricultural modernisation, improve productivity, and strengthen value chains.

“As a Bank with a longstanding record of supporting agriculture and agribusiness, ADB is strategically positioned to contribute to the sector’s transformation through expert financing solutions,” he stated.

According to Mr Ato Sarpong, the emphasis on agriculture aligns with ADB’s broader ambition to support businesses, empower communities, and contribute to economic development.

“As a universal Bank, our role in the emerging economic framework is to deepen lending, facilitate strategic partnerships, strengthen financial inclusion, support industrialisation, and connect production to processing, distribution, and export markets,” he added.

Mobilising Capital Through Strategic Partnerships

Delivering the New Economy agenda will require the ability to mobilise sustainable financing from domestic and international sources.

Given the scale of the proposed investments, commercial banks alone cannot finance the entire transformation programme.

ADB's Strategic Position in Ghana's Economic Transformation

ADB’s potential contribution to the New Economy agenda is supported by its strong turnaround from 2025.

According to the Bank’s unaudited financial statements, ADB recorded profits before tax of GH¢478.5 million and GH¢447.5 million in September 2026 and September 2025, respectively.

In September 2026, ADB’s total assets increased to GH¢20.28 billion from GH¢16.22 billion, while customer deposits grew to GH¢15.36 billion from GH¢12.85 billion.

The Bank also strengthened its capital position, with its Capital Adequacy Ratio rising to 27.41 per cent, compared with 0.49 per cent in September 2025.

This turnaround gives the Bank a stronger financial foundation to pursue its strategic objectives without compromising prudent lending, effective risk management, and continued improvements in asset quality.

And undoubtedly, the emerging economic agenda reinforces the unique relevance of ADB’s development-oriented mandate and its brand promise of going Beyond Banking to empower businesses, build futures, nurture communities, and drive prosperity.

Ghana News.title: GREDA boss explains why private hostels cost more than traditional halls
Ghana News.content:
The cost of operating privately financed student hostels cannot be fairly compared with charges at traditional university halls, which were mostly built decades ago and no longer carry the original construction costs, the Executive Director of the Ghana Real Estate Developers Association (GREDA), Samuel Amegayibor, has said.

He said private developers had to factor in the cost of their initial investments, loan repayments, maintenance, utilities and other operational expenses when setting accommodation charges, while older university halls were largely concerned with the cost of running and maintaining existing facilities.

Mr Amegayibor said the different financial circumstances made direct comparisons between the two categories of accommodation misleading, particularly as students continued to raise concerns about hostel fee increases at the University of Ghana (UG).

“Now, some people will want to compare traditional hall facility fees, for example, to a private person's fee. The traditional halls - most of them were built long ago. So they don't have any of those costs at their table. They only [deal] with maybe current management and then running the facility to make it habitable for continuous students,” he said.

He was speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, November 23, 2026, amid public debate over the cost of student accommodation at tertiary institutions.

According to him, private developers had to recover the capital invested in constructing hostels, repay loans and meet recurrent expenses before making any returns on their investments.

He said the situation was even more complex, where accommodation facilities were developed in partnership with universities, since the institutions could also expect to earn revenue from the arrangement.

“The private developer has to satisfy his investment, look at the period and pay back and then make some profits also, running cost and all that. And then now, if that facility was built in partnership with the universities, you see where the universities also have some ‘nokofio’ that they are also looking up to make from this small investment. So it's a long-term thing,” he said.

Mr Amegayibor's comments add another dimension to the controversy over accommodation charges at the University of Ghana, where students have questioned the affordability of residential facilities managed by the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL).

The university recently reduced a proposed 26 per cent increase in accommodation fees for standard four-bed rooms in its four Diaspora halls to 15 per cent following consultations with student leaders. The revised annual charge for the 2026/2027 academic year is GH¢8,050, up from GH¢7,000.

Management has explained that several of the UGEL-managed facilities were built with commercial loans secured to expand accommodation at a time when public funding was inadequate. It said the fees were intended to cover debt repayments, utilities, maintenance and other operating costs.

Mr Amegayibor has previously identified access to finance as the biggest obstacle to private investment in student accommodation, alongside difficulties in securing land and the terms of some university partnerships.

He said some developers had been offered build-operate-transfer arrangements of only 25 years by private universities, a period he considered unattractive given the substantial capital involved and the time required to recover the investment.

He also disclosed that loans contracted to develop some hostels could take as long as 30 years to repay, meaning owners might still be servicing their debts long after the students who first occupied the facilities had graduated.

Mr Amegayibor believes the private sector can play a significant role in addressing accommodation shortages at tertiary institutions but says investors need access to long-term financing and a predictable regulatory environment.

He has called for a system that provides certainty for developers and a clear mechanism for resolving disputes, stressing that regulation should not be confused with government-imposed price controls.

The debate over hostel charges has prompted calls for greater scrutiny of accommodation costs and conditions, with the Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, directing the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to engage the Rent Control Department on the regulation of fees in tertiary institutions.

The University of Ghana has welcomed the proposed engagement and indicated its readiness to provide financial and operational information to help determine fair and sustainable accommodation charges.

Ghana News.title: Gold Fields defends Ghana operations, says 74% of every dollar generated stays in country
Ghana News.content:
The Senior Vice President and Managing Director of Gold Fields Ghana Limited, Elliot Twum, defended the company’s contribution to Ghana’s economy, saying 74 per cent of every dollar generated from its operations stays in the country.

His remarks come amid mounting pressure from traditional authorities to keep the company’s Tarkwa Mine leases from being renewed when they expire in April 2027.

The Wassa Fiase Traditional Council and the Apinto Divisional Council have accused the mining company of failing to deliver development benefits commensurate with the scale of its operations.

They are demanding that Ghana hand the mine over to an investor.

However, speaking on Channel One TV on Monday, November 23, Mr Twum stressed that the company’s economic contribution extended beyond mining revenues.

“As I speak to you now, Bernard, every dollar that is generated out of our operation returns $0.74 into the local Ghanaian economy. $0.74 retained in-country for every dollar that we generate,” he said.

Mr Twum further disclosed that Gold Fields had spent $4.6 billion on procurement from local businesses and host communities over the past five years.

He maintained that supporting local businesses, creating employment and retaining wealth within the country were integral to the company’s operations.

“What’s most important is how we share value, but most importantly, what we turn back into the local economy and how to drive the fundamentals of our economy,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Gold Fields eyes $7.5bn investment in Tarkwa Mine as lease expiry looms
Ghana News.content:
Gold Fields Ghana Limited is planning a $7.5 billion investment in its Tarkwa Mine over the next two decades as it seeks to renew its mining leases, which expire in April 2027.

The proposed investment follows more than $5 billion injected into the mine over the past 30 years.

The company’s Senior Vice President and Managing Director, Elliot Twum, disclosed this on Channel One TV on Monday, November 23, highlighting the need for sustained investment and technological improvements to keep the mine operational and efficient.

“Mining is capital intensive. And so over time, what we’ve tried to do is to employ technology to make it more effective and to make it more efficient.

“And to put things in perspective, in the last 30 years, Gold Fields has injected more than $5 billion into Tarkwa Mine,” he said.

Mr Twum said the company estimates it would need a further $7.5 billion for the next phase of the mine’s operations, spanning 20 to 21 years.

He also highlighted the company’s contribution to the Ghanaian economy, noting that Gold Fields spent $4.6 billion on local and host-community procurement in the last five years alone.

“What’s most important, and I need to also call out, is that in the last five years, we have spent $4.6 billion through local procurement and host community procurement,” he said.

According to Mr Twum, the company retains 74 per cent of every dollar generated from its operations in the Ghanaian economy.

“As I speak to you now, Bernard, every dollar that is generated out of our operation returns $0.74 into the local Ghanaian economy. $0.74 retained in-country for every dollar that we generate,” he said.

The investment projections come at a critical time for Gold Fields as it seeks to secure the future of its Tarkwa Mine beyond April 2027.

The mine currently produces an average of 500,000 ounces of gold annually.

Ghana News.title: Rent Commissioner recounts resistance during UG hostel inspection
Ghana News.content:
Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku

The Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, has accused private hostel operators on the University of Ghana (UG) campus of exercising excessive control over accommodation facilities built on public university land, warning that the situation raises serious questions about accountability and the institution’s oversight responsibilities.

He said some private developers had secured arrangements to operate hostel facilities on university land but appeared to have acquired considerable control over the properties, leaving the university with limited influence over their management and charges.

Mr Opoku argued that the university’s role as a custodian of public land should not be reduced to that of a bystander while private operators determine how the facilities are run.

“ We all have a stake in the land, but they (UG) are there to supervise and watch things for us. The fact that you are a board and you are legal does not mean you own that land,” he said.

He was speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, November 23, amid the dispute between the Rent Control Department and the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL) over hostel fees and the regulation of student accommodation.

Mr Opoku said the department’s attempt to inspect some hostel facilities on the campus had been met with resistance, despite prior correspondence notifying the relevant authorities of the intended visit.

He said he had written to the university and UGEL, indicating his intention to inspect the facilities and requesting that the company’s management join the exercise.

However, he said the response he received was that UGEL did not consider itself subject to the department’s authority and would not participate in the inspection.

According to him, he subsequently visited the university and sought to engage the Dean of Students, who was unavailable at the time, before proceeding to meet the chief executive of UGEL.

He alleged that the encounter with the chief executive was unfriendly and that he was subsequently instructed not to proceed with the inspection.

Mr Opoku said some university officials and hostel managers were also reluctant to allow him and his team access to the facilities.

He credited some students, who he said used their access cards and vehicles to facilitate the team’s entry, for enabling the inspection to go ahead.

The Commissioner said the resistance reinforced his determination to establish the conditions under which students were being accommodated and whether the operators were complying with the country’s rent laws.

He expressed concern that the controversy was damaging the university’s reputation, arguing that the institution should not suffer reputational harm because of the actions of a few individuals managing accommodation facilities.

Mr Opoku further alleged that the university had limited control over some private operators because of contractual arrangements entered into by previous authorities.

He questioned the rationale behind granting private entities access to public university land without ensuring that the institution retained adequate supervisory control over the facilities.

The dispute, he said, should prompt a broader examination of how such arrangements were negotiated and the extent to which the interests of students and the university were protected.

Legal dispute

The comments come against the background of mounting complaints by University of Ghana students about accommodation charges and conditions in some hostel facilities managed by UGEL.

The Rent Control Department has maintained that the Rent Act, 1963 (Act 220), applies to accommodation providers who charge people for housing, including operators of student hostels.

The university, however, has called for legal clarification on whether the Act and the Rent Control Law, 1986 (PNDCL 138), apply to the arrangements between UGEL and students, arguing that the nature of those agreements raises questions about the department’s jurisdiction.

In a statement issued on November 19, the university said it respected the statutory responsibilities of public institutions but believed the legal position on student accommodation should be established through the appropriate processes.

It also said it was prepared to provide relevant financial and operational information to support discussions on a fair and sustainable accommodation fee structure.

The university disclosed that it had reduced a proposed 26 per cent increase in the fees for standard four-bed rooms for the 2026/2027 academic year to 15 per cent following consultations with student leaders. The adjustment raised the annual charge in the four Diaspora halls from GH¢7,000 to GH¢8,050 per student.

The Rent Control Department, meanwhile, on November 2 directed UGEL and private hostel operators nationwide to suspend rent increases that had not undergone the required assessment and refund excess payments by November 17.

It subsequently petitioned the Attorney-General on November 10 to investigate complaints concerning hostel charges and room conditions at UGEL facilities, and prosecute any persons or institutions found to have breached the law.

Mr Opoku has explained that the department does not have prosecutorial powers and therefore requires the Attorney-General’s intervention to pursue criminal proceedings where necessary.

The Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, has also directed the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to engage the Rent Control Department on the regulation of accommodation charges in tertiary institutions.

Ghana News.title: Past Ghana’s Most Beautiful contestant Ohemaa Sappama found dead
Ghana News.content:
A former contestant of TV3’s Ghana’s Most Beautiful (GMB) pageant, Ohemaa Sappama Angela, popularly known as Ohemaa GMB, has reportedly been found dead in her room.

Angela, who represented the Bono East Region in the 2023 edition of the pageant, was reportedly discovered dead at her residence, with police officers said to have visited the premises to retrieve her body.

Information attributed to her landlord indicates that the police were involved in the retrieval of the body. However, the circumstances surrounding her death remain unclear.

Neither the police nor her family has officially announced the cause of death.

Her reported death comes months after she was caught up in a controversy involving a viral video that allegedly linked her to a theft incident in Kumasi.

Ohemaa rose to public attention by participating in the 2023 edition of GMB. This cultural reality show celebrates Ghana’s diverse traditions, heritage, and tourism while giving contestants a platform to champion social causes.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
