World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.content:
Who: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund

What: UEFA Champions League

Where: Emirates Stadium, London, United Kingdom

When: Tuesday, November 24 at 8pm (20:00 GMT).

Premier League holders Arsenal face German giants Borussia Dortmund for the first time in more than a decade, as the Champions League returns for matchday five action.

Arsenal and their fans were left frustrated at the weekend despite opening up a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United.

But a firm grip on their English top-flight title defence and a 10-game unbeaten streak across all competitions give Mikel Arteta’s side plenty of reasons to be optimistic for Tuesday’s UCL fixture in north London.

Dortmund, too, have been impressive in their own ways. Unbeaten in Germany this season, they sit two points clear of defending champions Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga table. Niko Kovac’s team are also on an eight-match unbeaten run.

Eberechi Eze, who also scored in the last game, has been Arsenal’s leading scorer in this year’s Champions League with two goals so far, while fellow stars Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard have also bagged a goal each.

In the Dortmund camp, veteran striker Serhou Guirassy is the outright leader with four goals – figures that also make him the joint fourth-highest in the competition.

How have Arsenal played in the Champions League?

Arsenal are third in the league phase standings, with 10 points from four games. The Gunners have won three games – against Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague – and drawn once, with Bayern.



Only Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid have performed better than Arsenal, with 100 percent records.

How have Dortmund played in the Champions League?

Dortmund are 12th in the standings with nine points. They have won three games – against Villarreal, Sabah and Real Betis – and lost once, to Bodo/Glimt.

What happened the last time Arsenal and Dortmund met?

The last time the two teams met in a competitive match was in the 2014-15 season.

Dortmund won 2-0 in Germany in their first encounter and Arsenal beat them by the same scoreline in England in the reverse leg.

Opta’s supercomputer has picked Arsenal as favourites.

World.title: Pennsylvania reports ninth measles death in ongoing state outbreak
World.content:
CDC and state figures on measles deaths differ as Pennsylvania faces escalating health crisis in 46 counties.

Pennsylvania health officials have reported another death linked to the ongoing measles outbreak, bringing the state’s death toll associated with the highly contagious viral disease to nine.

The state Department of Health confirmed on Monday the death of an unvaccinated resident of Centre County in central ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Pennsylvania who tested positive for measles.

Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, has recorded 1,638 confirmed measles cases across 46 counties so far in 2026, including 330 hospitalisations.

The nine deaths were recorded across five counties, as Lancaster County accounted ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌for three deaths, while Jefferson County reported two.

Virginia recorded its first measles-related death in more than three decades on Friday, just days after the United States lost its hard-fought designation as having eliminated the highly contagious virus.

Meanwhile, Wisconsin has reported two deaths, and New York state has recorded one child death linked to the disease.

However, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported only six measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, without specifying the ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠states where the deaths were recorded.

The discrepancy between state and federal tolls emerged earlier this year after the health agency, under US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.

The US Department of Health and Human Services said it ⁠⁠⁠⁠was “saddened to hear of another death in Pennsylvania”, adding that the CDC has provided the state with nearly $4m in one-time emergency funding for ⁠⁠⁠⁠response efforts in 2027.



A total of 5,838 measles cases were confirmed across the country this year as of November 19, according to CDC data. The figure is the highest number reported by the CDC since 1991.

Children below the age of five account for 18 percent of cases, while children between the ages of five and 19 make up 41 percent of cases.

The number of confirmed cases in November 2026 is more than double the 2,289 confirmed measles cases reported for the full year of 2025.

World.title: WHO chief visits Cuba as healthcare system deteriorates
World.content:
Analysts say fuel shortages blamed on US sanctions are worsening the crisis.

Share WHO chief visits Cuba as healthcare system deteriorates on social media

The World Health Organization’s top official is in Cuba, as the island continues to suffer under an ailing healthcare system amid an economic crisis deepened by United States sanctions.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited a paediatric cardiology centre in Havana on Monday alongside the country’s Public Health Minister Dr Jose Angel Portal Miranda.

“Hola, Havana!” Tedros wrote in a post on X during his tour. “Here for a visit to discuss Cuba’s health situation, challenged by sanctions, fuel and electricity shortages.”

The WHO leader arrived Sunday at the invitation of health authorities in the Caribbean nation for a three-day visit, the second time he has visited Cuba as WHO director-general.

Portal Miranda welcomed Tedros, saying it was an opportunity for him to see firsthand the reality of the Cuban healthcare system and the challenges that it faces.

Sharp decline

Cuba’s once-vaunted system of free universal healthcare has deteriorated sharply.

Analysts say the crisis has been compounded by fuel shortages that they blame on stricter US sanctions on the island’s energy sector, worsening an economy that already had been limping for years.

A government report released in June said that the survival rate for children with cancer had fallen to 65 percent from 85 percent, before the energy blockade began in January.

Hospitals across Cuba face shortages of supplies including syringes, gauze, vaccines and anaesthetics. They also lack spare parts to repair equipment such as haemodialysis and CT scan machines.

“The situation is shocking,” said Mario Cruz Penate, the Pan American Health Organization and WHO representative on the island.



He noted that Cuba has long enjoyed health indicators comparable to those of developed nations, including low mortality, high life expectancy, broad vaccination coverage and widespread prenatal care.

World.title: Mexico to try ‘El Chapo Isidro’ despite US extradition request
World.content:
Fausto Meza Flores faces drug trafficking and weapons charges after his capture in a violent Sinaloa operation.

Share Mexico to try ‘El Chapo Isidro’ despite US extradition request on social media

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, an alleged cartel leader known as “El Chapo Isidro”, will be tried in Mexico despite an extradition request by the US, in a move that could worsen already-strained relations between the two countries.

Attorney General Ernestina Godoy told reporters on Monday that Mexican authorities “are going to put him on trial in this country”.

Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured after an hours-long firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen on Friday at a compound in Guasave, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa. He was flown to Mexico City the following day.

He faces local charges for weapons offences and methamphetamine possession with intent to sell.

US involvement

Earlier on Monday, Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said Washington had requested Meza Flores’s extradition after his capture in the northern state of Sinaloa.

President Claudia Sheinbaum said US authorities provided intelligence support but did not participate directly on the ground.

US surveillance drones were authorised to help track Meza Flores before ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠the raid, authorities added, despite sensitivities over US anti-drug operations in the country in recent months.

Four Mexican soldiers and 16 alleged cartel gunmen were killed in the overnight operation, according to the Mexican Secretariat of National Defence.

Meza Flores is accused by US authorities of leading a major trafficking network that moved heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, marijuana and fentanyl across the border.



The US Department of Justice said he faces six charges in the US that include running a continuing criminal enterprise, narcoterrorism, money laundering conspiracy and weapons offences.

His arrest is the latest in a series of high-profile anti-cartel operations by Mexico, including the February killing of Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera, as US President Donald ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Trump presses ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌the Sheinbaum government to crack down on organised crime.

World.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
World.content:
The head of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI told the BBC that the Nvidia board must have been under "enormous pressure" from the White House to reinstate Huang.

Prof Stuart Russell, who is professor of computer science at UC Berkeley, said the stock price of Nvidia and similar firms has been a major factor in "underpinning US economic growth for years".

"I assume the White House was worried that the markets would go down a lot further in the next few weeks unless they go him back in," he says.

Trump's vocal backing of Huang comes despite the concerns of US lawmakers, including some Republicans, over the CEO's affair and Nvidia's compliance with US export controls.

Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to lead the House of Representatives as Speaker when Democrats take control in January called the decision to reinstate Huang "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible" and vowed that Congress will conduct "a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation".

"We will not allow America's national security to be sold out by the Trump Administration for personal financial gain," he said, echoing many lawmakers on Monday who said that Congress must pass strong export control legislation.

Huang is scheduled to appear before Congress for a closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December. Two days later, he has been asked to testify before the Senate banking committee.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, who is set to be chairwoman of the Senate Banking Committee once Democrats take control of the chamber in January, said in a statement that the reinstatement was "reckless".

"The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement," she also said.

Republicans, too, called for answers.

"Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang," said Republican Representative Don Bacon, who chairs a House subcommittee on cyber security.

"We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible."

The chair of the Senate's select committee on intelligence, Republican Tom Cotton said: "The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it's not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back."

World.title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
World.content:
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.

The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.

The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as a spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.

The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.

When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.

Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.

Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.

China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.

On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".

The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.

The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.

China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.

Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.

Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, has been reported to be one if its largest customers.

Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.

Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.

Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.

That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.

Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.

Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.

Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take.

The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.

In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.

Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

World.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
World.content:
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.

Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.

Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".

The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".

Rutte told the press conference in Berlin that Nato had a variety of response options.

"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary," he said.

Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, the reports by broadcasters NDR and WDR, and newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.

Standing alongside Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".

"Reports that Russia is planning to introduce nuclear weaponry into space are not new, yet they remain no less shocking," he said.

A German government spokesman earlier also did not confirm or deny the reports, but said it was taking the reports "very seriously", AFP reported. The spokesman, however, warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".

Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, said having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario", German paper Handelsblatt reported.

Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit. Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.

In 2024 the US claimed Russia was developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead. Russia denied the accusation.

"Our position is clear and transparent. We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.

In September the US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the US had "on-orbit, space-control weapons" circling the planet, but did not provide specifics. In response to the announcement, the Kremlin's Peskov told Russian media that space "must be free of any weapon".

World.title: India's 'cockroach' party leader says he was stopped from flying to UK
World.content:
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.

Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".

It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

Das, who rose to prominence in India earlier this year after Gen Z-led protests, said that he had been invited by the Oxford Union to speak about the movement.

He said that he was also scheduled to speak at other universities in Cambridge and Edinburgh.

"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual [government] was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions," he wrote on X.

A federal home ministry spokesperson directed the BBC to airport authorities and the Delhi police for comment on Das's allegations.

Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said in a post on X that she and Das had been invited by the Oxford Union but that her visa had been rejected a few days ago.

"The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country," she wrote.

Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.

In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .

In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands of people detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.

The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.

There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.

In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.

In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

World.title: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
World.content:
Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't.

The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi, co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?

The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch.

Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes, has called it "a dangerous escalation".

It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism.

Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga.

Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks â what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" â have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia.

The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers.

And Ukraine has also been active further south in Africa where its forces have targeted Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps, the successor to the infamous Wagner Group that was accused of carrying out numerous human rights abuses.

It's not just Russia that will be alarmed by this latest Ukrainian operation in Benghazi harbour. The United Nations mission in Libya has already expressed its "deep concern".

Libyan officials point out that their country is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, although the Merkury and an accompanying cargo ship that was also hit were berthed in the eastern part of Libya controlled by the pro-Moscow warlord and self-styled "Field Marshal" Khalifa Haftar.

World.title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book
World.content:
GisÃ¨le Pelicot has said she has been "once again humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media to promote a book about coercive control.

The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay.

Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious.

The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".

Pelicot told BFM: "I am deeply shocked that images from the most intimate part of my private life are being displayed and exploited for commercial purposes."

"Today I find myself once again humiliated, exposed and hurt, as if the ordeal of the trial had not been enough," she said.

The essay was written by Sabine Prokhoris, a philosopher and psychoanalyst, who has previously criticised the Me Too movement.

French media reported that Tinbad, a small Paris publishing house, emailed nude photos of Pelicot taken by her ex-husband to some media outlets in order to promote the essay.

In a statement on its website, Tinbad said that no further print runs of the book would be produced beyond the 280 copies already in circulation.

"We offer our sincerest apologies to Ms GisÃ¨le Pelicot," it said. The company also apologised to the author.

Tinbad said "no images of rape or pornographic videos" were sent to the media.

French news agency AFP quoted the blurb of the book as saying coercive control was "a cornerstone of #MeToo orthodoxy".

"These psychological situations, fundamentally ambiguous in nature, involve each of the parties in an equally responsible, though not symmetrical, way," it said.

Pelicot's lawyer Christophe Bigot told BFM the book "calls into question her status as a victim".

Prokhoris told AFP that she placed "full responsibility" for the "inappropriate" promotional campaign on her publisher.

Fifty men were convicted alongside Pelicot's ex-husband in 2024, in a case that made her a global feminist icon.

After her husband was arrested for secretly filming underneath women's skirts in a supermarket, she discovered she had been repeatedly raped by dozens of men, including her husband, while unconscious, over a period of nearly a decade.

Pelicot said she decided to waive her right to anonymity to show how "shame has to change sides" from victims to perpetrators.

If you have been affected by the issues in this story help and support can be found at BBC Action Line.

World.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
World.content:
Gaza has been turned into "a toxic wasteland", with more than 99% of the Palestinian territory showing indicators of environmental contamination from Israeli military attacks, a new report from the charity Oxfam says, external.

Heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and dioxins and biological contaminants are threats to Palestinians now and potentially for decades to come, it says.

Oxfam International's executive director, Amitabh Behar, said the impact on Gaza "will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival".

In response, the Israeli embassy in the UK said the report "falls short of professional standards".

Behar also accused Israel of "environmental war crimes" as part of an "ongoing genocide in Gaza".

Israel has rejected genocide accusations in an ongoing case at the International Court of Justice as baseless and distorted. It maintains that its military campaign in Gaza is an act of self-defence against Hamas in response to the group's deadly attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, and that it takes steps to mitigate civilian harm.

World.title: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
World.content:
A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.

Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.

Ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024. Iran's laws ban public performances by women and require them to wear headscarves and modest clothing.

This June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material", which they had denied.

In addition to being sentenced to 74 lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years.

At the end of September, an appeals court in Qom rejected the defendants' appeal and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said.

There was widespread condemnation of the sentences from other Iranian artists and human rights activists, who warned that flogging constituted cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violated the international prohibition on torture.

On Monday, one of the defendants' lawyers told the BBC that Ahmadi and four of her male co-defendants had been flogged at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom.

"We did everything in our power to have the verdict overturned, or at least to secure a reduction in the sentence or a suspension, but it didn't work out," he said.

"The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately."

Pro-reform daily Etemad cited another defence lawyer, Mostafa Nili, as identifying the four men flogged alongside Ahmadi as Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari.

"Parastoo Ahmadi's flogging for singing and dressing as she chooses is a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights and a chilling demonstration of the Iranian authorities' determination to suppress women's freedoms and to violently punish anyone who dares to challenge their discriminatory laws and policies," said Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI).

Under Iranian law, which is based on the country's interpretation of Sharia, women and girls above the age of puberty must cover their hair with a hijab and wear long, loose-fitting clothing to disguise their figures.

In 2022, protests swept across the Islamic Republic following the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman who was detained by morality police in Tehran in September that year for allegedly wearing her hijab "improperly".

Women burnt their headscarves or waved them in the air at the nationwide demonstrations against the clerical establishment, during which hundreds of people were killed in a crackdown by security forces.

Since then, many women and girls have stopped covering their hair in public altogether in open defiance of the dress code. Authorities have responded with periodic waves of arrests, warnings, business closures and other measures.

In January this year, thousands of people were killed and tens of thousands were arrested when security forces crushed another wave of mass anti-establishment protests, this time sparked by the country's economic crisis.

Since the start of Iran's war with the US and Israel in late February, authorities have intensified their use of the death penalty against protesters.

According to the Norway-based group Iran Human Rights, at least 39 men convicted over January's protests and two convicted over the 2022 unrest have been executed, along with 16 people allegedly affiliated with banned opposition groups and 17 others convicted of espionage or collaborating with foreign states.

Another 121 protesters detained in January, including six women and five juvenile offenders, have been sentenced to death and are at imminent risk of execution, it says.

World.title: Gombe PDP opposes Governor Yahaya’s proposed ₦100 billion borrowing ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
The Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has opposed Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s plan to borrow ₦100 billion, describing the move as fiscally detrimental to the state’s incoming administration.

In a statement issued on Monday and signed by the state PDP’s spokesperson Abdulkadir Dukku, the opposition party expressed concern over the loan’s timing and structure, as it is being sought with about six months remaining in the current administration’s tenure and less than 60 days before the general elections.

According to the PDP, Governor Yahaya wrote to the Speaker of the Gombe State House of Assembly on 4 November—a letter acknowledged the same day—seeking legislative approval to participate in the Sovereign Promissory Note Discounting Programme II.

The PDP alleged that under the terms outlined in the governor’s correspondence, Gombe State would commit to a ₦100 billion obligation while receiving only ₦77 billion before applicable taxes, resulting in an immediate ₦23 billion deduction.

“Furthermore, approximately ₦8.333 billion will be deducted monthly from the Federation Account for twelve consecutive months to service this dubious debt,” Mr Dukku stated.

The party warned that the repayment structure could consume over 60 per cent of the state’s monthly Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) receipts, potentially hampering the next administration’s ability to fund salaries, healthcare, education, and social welfare.

The opposition party also faulted the executive request for a lack of project specificity.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

While the state government reportedly indicated the funds would finance priority capital projects captured in the Appropriation Law, the PDP noted that the letter omitted project names, locations, contract sums, and implementation timelines.

Citing multidimensional poverty statistics in the state, the PDP appealed to President Bola Tinubu to intervene and restrain the state government from taking on additional debt despite increased federal allocations to states.

The party further urged commercial banks and financial institutions to exercise caution before extending credit facilities to an outgoing administration, vowing to resist the borrowing through lawful means.

The Gombe State Government had not yet issued an official response to the opposition party’s allegations.

World.title: 15 APC supporters killed, 27 injured in Zamfara road crash; party postpones rally
World.content:
Fifteen supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) died, and 27 others were injured in a road crash in Zamfara State on Monday, according to the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC).

The accident occurred near Kisami village on the Gummi–Daki-Takwas–Anka road as the supporters travelled to or from the party’s presidential and governorship campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara.

The crash prompted the postponement of another campaign rally scheduled for Tuesday, 24 November, in Maru Local Government Area.

According to an FRSC First Information Report forwarded to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) following a confirmation request, the accident occurred at about 12:30 p.m. and involved a Toyota Camry and a Mitsubishi Canter truck. The report’s findings were published by SolaceBase in a NAN account.

The report, issued by Isah Aliyu of the FRSC Zamfara Sector Command, recorded 52 people involved in the crash, comprising 50 men and two women.

Fifteen men died, and 27 other men sustained injuries, while eight men and two women escaped unhurt.

The injured and the bodies of those who died were taken to General Hospital, Gummi, for medical attention and other necessary procedures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The FRSC identified wrongful overtaking and loss of control as the suspected causes of the accident.

The report did not explain how the 52 people were distributed between the two vehicles.

Conflicting accounts of direction of travel

The Zamfara State APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign Council said the supporters were travelling from Gummi to Talata-Mafara to attend the campaign flag-off when the accident occurred.

However, Channels Television reported that the victims were returning to Gummi after the event.

The conflicting accounts have not been independently reconciled.

APC postpones Maru rally

In a statement issued on Monday by its Secretary-General, Abubakar Nakwada, the Zamfara State APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign Council announced the postponement of Tuesday’s rally in Maru.

The council said the decision was taken in honour of those who died and in solidarity with their families.

It said the injured were receiving medical attention and pledged to monitor their condition and support them and the bereaved families. A revised campaign timetable would be announced later, the council said.

The Zamfara State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Muhammad Dantawasa, separately confirmed the accident in a statement issued on Monday.

“The government expresses its deep sorrow over the unfortunate incident and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families,” he said, according to the NAN report.

He also conveyed condolences to the Gummi Emirate and the APC, expressed sympathy for the injured and urged residents to remain calm.

Campaign flag-off

The crash occurred on the day the APC formally launched its 2027 presidential and governorship campaigns at the main Eid Ground in Talata-Mafara.

According to a promotional press release published by PREMIUM TIMES on Monday, the rally was attended by Governor Dauda Lawal, former governors Abdul’aziz Yari, Ahmad Sani Yarima and Mahmud Aliyu Shinkafi, alongside other party leaders.

Mr Lawal used the occasion to seek support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and his own bid for a second term as governor.

World.title: Cornerstone Plc reaches deal to merge with AIICO Insurance
World.content:
Lagos-listed Cornerstone Plc, an insurance holding company lately acquired by Chapel Hill Denham, the investment banking firm of one of Nigeria’s most aggressive dealmakers, Bolaji Balogun, entered into a pact with rival AIICO Insurance to combine into a single entity that will create Nigeria’s largest insurer by “gross written premium, insurance revenue, and capital.”

Mr Balogun, who is the first son of the late Subomi Balogun, founder of First City Monument Bank, currently chairs Unilever Nigeria.

Two insurance subsidiaries of AIICO Insurance, the country’s biggest quoted insurer by assets, will also be folded into the surviving company.

The deal has secured approval from both companies’ boards and will now seek shareholders’ approval, Cornerstone said in a Monday regulatory filing.

“The merger would bring together two complementary insurance businesses, with combined shareholders’ funds of approximately ₦194 billion and total assets of approximately ₦858 billion,” the group said.

“On completion, the merged company will remain listed on Nigerian Exchange Limited,” it added.

Shares in Cornerstone and AIICO accelerated by 10 per cent and 9.9 per cent respectively at market close on Monday on account of the news, making them the day’s second- and third-best-performing stocks.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Chapel Hill Denham became Cornerstone’s majority owner this year in the wake of the insurance industry’s recapitalisation, snapping up a 75 per cent stake in the underwriter, a company insider who doesn’t want his identity divulged told PREMIUM TIMES.

That is worth N74.9 billion, using Cornerstone’s closing share price on Monday.

Cornerstone announced last week it had completed a transformation into a holding company after the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission greenlit the move, the National Insurance Commission gave approval in principle, and the Federal High Court sanctioned the plan.

Under the new structure, subsidiary Cornerstone Life Assurance runs the group’s life insurance operations, Cornerstone General Insurance Limited (formerly FIN Insurance Company Limited) oversees its general insurance business, while Hilal Takaful Insurance Limited will continue to undertake the Group’s Takaful insurance operations.

In a statement on Monday, AIICO disclosed that Leapfrog III Nigeria Insurance Holdings, its second-biggest shareholder, agreed to offload its 30.5 per cent interest or 11.17 billion shares in the company to Insur Investments Limited, an investment vehicle sponsored by Cornerstone.

Using AIICO’s closing share price on Monday, the stake is worth N48.5 billion.

World.title: Eno admits Akwa Ibom federal lawmaker ‘not doing well’, pleads with voters to re-elect him
World.content:
Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has publicly acknowledged concerns about the performance of Clement Jimbo, the member representing Abak/Etim Ekpo/Ika Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, but appealed to voters to re-elect him.

Mr Eno made the appeal on Monday during the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign in Ika Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom, where he called on the electorate to support Mr Jimbo despite what he described as concerns about the lawmaker’s performance.

In an unusually candid appeal, the governor said he had been told that Mr Jimbo was “not doing well” but asked the people to vote for him, invoking their respect for political leaders and elders.

“I learnt you (Clement Jimbo) are not doing well. But Ika people, please vote for him. What we have done today, let it cover him. Show the respect you people have for elders,” Mr Eno told the crowd.

The governor’s intervention appeared to point to the political difficulty facing the lawmaker as he seeks a second term ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Eno first asked Mr Jimbo to come forward, saying he had heard complaints about his performance. He then handed the lawmaker over to Senate President Godswill Akpabio to raise his hand, before also presenting him to the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo.

The governor then explained why he believed the electorate should not reject the lawmaker, suggesting that Mr Jimbo had sought the backing of powerful political figures to secure his political future.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Vote for Clement Jimbo. We are saying someone used to hide under someone’s back and stand out. He has run and hidden behind the Senate president and the governor. He has run to embrace someone. He has run to embrace the minister,” he said.

Using an illustration from childhood, Mr Eno likened the lawmaker’s political manoeuvring to a child seeking protection from another adult to escape punishment from his father.

He argued that rejecting Mr Jimbo would embarrass the influential leaders whose support the lawmaker had sought.

“He has run to hide behind the Senate president; will you disgrace the Senate president? He has run to hold the governor; will you disgrace your governor? He has run to hide behind the minister; will you disgrace the minister?” he asked.

“So, forget that unwholesome plan.”

Mr Eno further told the gathering that he and other political leaders had intervened to address issues the lawmaker could not resolve on his own.

“Ironing out issues is good. Now, what he cannot do, we have done,” he said.

The governor’s appeal comes amid questions about Mr Jimbo’s representation and whether his record in the House of Representatives justifies another term.

Previous rejection in Etim Ekpo

Monday’s appeal is not the first time the APC lawmaker has faced apparent resistance from constituents during a campaign for his re-election.

On 24 September, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Jimbo faced apparent rejection at a political event in Etim Ekpo Local Government Area when APC chieftain and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Emmanuel Enoidem, appealed to residents to support his return to the House of Representatives.

Mr Enoidem, who had previously served as national legal adviser of the Peoples Democratic Party, told the gathering: “We will return him whether you like it or not.”

The audience’s apparent resistance to Mr Enoidem’s appeal raised questions about the lawmaker’s acceptance in parts of his constituency, despite the backing of influential political figures.

Governor Eno’s latest intervention in Ika suggests that persuading constituents to support Mr Jimbo’s second-term ambition remains a concern for the APC leadership in the federal constituency.

Questions over performance

Mr Jimbo’s performance has previously come under public scrutiny.

In August 2025, PREMIUM TIMES reported that a constituent, Fabian Atang, publicly challenged the lawmaker to provide evidence of his achievements since assuming office.

Mr Jimbo responded by listing several interventions, including the completion of a town hall in Abak, grading of the 10.8-kilometre Ediene/Etinan Road, construction of a solar-powered borehole, provision of school furniture, facilitation of a federal government job and business grants to constituents.

He also cited his legislative activities and petitions on behalf of constituents.

Mr Atang subsequently described the listed achievements as impressive but said more needed to be done, arguing that a good record of representation should speak for the lawmaker beyond political considerations.

Mr Jimbo is serving his first term in the House of Representatives, having been elected in 2023 on the APC platform.

PREMIUM TIMES could not immediately get a comment from the lawmaker as he did not respond to calls and text messages from our reporter.

World.title: 2027: APC will lose Delta State to NDC – Omo-Agege
World.content:
Ovie Omo-Agege, a former Deputy Senate President, has predicted that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) will lose Delta State to the opposition in the 2027 general elections.

Mr Omo-Agege, who is contesting the Delta Central Senatorial District seat on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) platform, said the state’s political dynamics favour Peter Obi, his party’s presidential candidate.

He made the prediction on Monday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he discussed political violence recorded in the state during campaigns and political rallies.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that Mr Omo-Agege’s campaign team was attacked, leaving four people dead and others injured.

The former senator said the political atmosphere in Delta favoured Mr Obi, as it did in the 2023 presidential election, noting the former Anambra State governor remained the most popular presidential candidate in the state.

“Peter Obi won here in 2023, and he did so without an agent; he did so without Omo-Agege, he did so without others. He remains very popular here, and a combination of my support base and Obi’s own support base here in Delta State; there’s no chance that APC will have anything, and they know that,” he said.

Mr Omo-Agege maintained that the factors that contributed to Mr Obi’s victory in Delta in 2023 would remain relevant in the 2027 elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The same reason that made Obi win in 2023 here when the PDP was in power, it is the same PDP character that moved to the APC, and when they did that, those of us whom they pushed out left the party and went to NDC. So, basically what we have now is the same PDP but under a new name, the APC,” he said.

The former deputy senate president also said many voters in the state were dissatisfied with the ruling party because of the rising cost of living.

“We’re fighting very hard to ensure that Peter Obi wins. Here in Delta State, the challenge we’re having is this. These guys knew that on the campaign trail, they have nothing to tell the people. The electorate, the people here, are hungry, they’re very angry, and they’re looking for the slightest opportunity to get rid of this government. They cannot go and tell people that this is what this government has done,” he said.

The outcome of the 2023 presidential election in Delta State was a major setback for the two dominant political parties, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the APC, as Mr Obi, who contested under the Labour Party, defeated their candidates.

Mr Obi polled 341,866 votes to emerge winner in the state, defeating Atiku Abubakar of the PDP, who secured 161,600 votes, while Mr Tinubu of the APC came third with 90,183 votes.

Mr Obi’s victory was particularly significant because Delta was governed by the PDP at the time, and the then governor, Ifeanyi Okowa, was Mr Atiku’s running mate in the election.

Mr Obi’s victory reflected the strong support he enjoyed during the 2023 elections, particularly amid the nationwide political movement that attracted many young voters and supporters seeking an alternative to the two dominant parties.

Mr Obi won 18 of the state’s 25 local government areas, while the PDP won the remaining seven, according to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Oborevwori not working for Tinubu

Mr Omo-Agege also alleged that Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori was not making sufficient efforts to secure President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 because he knew the president would lose the state.

The former senator claimed that the governor was more concerned about ensuring his defeat in the Delta Central senatorial election than securing victory for Mr Tinubu.

READ ALSO: Police speak on deadly attack on NDC supporters in Delta

“I’m not running for the same office with him (Oborevwori), but he’s giving the impression in Delta State that it is he and I in the contest.

“He’s even telling people that even if Tinubu doesn’t win, Omo-Agege must not win because, as far as he’s concerned, Tinubu is not really his issue. He’s not working for Tinubu; all he wants to do is to make sure that I lose this election,” he alleged.

Mr Omo-Agege further alleged that opposition parties, particularly the NDC, were being intimidated by the ruling party in the state.

He appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to ensure adequate security for opposition parties and their members in Delta State ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: 2027: Ebonyi PDP inaugurates campaign council
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State on Monday inaugurated its campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party announced the council’s constitution in a statement issued in Abakaliki and signed by its spokesperson in the state, Darlington Onwe.

According to the statement, the council comprises experienced political leaders, grassroots mobilisers, women, and youths drawn from the 13 local government areas and 171 political wards in the state.

The statement said the council would coordinate the party’s statewide campaign activities, strengthen voter engagement and mobilise support for the PDP across all elective positions in the general elections.

It described the council as part of efforts to advance the political ambition of the party’s governorship candidate, Ifeanyi-Chukwuma Odii.

The party urged all appointed members and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline and commitment towards achieving its electoral objectives.

It also called on party faithful and stakeholders to work collectively towards rebuilding and repositioning the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The campaign slogan for the election is “Anyi G’Emeya,” Igbo words translated to mean “Yes, We Can.”

The Director-General of the campaign is Nwanne Ominyi, while Paul Okorie is the deputy director-general operations.

Others are: Chigozie Omege, deputy DG Ebonyi North Zone, Justus Ikechukwu-Okorie, deputy DG Ebonyi South Zone, Festus Okoha, deputy DG Ebonyi Central Zone and Mudi Erenede, director legal services.

Ikechukwu Nwobo is the campaign spokesperson, while Okorie C. Okorie is the director special duties & protocol, among others.

(NAN)

World.title: Killing of Delta NDC Supporters: Keyamo asks Oborevwori to urgently address the people
World.content:
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has urged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State to urgently address the people of the state over Monday’s killing of four Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters by gunmen suspected to be political thugs.

The incident happened at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State where the NDC went on a campaign tour ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said in a statement on Monday evening that four people were killed in the attack, and that Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for the Delta Central Senatorial District for the elections, was the target of an assassination attempt.

Mr Keyamo, in a statement on Monday night, condemned the killing and offered condolences to the bereaved families.

“I condemn in the strongest possible terms the killing of these persons, just as I also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator in broad daylight by identified supporters of a political party in Asaba on 7 November, 2026,” said Mr Keyamo who is from Delta State.

“I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone.”

The minister called on security agencies to fish out perpetrators of the killings in the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country.

“As can be seen, anyone can be a victim. I have always maintained that it is only law enforcement agencies that are allowed to deal with offenders. It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” the minister said.

READ ALSO: Police speak on deadly attack on NDC supporters in Delta

The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area over the killing, while the police have deployed operatives to the area.

Meanwhile, Omo-Agege campaign mentioned a local government official whom it alleged led the attack. It challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to condemn the attack and order immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for it.

World.title: Police speak on deadly attack on NDC supporters in Delta
World.content:
The police command in Delta State said it has deployed its operatives to the area where gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed some members of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) who were on a campaign tour on Monday.

The incident happened at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said in a statement on Monday evening that four people were killed in the attack, and that Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for the Delta Central Senatorial District for the 2027 elections, was the target of an assassination attempt.

Mr Omo-Agege is a former deputy president of the Nigeria Senate.

“The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, Samuel E. Erale, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order,” Bright Edafe, the police spokesperson in the state, said in a statement on Monday night.

“The commissioner of police has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.”

The police also urged residents to comply with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government on Ughelli North over the incident.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The commissioner of police warns political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives.”

Mr Edafe, a superintendent of police, said the police commissioner condoled with the bereaved family and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

The Omo-Agege campaign mentioned a local government official whom it alleged led the attack. It challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta to condemn the attack and order immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for it.

It also called on the police and the State Security Service to investigate the incident.

‘Campaigning is not a crime’

“We state it clearly: Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence,” Sunny Areh, a media adviser to Mr Omo-Agege, said in the statement on behalf of the campaign.

“We call on INEC, civil society organisations, the international community, and all lovers of democracy to take note: Deltans are being shot and killed for exercising their democratic right to campaign.

“To the families of Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro: We mourn with you. Your loved ones did not die in vain. Their blood cries out for justice, and we will not rest until justice is done.

“To our supporters: Do not retaliate. Do not take the law into your hands. We refuse to be intimidated. We refuse to be silenced. Our ward-to-ward tour of Delta Central will continue.”

World.title: Omo Agege attack: ‘Enough is enough’, arrest, prosecute perpetrators – Keyamo tells police
World.content:
Festus Keyamo, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible.

Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment.

He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery.

The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice.

“I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said.

Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings.

“Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said.

He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence.

The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said.

Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens.

He described such conduct as a sign of desperation and called on the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address residents and warn those threatening violence.

“I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone.

“Enough is enough,” he said.

World.title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, meets Enikanolaiye
World.content:
Fani-Kayode

Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials.

Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja.

He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled.

“There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue.

“If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he said.

The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa.

He said he had initially planned to spend only a few days in South Africa following his posting but had extended his stay to complete necessary diplomatic procedures.

Fani-Kayode also dismissed reports that his meeting with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) over the controversy surrounding the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa amounted to a reprimand.

He described the engagement as cordial and constructive, saying concerns were addressed professionally by both sides.

“Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said.

The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest.

“I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. We will do our best to build that bridge, and that bridge must never be broken,” he said.

He, however, stressed that efforts to improve bilateral relations must not come at the expense of Nigeria’s national interests or the dignity, rights and welfare of Nigerians living in South Africa.

Fani-Kayode expressed concern over persistent xenophobic attacks, killings and discriminatory rhetoric targeting Nigerians in the country.

He also condemned attempts to portray Nigerians collectively as criminals and drug dealers, insisting that the actions of a few individuals should not be used to stigmatise an entire community.

“As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa.

“Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minority engaged in wrongdoing should not be used to define an entire community,” he said.

The envoy pledged to continue raising concerns whenever Nigeria’s dignity and the rights of its citizens abroad were threatened.

World.title: Tinubu to Lagos Igbo: Vote for me in 2027, I was angry you didn’t vote for me in 2023
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Igbo residents in Lagos to vote for him in the 2027 presidential election, admitting that he was angry with those who did not support his candidacy in the 2023 polls.

Tinubu made the appeal on Monday during a town hall meeting with Igbo youths, elders and community leaders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, National Theatre, Lagos.

The meeting was organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative.

The president, who described the Igbo as his brothers and sisters, said his administration remained committed to inclusive governance, national unity and equity, assuring that no section of the country would be left behind under his Renewed Hope Agenda.

He urged the Igbo community to strengthen its unity, deepen its participation in national politics and collaborate with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful and prosperous Nigeria.

Tinubu also acknowledged the contributions of Igbo communities to the country’s economic growth, while commending the stakeholders for attending the meeting.

Expressing appreciation for their presence, he said: “To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses, left money-making to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you.”

He stressed that national development required collective commitment, mutual understanding and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement in addressing its challenges and advancing its interests within the Nigerian federation.

Explaining some of his administration’s policies, Tinubu said his government was working to ensure stability in tertiary institutions, improve infrastructure and expand access to education for disadvantaged Nigerians.
