“To eliminate the crisis in the universities and to build good roads and the engineers that will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop,” he said.

The president said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) was helping to improve access to higher education, while the government was also providing financial support for agriculture and businesses through relevant intervention programmes.

“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money into agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan,” he said.

Tinubu, who confirmed his intention to seek re-election, said the Constitution permitted him to serve a second term.

“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.

“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat akpu,” he added.

He subsequently appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and support him, Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, and other party candidates in the 2027 elections.

“I am here to listen to you. I am here to work with you. Igbos are my brothers and sisters.

“Some of you did not vote for me in 2023; I vex o. Now, we have settled. Get your PVC, and you will vote for me this time. Come by January 16; you will vote. Agreement is agreement. Tinubu is APC,” he said.

According to the Independent National Electoral Commission’s election timetable, the presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027.

Tinubu contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the APC alongside Peter Obi of the Labour Party and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party.

However, he lost Lagos State, his political stronghold since 1999, to Obi in the election.

World.title: It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
World.content:
Omo-Agege

Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him.

Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North.

He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him.

He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details.

He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue.



His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on.

“As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started. The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing.

The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing.

Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice.

“We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said.



We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said.

He also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, saying the attack would not deter him from continuing his campaign.



“If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” Omo-Agege said.

World.title: Police arrest eight suspected drug dealers in Jigawa
World.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested eight suspected drug dealers and consumers, including two women aged 18 and 20, during operations targeting illicit drug trafficking and substance abuse across the state.

The arrests were disclosed in a statement issued to newsmen by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam.

Adam identified the suspects as Garba Sabo, 20; Kamal Ibrahim, 20; Muhammad Ibrahim, 25; Muhammad Nura, 25; Muhammad Bako, 25; Habu Usman, 23, also known as Makwa; Firdausi Sani, 20; and Nusaiba Ibrahim, 18.

According to the statement, the suspects, aged between 18 and 25, were arrested at different locations, including Gadama, Bulangu, Sara, Gumel and Kazaure towns. One of the female suspects was identified as a resident of Sandamu Daura in Katsina State.

During the operations, the police recovered 8,739 assorted illicit drug-related substances, including suspected Indian hemp, tramadol, pregabalin, diazepam and other intoxicating substances.

The recovered exhibits included 4,035 pieces of Exol, 1,384 pieces of D5, 634 pregabalin capsules, 896 tramadol capsules, 248 diazepam tablets and 1,199 wraps of marijuana, alongside three and a half blocks of the substance.

Other items recovered included rubber solution, whisky, shisha, syrups, snuff and other intoxicating substances.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Tijjani Murtala, said the command would sustain its operations against drug trafficking and substance abuse, warning those involved in the illicit trade to desist or face prosecution.

He said the police would continue to deploy intelligence-led policing, surveillance and targeted operations to dismantle drug distribution networks and tackle criminal activities associated with substance abuse.

The commissioner also called on parents, guardians, community leaders and religious institutions to intensify efforts to discourage drug abuse, particularly among young people.

He urged members of the public to support the police in the fight against drug-related activities across the state.

World.title: INEC not anticipating technical glitches in 2027 — Abia REC
World.content:
…Says commission building ICT facility, procuring equipment to prevent glitches

…Gives Abia’s total registered voters as 2.62m

…Explains why INEC relies on federal university VCs for collation, returning officers

…Rules out owing ad-hoc staff allowances

By Steve Oko

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured voters in Abia State that their votes will count in the 2027 general elections, declaring that the commission is putting necessary measures in place to deliver a free, fair, credible and seamless exercise.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Abia State, Professor Sylvia Uchenna Agu, gave the assurance in an exclusive interview with Vanguard, disclosing that the commission had commenced the receipt of non-sensitive election materials, including generators and brand-new Hilux vans, from its headquarters in Abuja.

Agu, who assumed office in April, also spoke on the commission’s efforts to address infrastructural deficiencies at its Abia office, prevent a recurrence of the electronic transmission controversy, popularly known as the ‘technical glitch’, during the 2023 presidential election, ensure credible recruitment of ad-hoc personnel and improve election logistics.

She disclosed that Abia’s voter register had increased from 2,180,140 in 2023 to 2,620,151, following the registration of 460,011 additional voters in the last Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.

The REC also explained why INEC relies heavily on federal universities in recruiting collation and returning officers, defended the commission’s use of other categories of ad-hoc personnel and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

Excerpts:

The 2027 general elections are approaching. How prepared is INEC in Abia State for the exercise?

We are very much prepared. By the grace of God, we are still receiving our non-sensitive election materials. We have received generators, vehicles and other materials. For the first time, we have received brand-new Hilux vans, and more vehicles are expected in the coming days.

Preparations are on top gear. On a weekly basis, we receive materials from Abuja, and the commission is making every effort to ensure that we deliver a seamless election. I can assure you that we are working towards a very successful election in 2027.

You mentioned receiving new vehicles and other materials. But what is the state of your operational facilities in Abia, particularly your ICT infrastructure, which is critical to election management?

When I assumed office in April, I was not impressed with what I saw. The condition of the facility was not encouraging. Sensitive materials, including result sheets for the local government areas, were packed in Ghana-Must-Go bags. There were no proper cabinets for storing them.

I was equally concerned that there was no dedicated ICT building. The ICT Department was sharing an office with the Operations Department, which was not conducive to the effective handling of our Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines. The BVAS machines occupied the strong room meant for the Operations Department, while the Operations materials were squeezed into a corner.

I immediately travelled to Abuja and met the National Chairman of INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan. I explained what I had seen, but he initially found it difficult to believe.

However, what he did afterwards was quite remarkable. He immediately dispatched a fact-finding team to Abia to verify my claims. He wanted to establish whether we truly had no dedicated ICT building, whether our result sheets were stored in Ghana-Must-Go bags and whether the ICT and Operations Departments were sharing the same office.

The next day, he sent the Estate and Works Department to inspect the facility. I was still in Abuja when I received a call that the officials had arrived. I instructed my staff to show them everything without hiding anything because I was in Abuja to address the same problems.

What has changed since then?

Following the inspection, plans were drawn for an ICT building, and construction is ongoing. Work is progressing day and night, and we hope to commission the facility in the first week of December.

We have also received 17 cabinets meant for the 17 local government areas to ensure proper storage of sensitive election materials.

The cabinets are already in our stores. We are waiting for the ICT building to be completed so that we can move the relevant materials there and allow the Operations Department to reclaim its office.

So, significant improvements are taking place, and I appreciate the National Chairman for responding promptly to our concerns.

Electronic transmission of election results remains a major issue of public concern, particularly following the technical glitch that marred the uploading of presidential election results in 2023. What has INEC done to prevent a recurrence in 2027?

In 2023, the BVAS worked, but unfortunately, we experienced a technical glitch that affected the uploading of the presidential election results.

We were supposed to upload the results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), but we could not do so because of the glitch. It was unfortunate.

What assurances can you give Nigerians that there will be no such technical problem in 2027?

We are not anticipating any glitch in 2027. We have held several meetings to ensure that whatever caused the problem is addressed and nipped in the bud. By the grace of God, I trust that there will not be a recurrence.

Some Nigerians have lost confidence in INEC following the controversies surrounding previous elections. Some have even vowed never to vote again because they believe their votes will not count. Has the commission done enough to restore public confidence?

I would be surprised if Abia voters expressed such sentiments because, in 2023, votes counted in Abia, and in 2027, they will count again. We are determined to ensure that the electoral process is credible and that the will of the people prevails.

By the grace of God, we have addressed the problem that resulted in the technical glitch. We are working to ensure that such a situation does not arise again.

There have been persistent allegations of compromise against some ad-hoc election personnel, particularly university-based collation and returning officers. What measures has INEC put in place to ensure that only credible persons are recruited for the 2027 elections?

You know that INEC usually recruits university personnel, and we believe they are people of integrity. We normally approach the vice-chancellors of federal universities in the relevant environments and ask them to nominate men and women of substance who will not compromise when deployed for election duties.

We rely on the integrity of the vice-chancellors to give us credible personnel.

So, INEC actually involves vice-chancellors in the recruitment of ad-hoc staff?

Yes. We engage the vice-chancellors, who send the names directly to our headquarters in Abuja. Our responsibility thereafter is to train those selected.

We normally use federal universities rather than state universities.

Why does INEC prefer federal universities?

Because it is a Federal Government arrangement.

Why not also involve university-based associations such as the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) in the recruitment process?

I know the vice-chancellor is the figurehead of the university. However, I can also speak from personal experience.

Before my present assignment, when I was a lecturer in the university, I was selected to work for INEC during the 2019 elections. In my case, it was ASUU that selected me, not the vice-chancellor.

So, different arrangements may apply, but INEC works with the university authorities.

Given the criticisms and allegations against some university personnel used as ad-hoc staff, should INEC not consider involving other professional bodies, such as the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) and Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), to nominate credible members for election duties?

It is important to understand how INEC’s ad-hoc staffing arrangement works. It is not only university lecturers who work for the commission during elections.

We recruit different categories of personnel, including corps members and civil servants.

We have Assistant Presiding Officers (APOs), Supervisory Presiding Officers (SPOs), collation officers and returning officers, among others.

The APOs are usually corps members, penultimate-year university students or recent graduates. The supervisory personnel are also drawn from various government establishments and other eligible applicants.

The university personnel we primarily rely on are those serving as collation and returning officers.

Remember that the results are generated at the polling units by the personnel in the field before being taken to the collation officers. So, if there is any error or compromise, we must also examine what happens at the polling unit level.

I am not trying to exonerate university lecturers, but it is important to understand that collation officers work with the results brought to them from the field.

We have mechanisms to check possible compromise. One of them is the IReV portal, which allows members of the public to access uploaded polling unit results and monitor the process.

Once we conclude the process at the polling units, the results are uploaded. Anybody can access the IReV portal and follow the uploads.

That is one of the mechanisms designed to check electoral malpractice and enhance transparency.

Can Nigerians, therefore, trust INEC to deliver a credible election in 2027?

Emphatically, yes!

There have also been complaints in previous elections about delayed payment of allowances to ad-hoc personnel, sometimes resulting in protests. What is INEC doing to prevent such incidents in 2027?

Where I worked before, in Imo State, I am sure you did not hear such complaints. I can speak confidently about my experience there.

You will not hear such complaints in Abia because we have never owed our ad-hoc personnel.

How much do we pay them that we would want to owe them? Immediately after the election, we transfer their allowances directly to their bank accounts.

The only challenge we may encounter is where an Electoral Officer (EO) recruits somebody who subsequently provides bank account details different from the ones submitted during registration.

Remember that the EOs recruit personnel from their respective local government areas. Applicants indicate their local governments and states during registration, and they are generally deployed within those areas.

But as far as payment of allowances is concerned, we do not owe our workers.

Are you anticipating any major challenges in the 2027 elections in Abia?

At the moment, I am not anticipating any major challenge. By the grace of God, I am looking forward to a seamless election.

Are you carrying political parties and other critical stakeholders along in your preparations?

Yes, we are.

Have you held meetings with the political parties?

Yes. I have held a meeting with the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC).

I also directed the leadership to invite all the political parties because we need to engage them collectively and ensure that everybody is carried along.

We are also engaging security agencies. I just had a meeting with the police, and we are discussing security arrangements and the peace accord.

We will continue to meet with the relevant stakeholders to ensure a peaceful electoral environment.

What assurances have the security agencies given you?

We have had discussions with them, and they have assured us of their cooperation.

We are working towards a peace accord involving all the political parties. Whoever wins should be allowed to win, and whoever loses should accept the outcome peacefully.

Our desire is to have a free, fair, credible and seamless election.

What is INEC doing to sensitise voters and encourage greater participation in the 2027 elections?

We have what we call INEC Half Hour, which we use for voter education every week on radio stations. We have also been on air, engaging the public on electoral matters.

PVC collection is ongoing, and we have been distributing the cards to registered voters. We have also been using online jingles and other communication channels to create awareness.

We will intensify the sensitisation campaign when we receive the full complement of the PVCs for distribution.

How many new voters were registered in Abia during the last Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise?

We registered 460,011 new voters.

How many PVCs have arrived for collection, and what has been the response of voters?

We have received the first batch of 21,528 PVCs as of October 22, 2026. Collection is still ongoing, and we expect more batches because the cards are arriving in phases.

What is your assessment of the attitude of Abia voters towards PVC collection?

I think Abia is ready. The people have really tried this time around. They have shown interest, and they are coming out to collect their PVCs.

The turnout has been quite impressive. We expect more people to come forward as additional batches of cards arrive.

What is the current total number of registered voters in Abia State?

Abia has 2,620,151 registered voters.

In 2023, we had 2,180,140 registered voters. The additional 460,011 voters recorded during the last Continuous Voter Registration exercise have brought the total to 2,620,151.

What is your general advice to Abia voters, and what assurances can you give them that INEC is ready to deliver a credible election in 2027?

My general advice is that eligible voters should go and collect their PVCs. Your vote is your voice, and your vote will count.

Abia voters will decide. INEC will not decide for them.

Our responsibility on election day is to go to the field early enough, ensure that materials and personnel are deployed promptly and provide the necessary environment for voters to exercise their franchise.

We are going to activate our Registration Area Centres (RACs) to facilitate early deployment of personnel and materials.

I promise the people of Abia that, by the grace of God, their votes will count. Abia decides, not INEC.

Late commencement of voting has often been attributed to logistical challenges, particularly delays in the deployment of election materials and personnel. What measures are you taking to ensure that voting starts early in 2027?

We have been engaging security agencies and other relevant stakeholders. We just had a meeting with them, and we agreed that such meetings would hold every two weeks.

The essence is to identify and address potential challenges ahead of the election.

By the first week of December, we intend to visit and activate the Registration Area Centres (RACs). We want to ensure that the centres have conducive environments and the necessary facilities for election personnel to operate from.

How will RACs activation improve election logistics?

They are strategic locations from which election materials and personnel can be deployed to several polling units within an area.

The idea is to move our personnel and materials closer to the polling units ahead of election day rather than having them travel long distances from our local government offices.

Once the RACs are activated, personnel will stay close to their polling units. So, when it is time for deployment, they can leave early and get to their respective polling units without unnecessary delays.

If we can properly activate the RACs and position our personnel and materials there, it will significantly improve early deployment.

That is part of our strategy to ensure that voting commences on time and that Abia voters have a seamless electoral experience.

World.title: Troops kill two bandits, recover rifles in Kogi operation
World.content:
File image.

By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two armed bandits and recovered two AK-47 rifles and other items during an intelligence-led ambush operation in Asungwe Forest, Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State.

According to a statement by Col. Appolonia Anele, the operation followed sustained offensives against banditry and kidnapping gangs in the state.

The statement said the operation was conducted on Monday, November 23, 2026, by troops of the 12 Brigade under Operation Bem Hembe, in conjunction with other hybrid forces.

It added that the operation was launched following credible intelligence obtained from previously arrested bandits, which provided actionable leads on the movement of criminal elements operating in Asungwe Forest and adjoining communities along the boundaries of Kogi, Edo and Ondo states.

Acting on the intelligence, troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba and positioned themselves along a suspected bandits’ crossing route within the forest.

The troops subsequently made contact with the criminals and engaged them with superior firepower, neutralising two bandits, while others fled.

Items recovered during the operation included two AK-47 rifles, three magazines, 27 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, two Android phones, three Tecno keypad phones, assorted drugs and bags suspected to belong to the fleeing criminals.

The statement said the operation demonstrated the Nigerian Army’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks, disrupt bandits’ movements and deny terrorists and kidnappers freedom of action across vulnerable communities.

It added that the Army remained committed to intensifying intelligence-driven operations and sustaining pressure on criminal elements to enhance the security of lives and property.

The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations against criminal activities.

World.title: The last thing we heard was “Shoot Omo-Agege”’ – Witness
World.content:
…My three men were killed — LG chairman

By Efe Onodjae

A witness to the alleged attack on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign rally at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, has narrated how gunshots erupted at the venue, alleging that the last words they heard from a rival group were: “Shoot Omo-Agege.”

The witness, Pius Eguono, alleged that the incident followed a series of confrontations between Omo-Agege’s supporters and some youths in the community ahead of the campaign rally.

According to Eguono, Omo-Agege had been conducting consultations ahead of his campaign and had paid for the use of the community town hall for his official campaign rally scheduled for the following day.

He alleged that the town crier engaged to announce the campaign in the community was beaten up.

Eguono further claimed that on the morning of the rally, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of Ufuoma arrived at the venue alongside some youths allegedly linked to Otovwodo community and insisted that the organisers could not use the town hall.

He said the organisers accepted the decision and made alternative arrangements by erecting canopies nearby.

Recounting the events, Eguono said: “Ovie Omo-Agege had been conducting consultations ahead of his campaign. Yesterday, he sent money to pay for the town hall for his official campaign, which was scheduled to kick off today at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

“The town crier, who was also paid to make announcements about Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign, was allegedly beaten to a stupor.

“This morning, the Ufuoma DPO came in the company of Otovwodo youths and insisted that we should not use the community town hall, which we obliged. We then arranged canopies nearby.

“As the rally was ongoing, they brought a cow to roast, apparently to suffocate us with smoke, but we did not mind.

“Meanwhile, the president of Otovwodo Motor Park, Gueke, and his boys started shooting while the police were there. We drew the attention of the most senior officer, the Ufuoma Divisional Police Officer, and he stylishly said he would talk to them.

“If you watch the video clearly, you would hear the sound of gunshots while Ovie Omo-Agege was speaking. But because they were shooting up, we just decided to carry on.

“So, in order to keep us alert, some of the security men with us also fired shots up. Immediately, it was as if they were waiting for our gunshots. The next thing we heard from the Otovwodo youth leader, named Gueke, who was shooting with his boys, was: ‘Shoot Ovie Omo-Agege.’”

On his part, the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, has claimed that three of his supporters were killed during the incident.

Egbo, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the disagreement began over the use of a community hall, which he claimed had already been booked for an event he was organising for residents of Uduere.

According to him: “Yesterday (Sunday), at the village, we went there to set up our canopy for today’s and tomorrow’s events because I am hosting the entire village.

“When we got there, some people said Omo-Agege was coming and that they wanted to use the hall. So, my president told them that the hall had been booked and that they could take their event elsewhere. They refused.”

Egbo said the NDC campaign subsequently proceeded with its activities close to where his supporters had gathered, despite the disagreement.

He added that security personnel had been alerted ahead of the incident, insisting that he had taken steps to prevent violence.

“In the morning, we had received intelligence that they had brought AK-47 rifles and armed men from Sapele and Ughelli. So, I called the Area Commander and the DPO to go there and maintain peace. We even called the Army.

“When the DPO got there, he called me to say that he was appealing to them not to fight.

“So, I told my people not to talk to anybody but to enjoy themselves. They should drink, eat and be merry. They had their own event, and that was when he (Omo-Agege) was saying that I was his PA, I was this, I was that.”

Egbo, however, accused members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters, claiming that three of his men were killed.

He specifically accused one Akima, whom he described as an anti-cult operative, of shooting at his supporters at close range with a pump-action rifle.

He said: “Thereafter, as he was going, one of his boys, one Akima, who calls himself Anti-Cult, brought out a pump-action gun and opened fire on innocent citizens. He shot three of my people at close range.

“As they fired, two died. The other one we rushed to the hospital has just died. Three others are in critical condition.”

World.title: NDC’s Omo-Agege Alleges Assassination Attempt, Four Killed, Others Injured
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

• Two aides among those murdered during shooting

•Delta declares curfew in Ughelli North

•Keyamo says development disturbing, seeks probe

Sylvester Idowu in Warri





Palpable tension enveloped parts of Delta State yesterday as a former Deputy Senate President and Delta Central Senatorial Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Ovie Omo-Agege escaped an alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour of Uduere in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The incident, which occurred while the senator was addressing supporters during a campaign visit, allegedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation, in a statement issued by its Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, last night alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and members of his entourage at close range.

According to the organisation, Omo-Agege narrowly escaped being hit as bullets reportedly passed close to his head.

The campaign organisation identified two of the deceased as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, close aides of Omo-Agege.

It also named Chief Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho as among those injured, noting they were receiving medical attention.

The organisation further claimed that eyewitnesses heard the attackers shouting, “It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill,” insisting that the incident was a targeted attack on the senator rather than a political clash.

“Senator Ovie Omo-Agege was saved by a divine distraction, when bullets wheezed past his head as he was addressing the crowd that gathered to receive him

“This was not a clash. This was not a misunderstanding. This was, according to witnesses, a targeted attempt to assassinate Senator Ovie Omo-Agege”, it added.

The campaign organisation alleged that eyewitnesses said a local government boss (names withheld) allegedly led the killer squad, adding: “These are grave allegations. We demand that they be investigated immediately, transparently, and without political cover.

“We state it clearly: Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence.”

The campaign organisation demanded a public apology from the state governor if truly he was committed to peace and order the immediate arrest and investigation of all persons alleged to have participated in, financed, or directed the attack, including one Jaro Egbo, the Ughelli North LGA Council Chairman.

It also demanded that the governor should guarantee the safety of Omo-Agege, the NDC leadership, and all opposition candidates in Delta State.

“We also call on the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), and the Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, to immediately take over this investigation. The Nigeria Police must not allow this matter to be swept under the carpet.

“We in fact, call on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation as we no longer have confidence in the Delta State Police Command whose officers were present with six trucks but did nothing to prevent the attack and killings”, it added.

It called on INEC, civil society organisations, the international community, and all lovers of democracy to take note that Deltans are being shot and killed for exercising their democratic right to campaign.

Also, the Delta State Government has Imposed a curfew In Ughelli North Local Government Area until further notice.

In a statement signed by the Secretary to the Delta State Government (SSG), Dr Kingsley Emu, the government said the curfew covers the entire council area.

“Arising from alleged gunshots and attendant deaths in some parts of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, the State Government hereby declare an immediate curfew from 6pm to 6am everyday starting from today (last night) until further notice. This is to bring the situation under control. The affected area is the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area.

“The residents in the local government area are hereby advised to adhere strictly to this directive”, it warned.

Besides, the Delta State Police Command said it has commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the violence that characterised the shootings during the campaign rally of the NDC at Uduere community.

It stated that efforts were being made to identify those responsible for the incidence aimed at apprehending them and called for public support.

“The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice.

“Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety”, it stated.

According to a statement signed by the Command’s Public Relations Officer, Edafe Bright, a Superintendent of Police (SP) last night, the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order.

“The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations”, it added.

Meanwhile, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has described yesterday’s shooting as disturbing.

“I offer my deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims. I also wish all those who are injured a quick recovery.

“I condemn in the strongest possible terms the killing of these persons, just as I also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator in broad daylight by identified supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026.

“I call on the law enforcement agencies to fish out the perpetrators of these killings, both in Asaba and Ughelli, and bring them to book. I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” the minister stated

According to Keyamo, since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically, as disagreements have never led to violence and killings.

“We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is absolutely no need for a descent into violence.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim. I have always maintained that it is only law enforcement agencies that are allowed to deal with offenders. It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he maintained.

The minister called on leaders as well as the governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone.

World.title: Nvidia Stocks Surge over 30%, Gains Record $952bn as Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

• Trump hails move, says board made right decision

•I’m honoured to return, says CEO as Kress reverts to CFO position

•Senator Kennedy: It’s most expensive sex since Helen of Troy

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





Nvidia yesterday reinstated its co-founder, Jensen Huang, as president and chief executive officer, reversing its earlier decision to remove him following revelations about his personal relationships, including an alleged affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of having links to Beijing’s intelligence services.

The decision, effective immediately, followed mounting pressure from employees, shareholders, business partners and US President Donald Trump, who publicly backed Huang’s return despite the controversy surrounding his departure.

Shares of Nvidia surged 33 per cent following Huang’s reinstatement, having shed nearly 33 per cent from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on November 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on November 6.

In all, Nvidia added $952 billion in market value on Monday, setting a record for the largest single-day market cap gain by any US-listed company and pushed the company’s total valuation back to roughly $3.98 trillion, overtaking Microsoft and Alphabet to reclaim its spot as the world’s second-most valuable public company behind Apple.

The $952 billion single-day jump more than doubled the previous record set by Microsoft (~$450 billion in July 2026) and surpassed the entire market capitalisation of Samsung Electronics, THISDAY learnt.

Earlier, invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy, representing Louisiana, characterised Huang’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”.

“Mr Huang … did what he did. I hope he had a good time. It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy,” Kennedy said.

But the board of the world’s leading artificial intelligence chipmaker announced in a statement that it had unanimously voted to restore Huang as president, CEO and a member of its board of directors, following a series of discussions with him.

In the statement, the company said the board was satisfied with Huang’s candour and leadership ability, adding that it had received input from senior US government officials before reaching its decision.

“Based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” Nvidia said.

Board Chairman, Harvey Jones, said the company remained convinced that Huang was the right person to lead the technology giant, notwithstanding the circumstances that led to his resignation on November 12.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Jones said.

The reversal came less than two weeks after the board accepted Huang’s resignation and appointed its Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO while it began searching for a permanent replacement.

Jones had also publicly ruled out bringing Huang back, despite growing calls from within and outside the company for his reinstatement.

However, the campaign gathered momentum, with a petition demanding his return attracting more than 180,000 signatures, including support from billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk.

Trump also weighed in last week, expressing his desire to see Huang return to the top position, adding to pressure on the company’s leadership to reconsider its earlier position.

Huang, who built Nvidia from a video-game graphics chip designer into the dominant supplier of processors powering the global artificial intelligence industry, said he was grateful for the board’s renewed confidence.

“I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” he said. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he added.

He thanked employees, shareholders, industry leaders and business partners for their support, while expressing particular appreciation to his family.

“Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work,” he added.

Huang’s return, however, does not bring an end to the investigations surrounding the circumstances of his departure. Nvidia said an independent committee comprising only independent directors would continue investigating reports that the chief executive had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation.

The committee, which has retained independent legal counsel, was established following reports that Huang had been involved in relationships, including one with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of having links to China’s Ministry of State Security.

The allegations have not been established as findings of wrongdoing against Huang, while Beijing has denied the spying allegation. The board said Huang supported the investigation and was committed to cooperating fully until its conclusion.

In a further move to strengthen its corporate governance and address national security concerns, Nvidia disclosed that it had established a separate National Security and Export Control Committee, also comprising independent directors.

The committee will oversee trade compliance and national security risks, while the company is engaging specialist legal advisers with expertise in national security matters.

Nvidia also announced plans to recruit a Chief Compliance Officer to supervise compliance across the organisation and report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. The company said it would continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

Kress, who took over as interim chief executive following Huang’s departure, will retain her position as chief financial officer, while Jones will remain chairman of the board.

Huang’s departure had sent ripples through Silicon Valley, Taipei and Washington, given the company’s central role in supplying the advanced processors required for artificial intelligence development.

At the announcement, Nvidia shares rose more than 31 per cent in premarket trading following news of his reinstatement, reflecting the market reaction to the board’s decision to restore the executive at the centre of the company’s growth.

Meanwhile, Trump welcomed the Nvidia board’s reinstatement of Huang as CEO and said his return poses no risk to US national security.

“The Nvidia Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump said in a social media post. “The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security,” he stressed.

Trump counts Huang as a strong ally in the business world and was pushing for his reinstatement despite revelations about his extramarital affair with Chinese national Alice Huang, a suspected spy. The two are not related.

“Separately, Nvidia should continue its thorough internal investigation of the company’s compliance with US export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and patriotic duty to protect US national security,” Trump pointed out.

Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, having become the dominant supplier of advanced processors used in artificial intelligence systems, data centres and high-performance computing.

Trump stated that he had been speaking to Nvidia’s board “directly and indirectly,” and that Huang “did nothing wrong.” He said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to “work hard.”

World.title: Bala Mohammed: Bauchi 2027 Budget to Prioritise Completion of Ongoing Projects
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi





Governor Bala Mohammed of Bauchi State has affirmed that his administration will make the completion of ongoing projects and outstanding gratuity payments major priorities in the 2027 proposed budget, assuring the exercise will be concluded before the end of the administration.

The governor who stated this on Monday at the opening of the State Executive Council meeting described it as a consolidation budget and his final fiscal plan as governor.

He explained the five-month budget would focus on completing existing projects, with minimal provisions for new initiatives.

Bala Mohammed said the state has consistently maintained about 60 per cent capital expenditure, prioritised health and education, and recorded impressive budget performance through prudent financial management.

He explained the budget, which covers only five months under his watch, would provide for the completion of existing projects, with limited additions to address critical needs, including road connectivity, improvements to schools and the state’s health system.

The governor said his administration had consistently maintained capital expenditure at nearly 60 per cent of the total budget, while sustaining substantial allocations to health and education over the last three years.

He expressed satisfaction with the state’s budget performance, noting it ranks among the leading states nationally in terms of implementation, a feat he attributed to the cooperation of the State Executive Council, revenue-generating agencies and the public service.

He also noted the administration had minimised borrowing, strengthened revenue generation and aligned its budget preparation with the Nigerian Governors Forum’s template for improved transparency and accountability.

The governor identified road connectivity across the three senatorial zones, completion of schools, expansion of healthcare facilities and payment of outstanding gratuities as key priorities in the proposed budget.

Governor Bala Mohammed also pledged increased investment in security through collaboration with security agencies and vigilante groups, urging public servants to remain focused on governance despite political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Barau Woos 2,000 Kano Clerics for Tinubu’s Re-election, Promises Motorcycles
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja





Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau, has intensified efforts to secure President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, rallying more than 2,000 Islamic clerics from the 13 local government areas of Kano North Senatorial District to mobilise support for the president and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates.

Barau, who met with the clerics in Kano yesterday, urged them to use their considerable influence within their communities to garner support for Tinubu, insisting that the president meant well for Kano State, the North-West geopolitical zone and the country.

He hinged his appeal on what he described as the administration’s development interventions in Kano and other parts of the North, including the establishment of federal institutions and the North-West Development Commission.

The Deputy Senate President also disclosed plans to distribute 390 motorcycles to Islamic clerics across the 13 local government areas of Kano North, alongside financial support of N50,000 for each beneficiary.

Speaking at the meeting, Barau acknowledged the contributions of religious leaders to peace, stability and development, attributing his political achievements, including his emergence as Deputy President of the Senate, partly to their prayers and support.

He said the gathering provided an opportunity to appreciate the clerics for their spiritual guidance and continued contributions to society.

He said, “This is a gathering of our fathers, our leaders, our sheikhs and our imams. You are our leaders. I warmly welcome you all to this gathering and sincerely appreciate your prayers and support.

“It is through your prayers and supplications, which Almighty Allah has accepted, that we have attained the positions we occupy today. Kano is one of the greatest states in Africa, and I believe the prayers of our religious leaders have contributed immensely to its greatness,” he said.

Highlighting the Tinubu administration’s interventions in Kano, Barau said he personally approached the president to secure approval for the conversion of the Federal Polytechnic, Kabo, into a university.

He added that the president also approved the conversion of the Federal College of Education, Kano, into a university.

World.title: Musa: We’ll Convert Brussels Engagement Outcomes into Support for Our Operations
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Linus Aleke in Abuja





Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa, has said the Ministry of Defence, under his leadership, would translate the diplomatic and technical engagements secured in Brussels into concrete operational support for troops of the Armed Forces of Nigeria across all theatres of operation.

The Minister, who returned to Abuja after an official engagement at the 2026 Schuman Security and Defence Forum in Brussels, Belgium, said troops would continue to adhere strictly to the principles of civilian protection, due process and international humanitarian law.

He described the engagements as a major milestone in advancing Nigeria’s counter-terrorism diplomacy and international defence partnerships.

Speaking on his arrival, the Minister noted that Nigeria’s participation in the high-level global forum, organised by the European External Action Service (EEAS), had yielded significant strategic dividends in line with the security priorities of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Musa identified the key strategic gains as strengthened EU–Nigeria counter-terrorism alignment, the advancement of emerging technology partnerships, global endorsement of Nigeria’s non-kinetic framework and reinforced regional security diplomacy.

According to a statement by the minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde Musa held bilateral consultations with African and European counterparts on the sidelines of the plenary sessions to strengthen joint security frameworks under the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) in the Lake Chad Basin, ECOWAS and the West Africa Police Information System (WAPIS).

He explained that Nigeria had secured broad international consensus and renewed commitments from European Union counterparts to deepen collaboration in intelligence sharing, counter-terrorism financing and border management.

Musa stressed that discussions with EU defence leaders and multilateral partners had opened new avenues for technical cooperation in counter-drone technologies, military artificial intelligence, digital forensics and satellite intelligence, while strengthening support for Nigeria’s indigenous defence innovation ecosystem.

World.title: 2027: Renew Tinubu’s Mandate, Support Hamzat, Sanwo-Olu Urges Lagos Electorate
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

• APC holds Lagos Central rally to drum up support for party candidates

Lagos State Governor, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has urged Nigerians to give President Bola Tinubu another mandate in 2027.

He also sought support for his deputy, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, in his quest to govern Lagos State.

The governor based his appeal on the current administration’s strong commitment to national development, demonstrated through landmark infrastructure projects and economic investments.

Sanwo-Olu made the appeal during the Lagos Central Senatorial APC Rally, held at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan, Lagos, where he highlighted the achievements of the Tinubu administration.

According to the governor, President Tinubu had made significant progress in transforming the country through investments in road construction, rail transportation, aviation and other critical sectors.

“The only way to show appreciation to the president is by coming out to vote massively for him and all APC candidates. That is the only way we can continue to enjoy the development he has started,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu also expressed confidence in the candidacy and capacity of Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat to move Lagos forward, calling on Lagosians to support his candidacy and allow him to build on the achievements of the present administration.

He said, “K.O.H. has served you well, and he will serve you even better. He will serve you with greater commitment and dedication. I urge you all to support him and give him the opportunity to continue the good work and build on the achievements already recorded.

“Let us come out in our numbers, mobilise our families, friends and neighbours, and ensure his overwhelming victory in the 2027 election.”

Hamzat, the APC governorship candidate, urged party faithful to intensify mobilisation for President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, declaring that no nation could make meaningful progress with a manifesto of grievances.

He called on party members and supporters to turn out in large numbers on January 16 to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the National Assembly elections, while urging them to extend the same support to him and all the House of Assembly candidates on February 6.

He said continued electoral support for the APC would enable Lagos State to sustain its development trajectory and consolidate the gains already recorded, rather than reverse the progress made.

The Senator representing Lagos Central Senatorial District, Senator Wasiu Eshilokun-Sanni, urged residents of the district to turn out in large numbers to vote for APC candidates, describing them as credible leaders with a strong commitment to infrastructure development and the overall progress of the country.

In his welcome address, the Chairman of the APC Lagos State Chapter, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, urged registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to enable them to participate in the forthcoming elections, stressing that the PVC remains the only instrument through which citizens can exercise their right to vote and elect their preferred candidates.

The Director-General of the PBAT/KOH Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, described Tinubu as a committed and steadfast member of the APC whose leadership and resilience exemplify the qualities of a true leader.

Obanikoro further described both Tinubu and Hamzat, as knowledgeable leaders with a strong interest in the development of the country, particularly in children’s education, which he identified as the bedrock of every developed society.

World.title: 2027: ActionAid Challenges INEC over Voter Register Errors, Result Transparency
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Michael Olugbode in Abuja





ActionAid Nigeria has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to account for errors in the voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general election.

It therefore demanded a state-by-state breakdown of complaints, corrections made and unresolved cases, as well as greater transparency in the collation and publication of election results.

The organisation said Nigerians deserved clear answers on how errors in the voters’ register would be addressed and how results recorded at polling units would be tracked through ward, local government and state collation stages to ensure that votes were not altered or lost in the process.

In a statement yesterday in Abuja, ActionAid Nigeria said INEC must explain how voters could inspect results at each stage of collation and identify discrepancies between polling-unit figures and results subsequently announced at higher levels.

The demand came amid concerns over the commission’s readiness to make collated results publicly accessible through its Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, reportedly said the commission had yet to build and test the system required to upload collated results to the portal, which currently displays polling-unit result sheets.

ActionAid said INEC must disclose where signed result sheets from subsequent collation stages would be published, how quickly they would be made available after announcement and what mechanisms citizens would have to report discrepancies.

“Nigerians should never have to beg to see how their votes were counted. They are entitled to an account of what happened to every vote,” the Country Director, Andrew Mamedu, said.

He said the availability of polling-unit results on IReV should be matched by public access to signed ward results to enable citizens verify whether figures from their polling units were accurately transferred during collation.

ActionAid also questioned INEC’s handling of discrepancies in the voters’ register, particularly following the commission’s acknowledgement of multiple registrations and reported removal of more than 1.6 million records.

World.title: Group: Opposition Deal Dead on Arrival, Atiku’s Name Must Be on Ballot in 2027 Poll
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

• Gombe offers presidential candidate appointment with one condition

Chuks Okocha in Abuja





Audu Aliyu, leader of supporters of the presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has ruled out his stepping down for either Peter Obi of the NDC or Seyi Makinde of the APM.

Addressing a press conference yesterday, the supporters group insisted that it was either his name on the January 16 presidential ballot or nothing.

“It is contesting to win or nothing. This is our mandate. He is contesting to win and not to step down for anyone,’’ Aliyu said clearly.

Reading the text of the press conference, Audu Aliyu said, “We are here for a short purpose. Over the past few days, a story has been circulated that Alhaji Atiku Abubakar has stepped down from the 2027 presidential race. It is false. It was invented, and it has been pushed in the name of people who have no standing to speak for him.

“Alhaji Atiku Abubakar has not withdrawn. He has said so plainly, through his Director of Strategic Communication, in words we gladly repeat: he is in this race to win, and he is stepping down for no one.

“On the groups behind the claim. The body that presented itself as “supporters” of our candidate is unknown to this Directorate. It is not in our register and not part of the accredited support-group family of the ADC.

“Genuine support is demonstrated through registration, organisation and work in the wards. It is not established by a gathering of friends and relatives under a borrowed name.

“We therefore invite them, as we have before, to name their member groups and present their certificates of registration with the Directorate of Support Groups. Until they do, the claim has no foundation.”

Meanwhile, the factional National Chairman of the ADC, Nafiu Bala Gombe, has said he was willing to appoint Atiku as Chairman of the party’s Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 general election if he formally registers as a member of the party.

Gombe made the offer amid the leadership crisis rocking the ADC, following a recent Federal High Court judgment, which removed the David Mark-led National Working Committee and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s emergence as the party’s presidential candidate.

The David Mark-led leadership has since challenged the ruling at a higher court but has continued its political and campaign activities ahead of the 2027 elections.

Speaking at an engagement with his faction’s presidential, governorship and National Assembly candidates in Kaduna, Gombe insisted that Atiku and other members of the David Mark-led faction had not completed the party’s formal registration process.

The meeting, organised to harmonise campaign plans and strengthen the party’s electoral strategy, was attended by its presidential candidate, Prof. Chris Uba, Vice Presidential candidate, Dr. Shamsuddeen Modibbo Barkindo, as well as governorship and National Assembly candidates from different parts of the country.

Gombe urged Atiku to resolve the membership issue by returning to his ward to complete his registration.

“Former vice president Alhaji Atiku Abubakar should sheathe his sword and return to his ward to properly register as a bona fide member of the ADC,” he said.

World.title: Will Zimbabwean star Jonah Fabisch finally make his PSL debut this week?
World.content:
Zimbabwe's Jonah Fabisch closes in on Golden Arrows debut after injury. Image: Facebook/263 Football

Zimbabwe international Jonah Fabisch could finally make his long-awaited South African Premier Soccer League (PSL) debut when Golden Arrows face Orlando Pirates on Tuesday evening.

Golden Arrows coach Mandla Ncikazi is hopeful that the 25-year-old midfielder will be available for the Betway Premiership encounter after missing the opening months of the season through injury.

According to SuperSport, Fabisch is closing in on his first appearance for Abafana Bes’thende, having endured a frustrating start to his career in South Africa.



The midfielder joined Golden Arrows ahead of the 2026/27 campaign after leaving German side FC Erzgebirge Aue.

However, his introduction to South African football was interrupted by an injury sustained during pre-season training.

The setback initially appeared minor, with Fabisch expected to spend only a few weeks on the sidelines. However, his recovery took longer than anticipated, leaving him without a competitive appearance for the Durban-based club.

Fabisch’s injury affected Warriors involvement

Fabisch’s prolonged absence also affected his involvement with the Zimbabwe national team.

The midfielder was included in Warriors coach Ramon Catala’s squad for the back-to-back 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Equatorial Guinea in November.

However, Golden Arrows subsequently communicated that the player was unavailable for national duty because of his injury. Catala replaced him with Highlanders midfielder Mongameli Tshuma.



Fabisch’s absence was another setback for the Warriors, who were looking to strengthen their midfield options during the qualifying campaign.

Golden Arrows face Orlando Pirates

Golden Arrows will travel to Orlando Amstel Arena to face Pirates on Tuesday, 24 November, with kick-off scheduled for 17:30.

Ncikazi will be hoping to have Fabisch available as his side looks to improve its recent run of results.

Abafana Bes’thende have struggled to find consistency, while Pirates enter the encounter after extending their winning run to seven matches across all competitions with a 2-0 victory over Stellenbosch.

The fixture could therefore provide Fabisch with an opportunity to make his first competitive appearance for his new club against one of South Africa’s biggest teams.

World.title: New Zealand Rugby gives ‘full’ backing to Dave Rennie
World.content:
Dave Rennie has now lost five of his 12 Tests as New Zealand coach following a 37-12 Nations Championship defeat by England at Twickenham. Image: Adrian Dennis / AFP

New Zealand Rugby has given its “full support” to All Blacks coach Dave Rennie after damaging back-to-back defeats including a first loss to Wales in 73 years.

With the World Cup less than a year away, the All Blacks suffered a record 37-12 defeat by England at Twickenham on Saturday.

That followed a stunning 35-28 Nations Championship loss to Wales in Cardiff.



READ | Not even Rassie Erasmus can save these All Blacks!

Dampen speculation

With the All Blacks and England facing off again this weekend, NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster moved to dampen any speculation about Dave Rennie’s future.

“I’ve told Dave that and I’m happy to state that publicly that Dave has our full support,” Lancaster told Radio New Zealand.

“We’re confident that we have the right person coaching this team, no question in our minds.”

Speaking on Monday, Lancaster added: “There’s clear leadership. The team are behind Dave but they know what they have to achieve.

“The last two weeks’ performance is really disappointing and we need to understand how that’s come to pass, but no question over Dave being the right person to lead the team.”



Took full responsibility

Speaking after the defeat at Twickenham, which was England’s biggest margin of victory over New Zealand, Dave Rennie said he took full responsibility.

The All Blacks have lost five of their 12 Tests under Rennie, equalling their worst run in the professional era.

“As a coach you’re responsible for the results,” Rennie, who was appointed in March, told reporters.

“I’m not going to hide that we weren’t good enough and I’m a part of that. We were miles off and this is not where we want to be.”

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Lewis Pugh swims in Strait of Hormuz (video)
World.content:
Lewis Pugh, who swam in waters in the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the "devastating environmental consequences of war", has called for the waterway to be reopened. Image: AFP

A British endurance swimmer who swam in waters in the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the “devastating environmental consequences of war” on Saturday called for the waterway to be reopened and the pollution in it to be cleaned up.

“Oil tankers, gas carriers and other merchant ships are being attacked, day after day. The environmental consequences of this war will last for generations,” Lewis Pugh wrote in a post on his website.

Oil tanker struck

Pugh, 56 and the UN Environment Programme’s “patron of the oceans”, swam in parts of the strait close to Oman’s coastline over three days in the past week to publicise his message.

On Monday, when he was just half an hour in the water, an oil tanker was struck a few kilometres away. Other attacks occurred during his swims that left vessels ablaze.

He completed a total 15km swim, starting from the Musandam Peninsula and rounding part of the Cape of Hormuz, both located in Oman.



Iran sits on the other side of the strait, which is 39km across at its shortest span.

Conflict

Iran began blockading the waterway and targeting ships in the area following US and Israeli strikes that sparked the conflict in February.

“The Strait of Hormuz is far more than a vital shipping route. It is one of the most beautiful places I have ever visited,” Pugh said.



“Dolphins, sea turtles and dugongs live in these waters. It is one of the great natural wonders of the world,” he said.

Pugh has previously undertaken high-profile swims in Antarctica, the North Pole and the Red Sea to advocate for rivers clean enough to swim and fish in safely.

“My message is simple: Stop the fighting, Open the Strait, Clean up the pollution,” he added.

World.title: What did Pastor Chris tell Uebert Angel days before his arrest?
World.content:
A warning by Nigerian televangelist Pastor Chris Oyakhilome telling people to “leave him alone” has once again resurfaced following the arrest of Zimbabwean preacher Uebert Angel.

Oyakhilome made the remarks while addressing Angel during a church gathering in Nigeria in the week before his arrest.

A recording of the message was circulating publicly by 15 November, according to reports.



The Christ Embassy founder said he had been praying for Angel when he received what he described as a message from God.

“I was praying for you a few days ago. While I was praying for you, the Spirit of God said to me, tell him, anyone who goes after him, I will kill him,” Oyakhilome said.

He then addressed those he believed were targeting the Zimbabwean preacher.



“God has spoken and said, don’t touch him. Leave him alone,” he said.

Oyakhilome repeated the warning, saying anyone who continued going after Angel risked consequences extending to their families and descendants. He also claimed Angel had been given spiritual authority to bring calm to Zimbabwe.

The remarks attracted renewed attention after the Zimbabwe Republic Police confirmed Angel’s arrest on Sunday, 22 November 2026.



Police said the Spirit Embassy founder had been arrested on allegations of indecent assault and sodomy.

The arrest reportedly took place at the Hippodrome in Harare, where his church holds services.

The police announcement did not provide details of the allegations or indicate that the arrest was connected to Angel’s public comments about politics.



Why Pastor Chris’s remarks are being revisited

Oyakhilome’s warning came amid criticism of Angel over his comments concerning the relationship between President Emmerson Mnangagwa and Vice-President Constantino Chiwenga.

Angel had defended Chiwenga against personal attacks during a church service in Harare, while insisting that his political allegiance remained with Mnangagwa.

His remarks drew criticism from former Norton legislator Temba Mliswa, who accused him of using the pulpit to engage in politics.



Following Angel’s arrest, Mliswa criticised Oyakhilome’s warning, describing the prophecy as “utter hogwash” and arguing that it should not be used to intimidate police or interfere with due process.

The resurfaced video has prompted discussion about the timing of the message, given that it preceded Angel’s arrest by about a week.

However, Oyakhilome’s remarks do not establish any connection to the police investigation, and the allegations against Angel have not been proven in court.

World.title: Good news for Capitec, Nedbank, and FNB customers shopping on Black Friday
World.content:
Some banking clients will be getting the best deals. Image: Pexels

By now, most South Africans know most Black Friday deals aren’t worth writing home about.

But Capitec, Nedbank, and FNB customers will be smiling all the way to the bank.

The best Black Friday deals for Capitec, Nedbank, and FNB customers

World.title: Helen Zille mocks Herman Mashaba with Springbok meme
World.content:
DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille took a swipe at ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba by sharing a satirical Springbok meme on social media. Image: X/Helen Zille

DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille has brought the Springboks into her political spat with ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba amid ongoing coalition negotiations in Johannesburg.

Taking to X on Monday, 23 November, Zille shared a satirical graphic depicting Mashaba as the newly appointed Springbok coach ahead of a clash against France.

“This sums it up well. I wonder who is ‘arrogant’,” Zille wrote.



ZILLE TAKES SWIPE AT MASHABA

The satirical graphic takes aim at Mashaba’s position in coalition negotiations, jokingly suggesting that he appointed himself Springbok coach after receiving 5% of the votes.

It further suggests that Mashaba would only agree to play France if the French dropped star winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey in exchange for the Springboks dropping Manie Libbok.

The graphic mimics an SABC News broadcast but is not a genuine news report.



This sums it up well. I wonder who is "arrogant". pic.twitter.com/VqqIvexVVy — Helen Zille (@helenzille) November 23, 2026

Zille’s reference to arrogance follows tensions between the DA and ActionSA over the leadership of Johannesburg.

ACTIONSA REFUSES TO BACK ZILLE

ActionSA has previously accused Zille of arrogance and remains opposed to her bid for Johannesburg’s mayoral chain.



The party also proposed that both Zille and Mashaba withdraw their mayoral candidacies to allow alternative candidates to contest the position.

Mashaba previously served as Johannesburg mayor under the DA between 2016 and 2019 before resigning from the party. He subsequently founded ActionSA in 2020.

Both Zille and Mashaba officially took their oaths as Johannesburg councillors on Monday.



Zille’s latest jab at Mashaba comes just weeks after she took aim at EFF leader Julius Malema.

World.title: RIP | Heart surgeon Chris Barnard’s daughter dies aged 76
World.content:
Dr Christiaan Barnard pictured with his daughter, Deirdre Barnard-Visser (left). The eldest daughter of the world-renowned heart surgeon has died at the age of 76. Images: Heart of Cape Town Museum and X

South Africans are mourning the death of Deirdre Barnard-Visser, the eldest daughter of pioneering heart surgeon Dr Christiaan Barnard, following a 12-year battle with Parkinson’s disease.

She died on Saturday, 21 November, at the age of 76.

The Heart of Cape Town Museum announced her death on Facebook, paying tribute to her accomplishments as an author and champion water-skier.



TRIBUTES POUR IN FOR CHRISTIAAN BARNARD’S DAUGHTER

“She lived a life of her own achievements, passions and stories, leaving behind a legacy that will not be forgotten,” the museum said.

According to the Heart of Cape Town Museum, Barnard coached his daughter throughout her childhood, spending hours with her perfecting her water-skiing techniques.

At just 12 years old, she became a champion water-skier.



However, their relationship changed when her father shot to international fame after performing the world’s first successful human-to-human heart transplant at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town on 3 December 1967.

Despite the demands of his newfound fame, Barnard-Visser continued to turn to her father for support.

LIFE AS THE DAUGHTER OF A WORLD-FAMOUS SURGEON

Barnard-Visser later penned a book, Fat, Fame and Life with Father, in which she recounted her experiences growing up as the daughter of an international celebrity.



Doctors diagnosed her with Parkinson’s disease in 2014, a diagnosis she later spoke publicly about in an interview with Sarie magazine.

News of her death comes less than two weeks before the 59th anniversary of her father’s historic heart transplant, which put South Africa on the world medical map.

Barnard-Visser leaves behind her husband, Kobus Visser, two children and two grandchildren, according to the museum’s biographical information.

World.title: Bongi Mbonambi called up to Springbok squad
World.content:
DUBLIN - The Springboks have turned to a familiar face, with veteran hooker Bongi Mbonambi called into the squad ahead of their Nations Championship final against France.

The double Rugby World Cup winner is expected to join the team in London on Tuesday as the world champions deal with injury setbacks.

Mbonambi's inclusion comes after lock Ruan Nortje and loosehead prop Ntuthuko Mchunu were ruled out through injury, with both players returning to South Africa.

The 35-year-old, who boasts 82 Test caps, has not featured in a Test match since last year. However, his experience and proven track record could prove valuable as the Springboks prepare for the crucial encounter.

Despite joining the squad, Mbonambi has not been included in the matchday 23 for the final against France.

World.title: Buffalo City up for grabs as ANC faces historic coalition challenge
World.content:
EAST LONDON - Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality is bracing for a crucial political showdown on Tuesday as its 100-member council prepares to elect new leadership.

For the first time since the dawn of democracy, the African National Congress (ANC) finds itself without an outright majority in the metro.

The party secured just 42 of the 100 council seats, leaving it short of the numbers needed to govern alone and forcing it to seek coalition partners to retain control.

READ | eThekwini pushes ahead with inaugural sitting despite Cogta directive

Meanwhile, opposition parties are exploring possible alliances in a bid to challenge the ANC’s grip on the municipality.

World.title: California braces for triple flooding threat of huge tides, El Nino, warm oceans
World.content:
CALIFORNIA - Exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather were threatening the California coast with possibly extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year.

The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit particularly hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, with forecasters warning that cascading seawater could deluge low-lying areas including the city's airport.

US authorities were meanwhile urging residents to reconsider travel plans for the Thanksgiving holiday.

San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie warned the situation was "extremely serious," and asked people to limit unnecessary travel.

The high tides were long-predicted: So-called king tides occur every year due to the gravitational pull and alignments of the Earth, Moon and Sun.

They will occur this week and again for periods in December and January.

This time around, the powerful tides, in San Francisco, they are predicted to approach or even exceed the more than 40-year-old record of 8.66 feet (2.6 meters), are arriving on top of already record-warm ocean waters.

The ocean is hotter than usual, and thus increasing in volume, both due to human-caused climate change and this year's exceptionally strong El Nino weather pattern.

World.title: The art of the steal: John Turturro on learning to pickpocket
World.content:
NEW YORK - Truly skillful pickpockets, as American actor John Turturro explains, are magicians.

He should know: he learned the art from a professional as he prepared for his starring role in "The Only Living Pickpocket in New York," a moving film about an aging criminal struggling to make his way in America's largest city.

"He worked with me and showed me how... if someone's on a pole in the subway, you can't touch their skin," he said of his work with illusionist Apollo Robbins, known as "The Gentleman Thief."

"You approach so their space doesn't feel invaded," he told AFP.

"You're coming in from the side, so your hand is just touching it like this," he said, demonstrating on his own wristwatch an imperceptible movement of the fastener.

With the strap unhooked, the thief goes in for his bounty, touching his mark for the only time.

"If you bump into them for a second, it's gone. The watch is gone."

After being tutored on the skill, Turturro had lots of dry runs with colleagues on set.
