World.title: Sin permiso para tutear
World.content:
“¿Quieres ser portavoz del PSOE?”, le preguntó Ester Muñoz a Rufián. “Yo de lo que no tengo ni puñetera gana es de que tú seas ministra”

Exposición didáctica de ideas, conjeturas o hipótesis, a partir de unos hechos de actualidad comprobados —no necesariamente del día— que se reflejan en el propio texto. Excluye los juicios de valor y se aproxima más al género de opinión, pero se diferencia de él en que no juzga ni pronostica, sino que sólo formula hipótesis, ofrece explicaciones argumentadas y pone en relación datos dispersos

Hubo un momento de este difícil pero bien llevado debate a ocho en el que Maribel Vaquero, portavoz del PNV, cortó las discusiones cruzadas para comentar que había que aumentar la potencia eléctrica en el País Vasco; se puso incluso, la desaprensiva, a dar algunos datos, y luego añadió que hacían falta consensos y no monólogos enfrentados como se estaba haciendo allí. Fue simpático porque pareció una marciana: por el tono de sosiego, la concreción de su medida y la cara con la que la miraron todos en plan “esta ahora de qué va”.

Repitió con tristeza cuando acababa el debate que aquello eran monólogos, y acto seguido reivindicó las medallas que ganó la selección vasca en pelota vasca, y hasta enseñó una. El moderador, Xabier Fortes, preguntó por ella con tanto interés que casi se levanta para tocarla.

Fue divertido por momentos. Es complicado que un debate así sea interesante pero si están Ester Muñoz (PP) o Gabriel Rufián (ERC) siempre se deja algún espectáculo en pantalla.

Miriam Nogueras, de Junts, pasó la noche diciendo “el dinero de los catalanes para Cataluña”, quizá era por una apuesta. Es una mujer que sonríe muchísimo. Tiene una sonrisa, es difícil tenerla en la vida, y la exhibe diga lo que diga. Además Puigdemont ahora es el héroe moral, la autoridad intelectual que PP y Vox reclamaban, y cada sonrisa enorme de Nogueras lo recordaba con ternura. “Prometimos la amnistía y la conseguimos”, dijo.

Pepa Millán (Vox) parecía estar presentando el telediario. Miraba la cámara de tal modo que quizá estuviese leyendo el teleprompter. Tiene rasgos de presentadora de las noticias Millán, quizá sea la llave moderadora con la que quiere entrar Vox entre lanzallamas a la televisión pública. “Ustedes han dado asco estos cuatro años”, le soltó Emilio Delgado (Frente Amplio). No movió una pestaña Millán, que se puso a fingir que leía, una táctica viejísima que falla poco. Millán había relacionado al PSOE con los amigos de los terroristas o algo parecido; a Rufián, señalando a Patxi López (PSOE) que “ha portado féretros de compañeros suyos”, se le “llevaban los demonios”: “no tiene vergüenza”. Delgado también saltó a por ese hueso, que era muy apetecible: “Yo no he visto a los de Bildu llamando a apalizar inmigrantes ni manifestándose con neonazis en centros de menores”, le dijo en referencia a las acciones de Vox.

Cada portavoz tenía un consumo limitado de tiempo. Cada vez que hablaba, se ponía en marcha, así fuese un gruñido. Cuando los bloques terminaban, los candidatos gestionaban segundos, así que se producían momentos excitantes como el que acreditó el moderador, Xabier Fortes, cuando hizo ver a Ester Muñoz el número de segundos que le quedaban: “Los quiere consumir ahora o picotear en lo que falta”.

Cuando un candidato acababa su tiempo, Fortes decía “correcto”, “correcto”, y claro, el candidato se veía apoyado por el árbitro y seguía tirando carrete.

Las alusiones a ETA de PP y Vox en la espalda de Oskar Matute (EH Bildu) provocaron que reaccionase dirigiéndose a las víctimas del terrorismo: “Verdad, justicia y reparación”. Ester Muñoz fue la agitadora del debate, atrayendo a Rufián, López y Delgado (mitinero, suelto, con ese punto populista que hace falta en los debates y que Muñoz y Rufián también tienen). Como es mujer y los otros tres hombres, Ester Muñoz decidió que discutir con ella era “machismo” a veces y otras no, pero “si yo fuera de izquierdas, lo diría”.

Patxi López no es tan impetuoso como los candidatos más jóvenes pero en la refriega de izquierda/derecha que encendió Pepa Millán (“qué fácil es ser de izquierdas”) levantó al votante —el suyo— del sofá: “Ser de izquierdas es mucho más difícil que ser de derechas. Incluso en otros tiempos se nos encarcelaba, perseguía o fusilaba, esos tiempos que añoran los que ustedes traen de la mano”.

“¿Quieres ser portavoz del PSOE?”, le preguntó Ester Muñoz a Rufián. “Yo de lo que no tengo ni puñetera gana es de que tú seas ministra”.

Antes, mucho antes, cuando empezaba el debate, Emilio Delgado se lanzó a embestir a Pepa Millán. “Yo no le he dado permiso para que me tutee”, dijo ella. “Yo no necesito tu permiso para hacer nada”, respondió él.

“Es verdad que hay gente que lo está pasando mal”, dijo Patxi López en algún momento para defenderse de Rufián, que le echó en cara ser la cuarta economía de Europa y que hubiese gente sin poder comer carne fresca.

Rufián, en su minuto de oro, dijo: “Yo le quiero bien a todas las izquierdas”, aunque no supo calcular, ni siquiera él, cuántas son.

World.title: Mentiras, inexactitudes y medias verdades en el debate entre los ocho portavoces
World.content:
Con los tiempos muy limitados en cada uno de los bloques y la necesidad de emplear buena parte de su tiempo en responder los reproches cruzados, los candidatos han tenido poco tiempo para el despliegue de datos habituales en los cara a cara o en los debates entre cuatro aspirantes. De ahí que, en esta ocasión, el balance de cifras falsas o descontextualizadas sea menor que en otras citas.

Las estadísticas han aflorado sobre todo en los apartados de vivienda y economía. Y ha arrancado con el rifirrafe sobre pensiones, donde el PP empezó la precampaña del 29-N con el patinazo de su portavoz Ester Muñoz, que este lunes ha sido la representante de los populares en el debate a ocho de TVE. Ante los ataques de sus oponentes, Muñoz negó que dijera que quería “tocar” esas prestaciones –aunque sí pidió cambiarlo al considerar que iba a “colapsar”— y se enzarzó en una discusión con el resto de portavoces sobre si el PP en su día las congeló o no.

La candidata del PNV, Maribel Vaquero, le recordó que fue su partido quien le obligó a “revalorizar las pensiones”. Muñoz puntualizó que no se estaban revalorizando de acuerdo al IPC, pero tampoco congelando. “Os tuvimos que forzar”, le insistió Vaquero. En realidad, esas prestaciones no quedaron congeladas, pero casi: solo subieron un 0,25% en 2017. Y ese año sí hubo inflación, de un 2% según el Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), por lo que los pensionistas perdieron poder adquisitivo. En cambio, en los tres años anteriores, se había subido ese mismo 0,25% en un entorno deflacionista.

Sin embargo, fue la portavoz de Vox, Pepa Millán, la que colocó más mensajes por lo menos inexactos. “Este Gobierno ha metido a más de seis millones de personas en menos de cinco años en España”, señaló la diputada para culpar a la inmigración de la crisis de vivienda. Se trata de un dato que viene manejando este partido desde el inicio de la campaña, pero no es cierto. En estos cinco años, según el INE, han entrado 2,1 millones de extranjeros. Es decir, un tercio de los que afirma Vox que han llegado. También afirmó que la inmigración devalúa los salarios, cuando estudios del Banco de España o del think tank Fedea desmienten o minimizan ese efecto.

Más tarde, Millán también criticó las subidas del salario mínimo interprofesional (SMI). “Con las sucesivas reformas del salario mínimo, tal y como las ha hecho este Gobierno, hemos perdido 150.000 puestos de trabajo”, sostuvo. La portavoz de Vox saca el dato de un análisis elaborado por la Autoridad Fiscal (Airef), pero descontextualizándolo. En un análisis publicado en septiembre de 2025, el organismo concluyó que las subidas del SMI no destruyeron empleos, pero sí frenaron la creación de puestos de trabajo adicionales. La Airef calculó, en concreto, el impacto de la subida del SMI de 2019, cuando se produjo la más elevada (22%), que habría impedido que se crearan entre 40.000 y 65.000 nuevos puestos, y la de 2023, que tuvo un impacto mayor, de entre 55.000 a 85.000 afiliados, pese a ser menor (8%) debido al mayor número de perceptores.

El cabeza de lista del Frente Amplio por Madrid, Emilio Delgado; y la portavoz de Vox en el Congreso, Pepa Millán, antes del debate. Eduardo Parra - Europa Press (Europa Press)

Sin embargo, el organismo aclaró que el cálculo solo estimaba “efectos directos por la afiliación”, y que no consideraba otros impactos indirectos, como el hecho de que la mejora salarial vinculada a la subida del SMI hubiera podido impulsar la demanda, elevando el consumo o generando cambios de la distribución salarial: “En conjunto, el aumento de los salarios tiene una mayor relevancia que la caída inicial del empleo, lo que hace que el impacto en la renta disponible de los hogares sea positivo, impulsando el consumo y por tanto la actividad”. Es más, la entidad publicó su análisis en el marco de los documentos técnicos de su opinión sobre la sostenibilidad de las Administraciones públicas a largo plazo, y concluyó que “el conjunto de medidas simuladas (SMI y medidas de reforma laboral) han tenido un impacto limitado, aunque ligeramente positivo, sobre la actividad económica, el empleo y las cotizaciones sociales en términos de PIB”.

La última afirmación al menos descontextualizada la hizo Ester Muñoz, cuando afirmó: “Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha sido presidente de la Xunta de Galicia durante 15 años. Y ninguno de sus consejeros jamás ha sido imputado”. La Sala de lo Civil y Penal del Tribunal Superior de Xustiza de Galicia imputó en 2010 a Agustín Hernández, entonces consejero de Medio Ambiente de Núñez Feijóo. El tribunal apreció indicios de criminalidad tras una denuncia del PSOE por el fraude en una certificación de una obra, aunque finalmente se acordó el sobreseimiento libre del caso y su archivo.

Sin embargo, varios altos cargos de la Xunta y del PP gallego liderados por Feijóo sí han sido condenados en 2017 por corrupción en el llamado caso Campeón, sobre un fraude de subvenciones y tráfico de influencias para favorecer a la farmacéutica Nupel: el diputado autonómico Pablo Cobián; y dos miembros de la cúpula del Igape (Instituto Galego de Promoción Económica). Más recientemente, en 2025, la Audiencia Nacional ha condenado a 19 años y medio de prisión a José Norberto Uzal, quien fuera director general de Administración Local de la Consellería de Presidencia de la Xunta de Galicia que encabezó Feijóo, por participar en un macrofraude del sector de los hidrocarburos años después de dejar su cargo y pasarse al sector privado.

World.title: Los momentos más tensos del debate electoral de portavoces parlamentarios
World.content:
Los momentos más tensos del debate electoral de portavoces parlamentarios

Los represenantes de los principales partidos políticos en el Congreso han cruzado acusaciones y reporches relacionadas con la vivienda, la corrupción o la inmigración, entre otro temas

World.title: Muñoz: “¿Qué quiere, ser el portavoz del PSOE?”. Rufián: “De lo que no tengo ni puñetera gana es de que usted sea ministra”
World.content:
La portavoz del PP en el Congreso, Ester Muñoz; el portavoz de ERC en el Congreso y cabeza de lista por Barcelona a las elecciones, Gabriel Rufián; el portavoz del PSOE en el Congreso, Patxi López; y la portavoz de Junts Per Catalunya en el Congreso, Miriam Nogueras; durante el debate electoral organizado por RTVE de cara a las elecciones generales del 29N.

El debate a ocho este lunes en RTVE puso de manifiesto que continúa en vigor el pacto de no agresión entre el PP y Vox y que las críticas de los últimos días de Santiago Abascal a Alberto Núñez Feijóo por sus llamamientos al “voto útil” fueron poco más que pellizcos de monja. La portavoz de los populares, Ester Muñoz, no mencionó al partido de extrema derecha, que según la mayoría de encuestas necesitaría para poder gobernar, y la representante de Vox, Pepa Millán, solo lo hizo una vez, para criticar en bloque a todos los que habían apoyado el acuerdo comercial de Mercosur. Antes de entrar al plató, ambas portavoces permanecieron juntas mientras el resto charlaba en ambiente distendido.

Muñoz se refirió en 29 ocasiones al Gobierno y al PSOE, añadiendo a menudo la coletilla “y sus cómplices” para señalar al resto de portavoces, salvo la de Vox. También aludió 13 veces a ERC y a su representante, Gabriel Rufián, al que definió como “un braveheart de Temu”, y con el que se enfrascó a lo largo del debate en sucesivos rifirrafes. Cuando Muñoz volvió a tergiversar las palabras sobre pensiones del vicepresidente Carlos Cuerpo —“¿Y este era el listo del Gobierno?“, preguntó—, el portavoz de ERC le replicó: “Más listo que ustedes sí que es”. Cuando la representante del PP recordó el escándalo de las joyas en la caja fuerte del despacho del expresidente José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, Rufián contestó que seguramente José María Aznar escondía mucho más y la discusión escaló:

—¿Qué quiere? ¿Ser el portavoz del PSOE?

―De lo que no tengo ni puñetera gana es de que usted sea ministra.

Rufián también defendió a los socialistas cuando la portavoz del PP acusó al PSOE de haber cedido ante ETA, para recordarle que el socialista que tenía al lado, Patxi López, había portado a hombros, al igual que políticos del PP, féretros de asesinados por la banda; cuando la dirigente popular criticó la gestión ferroviaria, el portavoz de ERC aseguró que “la falta de inversión había empezado con el PP” y cuando Muñoz se refirió al Gobierno como una pandilla de “jetas”, Rufián replicó: “Tiene bemoles que hablen de jetas los que van de la mano de Abascal”. La postura del candidato de ERC, que redujo prácticamente sus reproches al Gobierno a su política en materia de vivienda y a la detención de varios jóvenes durante la huelga del pasado 11 de noviembre, contrastó en ese sentido con la que mantiene en los mítines de campaña con la candidata de Podemos, Irene Montero.

También parecía haber otro pacto tácito de no agresión entre el PSOE y el Frente Amplio, el más perjudicado por la concentración de voto estratégico o útil que señalan las encuestas. López no aludió en ninguna ocasión durante el debate a la fuerza política a su izquierda. Emilio Delgado, cabeza de lista por el Frente Amplio por Madrid, sí se refirió en una ocasión a los socialistas, para sugerir, con ironía, que quizá, al final del debate, sus propuestas en materia de vivienda terminarían siendo las del PSOE, ya que la formación se ha quejado de que los socialistas les han “copiado” varias iniciativas de su programa electoral.

López dedicó el grueso de sus intervenciones a criticar al PP (21 alusiones) y a Vox (10 veces). Delgado aludió a los populares en 17 ocasiones y a Vox en otras 16. Por su parte, Rufián interpeló 14 veces a los populares y se refirió a otras 19 al partido de extrema derecha. El portavoz de ERC y el del Frente Amplio tuvieron algún roce en el debate sobre la vivienda. Después del PP y Vox, Rufián centró sus críticas en la portavoz de Junts (siete alusiones), Miriam Nogueras, quien, a su vez, acusó al candidato de ERC de “decir que sí a todo lo que dice el PSOE”.

Fuera el bloque temático que fuera, Nogueras inició o concluyó sus intervenciones reclamando “el dinero de los catalanes”, y fuera el bloque temático que fuera, la portavoz de Vox, Pepa Millán, respondió acusando a los inmigrantes de todos los problemas del país.

El menos confrontativo fue el PNV, cuya portavoz, Maribel Vaquero, se centró en hablar “del grupo vasco”, salvo por cuatro alusiones al PP y tres al partido de Abascal, a quienes les anunció un cordón sanitario desde sus siglas: “El PNV con Vox, no, nada, nunca”. La formación ultra ha llegado a pedir en el pasado su ilegalización.

Millán se negó a debatir con el portavoz de EH Bildu, Óskar Matute, al que relacionó con la voladura de “casas cuartel”. Matute le replicó: “Quiero decir a las víctimas que toda nuestra solidaridad. Verdad, justicia y reparación. Entendemos y sentimos muchísimo el dolor que hayan tenido que recibir en sus vidas. Por nosotros no va a ser que nunca más vuelva a suceder nada más por el estilo. Pero queremos decir una cosa más y utilizando palabras de una víctima de ETA: ‘¡Qué triste tiene que ser tener a ETA siempre en la boca! ¿No hay nada en su programa electoral que merezca la pena?”.

Los portavoces se acusaron unos a otros de ser los responsables del clima de crispación en la política y en la ciudadanía, salvo la de Vox, que se limitó a decir que “el clima que preocupa a los españoles es el de su calle”, llevando, una vez más, el debate a la inmigración y “los barrios irreconocibles”. Muñoz pidió a López que condenara las palabras de la ministra Diana Morant, quien, refiriéndose al cara a cara entre Pedro Sánchez y Feijóo, aseguró que a muchos les hubiera gustado que el líder socialista le hubiera dado cuatro “galtades” [bofetedas en valenciano] al candidato del PP. El portavoz socialista replicó que alguno del PP había pasado directamente de las palabras a las bofetadas y Delgado preguntó a Muñoz si ya no les gustaba la fruta, refiriéndose al mensaje ya nada críptico con el que los populares llaman “hijo de puta” al presidente del Gobierno.

World.title: El trascendental voto de las mujeres, que superan en 1,2 millones a los hombres en el censo y son mayoría entre los indecisos
World.content:
En el censo electoral de residentes en España para el próximo domingo hay 1,2 millones más de mujeres que de hombres. Como el resto del año, no deben ser tratadas como un colectivo compacto: están llamadas a las urnas estudiantes, monjas, urbanitas, trabajadoras del campo y, como recuerda la socióloga Cristina Monge, “cualquier parecido entre una señora mayor de un pueblo del Pirineo y una chica joven que estudia en la Universidad de Barcelona es mera coincidencia”, pero sí se aprecian ciertas “pautas comunes” o tendencias mayoritarias. Por ejemplo, son más de izquierdas que de derechas. Y también les está costando más elegir papeleta para el próximo 29-N: el 11% de todo el electorado femenino no sabe a quién votar o no quiere decirlo, frente al 7% del masculino, según los datos de 40dB. Las que se declaran indecisas suponen el 7,8% del electorado, frente al 5,8% de los hombres. Y de acuerdo al recuerdo de voto de 2023, se aprecia que la indecisión es mucho mayor en la izquierda que en la derecha.

Belén Barreiro, expresidenta del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas y actual directora de 40dB.‚ la casa que hace las encuestas para este diario, explica: “Las mujeres tienen una propensión a votar a opciones de izquierdas, pero no ha sido así siempre. En décadas pasadas, cuando los índices de religiosidad eran mayores, votaban más hacia la derecha. Y también han sido más propensas históricamente a la indecisión, es decir, a responder ‘no lo sé’ cuando se les pregunta a quién van a votar”. Esto, añade, Monge, se aprecia también en la escala de autoubicación ideológica, donde las mujeres se sitúan, mayoritariamente, más a la izquierda que los hombres. Los datos de 40dB. señalan que la estimación de voto al PSOE de las mujeres es 3,6 puntos más alta que al PP.

Barreiro y Monge señalan otra clave, la de las preocupaciones, que inclina el voto de las mujeres mayoritariamente a partidos socialdemócratas, y es que, al igual que ocurre entre clases bajas o población de origen migrante, se sienten más vulnerables y les preocupa en mayor medida todo lo que tiene que ver con los servicios públicos, los cuidados, el estado del bienestar.

Estrategias de campaña

Los partidos tienen tres objetivos en una campaña electoral: movilizar a su electorado, desmovilizar al del rival y tratar de pescar votos en el caladero del contrincante. Las estrategias electorales han dejado ejemplos de esas maniobras en cada formación política en lo que afecta al voto femenino. Cuando Pedro Sánchez sale al mitin con una camiseta en la que se lee “la fuerza de las mujeres” y advierte de la “involución” en derechos como el aborto que supondría un gobierno de PP y Vox está tratando de asegurarse de que las que escogieron su papeleta en el pasado no se queden en casa el 29-N. Cuando Alberto Núñez Feijóo repite en múltiples ocasiones en el debate cara a cara la palabra “prostitutas” para recordar los escándalos en torno al exministro socialista José Luis Ábalos está tratando de conseguir lo contrario: que esas mujeres que votaron por el PSOE opten ahora por la abstención. Y cuando Vox habla de “protegerlas” tras las reducciones de pena provocadas por la ley del solo sí es sí está intentando robar a sus rivales el voto que más se le resiste: aunque ha ido recortando diferencias, su estimación de voto entre los hombres está dos puntos por encima que la de las mujeres y esa brecha aumenta considerablemente entre los más jóvenes.

Barreiro recuerda que los escándalos sobre el consumo de prostitución por parte de miembros del PSOE tuvieron mayor impacto sobre su electorado femenino que la corrupción en sí. “Hace unos meses la intención de voto a los socialistas cayó de forma importante y la caída tenía que ver con eso, con la pérdida de apoyos entre las mujeres”.

Las diferentes reacciones a los casos de acoso denunciados en los distintos partidos también alude al peso del electorado femenino en cada sigla. Las dirigentes del PP optaron mayoritariamente por el silencio cuando este periódico reveló, el pasado febrero, que una compañera suya, concejal en el Ayuntamiento de Móstoles, había denunciado por acoso al alcalde de la localidad, Manuel Bautista, y que la dirección había intentado disuadirla de seguir adelante con su denuncia —el regidor está actualmente imputado en un procedimiento judicial—. Posteriormente, desde la filas del PP madrileño intentaron desacreditar a la denunciante con informaciones falsas y, en los últimos días, la presidenta madrileña, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, participó en un mitin de campaña con el imputado, al que auguró un gran futuro en el partido. El PP tampoco alude en su programa electoral al “feminismo”, aunque sí incluye una premisa importada del discurso de Vox cuando se compromete a “reunir a la nación” para que “se deje de gobernar enfrentando a hombres con mujeres”. Y, sabiendo que son menos fuertes que su adversario en ese sector de la sociedad, los populares han centrado sus mensajes de campaña dirigidos al público femenino sobre todo, en tratar de desmovilizar a la votante de izquierdas y no tanto en convencer al electorado femenino con sus propias propuestas.

Por el mismo motivo, esto es, el peso que las mujeres tienen en su cómputo de apoyos, el socialista Francisco Salazar, estrecho colaborador del presidente Pedro Sánchez, tuvo que renunciar al cargo el día que iba a ser nombrado en la ejecutiva del PSOE, así como a su puesto de asesor en La Moncloa, porque Eldiario.es reveló que pesaban contra él denuncias por acoso sexual. El mismo medio informó de que cinco meses después el partido ni siquiera había llamado a las denunciantes. Esa revelación indignó a las responsables de Igualdad de federaciones socialistas, quienes mostraron su malestar, exigieron explicaciones e incluso reclamaron que se llevara el asunto a la Fiscalía. Sánchez terminó pidiendo perdón públicamente. También tuvo que hacerlo la exministra Pilar Alegría cuando se descubrió que había comido con Salazar después de conocerse esas denuncias por acoso, algo que reconoció posteriormente como “un error”. El PSOE no se puede permitir perder el voto femenino, uno de sus puntos fuertes, del mismo modo que el PP no se puede permitir generar inquietud entre los pensionistas, el perfil mayoritario entre sus apoyos.

El ‘factor Begoña’ y las entrevistas de nicho

La campaña electoral se ha caracterizado por la participación de los candidatos en nuevos formatos, como las entrevistas con el youtuber Jordi Wild o la aparición de Sánchez en la revista del corazón Lecturas. Para Monge, las primeras “buscaban atraer el voto joven” y con la segunda, el candidato del PSOE “estaba pensando en el público femenino, al igual que entrevistas anteriores en ¡Hola! de Adolfo Suárez y Felipe González [este compartiendo portada con los herederos de Franco]”.

El diario Público aseguró que Feijóo suspendió una entrevista con Lecturas después de publicarse la de Sánchez. A preguntas de este diario, fuentes del PP desmintieron esa información. Posteriormente, fuentes de los populares aseguraron a EFE que Lecturas les había solicitado la entrevista y que ellos habían aceptado, pero que, al negarse a publicarla en la edición de papel, decidieron no participar.

Margarita Robles, ministra de Defensa y número dos en la lista electoral del PSOE por Madrid, irrumpió este lunes en la campaña electoral con un vídeo en el que aparece leyendo la famosa entrevista de Sánchez en Lecturas. “El presidente”, dice, “no conquista a las mujeres con las revistas del corazón, lo que hace es darles derechos. En España todos los avances para las mujeres se han conseguido con gobiernos socialistas. Vox y el PP representan la involución”. Robles despide el vídeo diciendo: “La verdad es que está guapo, menudo pájaro”, burlándose de la expresión que Sánchez empleó para referirse a ella en una conversación con Ábalos en 2015 revelada por El Mundo.

Barreiro opina, en todo caso, que el objetivo de la entrevista en Lecturas “obedecía más a una campaña de humanización del candidato que a un intento de convencer a mujeres”. “Ese tipo de formatos de entrevistas, al igual que las de Jordi Wild”, añade, “son una vía de entrada a un colectivo, pero trascienden al público original, porque los grupos sociales se contagian entre sí”. Monge también cree que al sacar a Begoña Gómez, esposa de Pedro Sánchez, en un mitin de campaña, “el PSOE buscaba humanizar a su candidato, exponer el machaque de una familia, más que intentar captar voto femenino”. La socióloga comparte que en este caso también había un factor provocación porque los socialistas sabían que el PP iba a salir en tromba contra esa aparición de Gómez, como así fue. Esa misma noche, Ayuso sugirió que la mujer de Sánchez había intervenido en el mitin porque tenía celos de ella y aseguró que la esposa del presidente podía dar clases “de gestión de saunas con final feliz”.

Las encuestas también revelan la brecha generacional que existe entre las chicas y los chicos más jóvenes: ellos cada vez más inclinados hacia la derecha y la extrema derecha y ellas, hacia la izquierda. Para Monge tiene que ver “con una reacción al feminismo: entienden que han perdido privilegios y se sienten descolocados por el cambio de roles”.

A baby who fell from a third-storey window in Amsterdam survived the incident, police have revealed.

The one-year-old boy was found lying on the ground on the evening of October 30 by a passer-by on Amstelveenweg.

Police are still investigating how the child fell and have appealed for witnesses or anybody in the area with video footage to contact them.

The boy was taken to hospital after the incident. Police did not disclose any details of his condition.

World.title: NL sends delegation to India over abducted Amsterdam girl
World.content:
The Dutch government is sending a delegation of officials to India this week to push for the return of Insiya, a girl from Amsterdam who was abducted on her father’s orders 10 years ago.

Foreign minister Tom Berendsen, who happens to be on a working visit to India, told broadcaster NOS that officials from the foreign and justice ministries will discuss what legal options are available, including the Netherlands’ request to extradite her father, Shehzad Hemani.

He said he hopes the delegation can take the first steps towards restoring contact between Insiya and her mother, Nadia Rashid, who has not seen her daughter since 2016.

Insiya was two years old when she was taken from her grandmother’s home in Amsterdam-Oost in 2016 by a group of men hired by her father. They took her to India via Germany using false documents. She is now 12.

A Dutch court sentenced Hemani in absentia to 8.5 years in prison. Several of his accomplices were jailed for up to four years. India has not extradited Hemani and has not signed the international treaty on child abduction. Indian courts do not treat a child’s removal as abduction if the child lives with one of the parents.

The delegation’s trip follows a video message to Insiya that Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema posted on social media on Sunday. The video is an attempt to get round an Indian court order that has hidden hundreds of articles about the case from users in India.

Since October 30, Google has blocked publications about Insiya for users in India, following an order by a court in New Delhi, NOS reported. The case was brought in the girl’s name by her father and grandmother, who cited safety concerns.

The block covers Dutch and international media reports, Dutch court press releases, government documents and Rashid’s social media accounts, which she had used to try to reach her daughter.

Halsema put out a video message while on a trade mission in Mumbai last week, in which Insiya’s mother tells her daughter that she misses her. Halsema encouraged people to share the video widely.

World.title: PvdD marks 20 years in parliament fighting factory farming
World.content:
Animal rights party PvdD celebrated its 20th year in parliament yesterday, two decades after it became the first political party on earth to gain such power under the banner of improving livestock welfare and banning factory farming.

Party leader Christine Teunissen addressed a crowd of members in Nieuwegein, Utrecht, saying that the group has grown to be “the thorn in the side of the ruling powers”, according to broadcaster NOS.

She drew attention to the leverage the PvdD achieved during the recent cabinet crisis, in which the Jetten government managed to pass its tax plan with essential support from the party, who lent its backing in return for (among other things) funding for alternatives to animal testing.

Teunissen said it she was proud that the PvdD could “break through the VVD’s power politics”, and had shown “what is possible when the VVD is not in control”.

The right-wing liberal VVD voted against its coalition partners, centrist D66 and Christian Democrat CDA, after they agreed a new tax proposal with left-wing opposition parties. This sparked a crisis that many feared would collapse the government.

The PvdD originally refused to support the plan, but its 3 seats in parliament became pivotal amid the dispute.

A bill on livestock farming, which addresses the party’s founding purpose, is due to be voted on in December. It would effectively ban factory farming by 2040, ensuring that all animals are kept in conditions that respect their natural behaviours.

There is already a government act in place that seeks to ensure the same ends, but the PvdD maintains it is too weak to be realistic. A separate bill on banning cruel slaughter methods is also in the works.

World.title: Prosecutors ask for 30 years and treatment for Erasmus shooter
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Prosecutors have demanded a 30-year sentence on appeal for a medical student who shot dead two of his neighbours and a teacher in a fit of “uncontrollable rage”.

Faoud L., from Rotterdam, was given a life sentence for the triple murder at his original trial in February last year.

The public prosecution service said a fixed term was more appropriate because it would allow L. to be given a compulsory treatment order. L. is also appealing against the sentence.

The trial judge said therapy was unlikely to be effective after 30 years in prison, whereas a prisoner on a life sentence can apply for parole after 25 years.

L. shot his next-door neighbour, a 39-year-old woman named as Marlous, and her 14-year-old daughter, Romy, in September 2023, before setting his own flat on fire.

He then rode his motorcycle to Rotterdam’s Erasmus Medical Centre where he shot dead 43-year-old Jurgen Damen as he was giving a lecture to a class of students.

L., now 35, was studying medicine at the university, but became enraged when the exams committee refused to let him sit for his diploma unless he underwent a psychological assessment.

He told an earlier court hearing that he originally planned to kill several students in the classroom, but persuaded himself to target only the lecturer after an “internal conflict”.

Researchers at the Pieter Baan Centrum, which carries out psychological assessments on criminal suspects, concluded that he had a type of autism that made it difficult to process and recognise emotions.

World.title: How much Dutch do you need to get hired in 2027?
World.content:
“Native Dutch” in every vacancy? Here’s how to get hired anyway:

New year, new job hunt! But two little words keep stopping internationals in their tracks. Here’s why they don’t have to stop you.

“Is it even worth trying?” Jamila Vriesman, founder of Amstel Dutch, hears it all the time. Her Dutch language & culture school in Amsterdam has one simple belief: you can’t really learn Dutch without understanding the Dutch. So her students learn both.

Lately, many of them share the same story. Months of lessons. A shiny new CV. Then they spot “native Dutch” in a vacancy and close the tab faster than you can say gezellig.

“I get it,” says Jamila, a born Amsterdammer. “But please don’t give up. The market has changed. So your strategy needs to change too.”

Harder, not hopeless

Short answer: it’s not just you. Since autumn 2025, job seekers in the Netherlands have outnumbered vacancies. The latest CBS figures show 92 vacancies for every 100 job seekers.

“When employers can choose, language often tips the balance,” Jamila explains. Every month you wait, the pile of CVs next to yours grows. And more of them say “some Dutch”. The good news? This is a tiebreaker you can train for.

“Native” is a signal, not a stop sign

“Native Dutch” tells you how important the language is in the job. “Honestly, ‘native’ is an unfortunate requirement,” says Jamila. “Most employers mean professional fluency: you can follow a fast meeting and write a clear email. That is something you can learn. Being born here is not.” Tick the other boxes? Apply. Be honest about your level and show how you are working on it.

And “Dutch is a plus”? “That is not a wall,” Jamila points out. “That is an open door. Walk through it!”

Show what you’ve got

For many other jobs, you don’t need to be fluent to stand out. “Imagine 200 people apply and 15 of them speak some Dutch,” Jamila suggests. “Who do you think gets noticed? Even A2 tells an employer: I’m planning to stay.”

And A2 is closer than you think. With a busy job and one lesson a week, many people get there in about 12 months. More time? You’ll go even faster.

So show it off. Write your LinkedIn summary in Dutch. Add a short Dutch paragraph to your cover letter. Start your interview with a warm goedemorgen (good morning). “Nobody expects you to discuss tax law in your first sentence,” Jamila laughs. “But that one word already does a lot of work.”

Know your world

Every sector sets its own bar. According to Indeed, Dutch is a must in healthcare, education and law, while many tech teams mostly work in English. Know which world you’re walking into, and learn the Dutch it speaks.

Survive your first Dutch meeting

An interview follows a script. A team meeting does not. Suddenly you are in a room full of jokes, shortcuts and half sentences, nodding along and hoping nobody asks you anything. Sound familiar?

“And when a Dutch colleague calls your plan interessant, it’s not always a compliment,” Jamila smiles.

Her tip: train your ears, not just your mouth. Pick two lifesaver phrases and use them this week: Kun je dat nog een keer zeggen? (Could you say that again?) and Wat bedoel je precies? (What exactly do you mean?). Small sentences, big difference.

Find your crew

Can you do all this on your own? Partly. Apps are great for words. But they won’t tell you why your colleague went quiet after your feedback. “A teacher hears the mistakes you no longer notice,” Jamila believes. “And a group gives you a safe place to get things wrong before you do it in a meeting.”

Her last tip: stop comparing yourself to native speakers. “Compare yourself to who you were a year ago. Every level opens more doors. Companies don’t just want someone who can do the job. They want someone who’ll stay and feel at home. Language is the door. Culture is the room behind it.”

Ready to stop nodding along? Jamila and her team at Amstel Dutch teach you the language and the unwritten rules of Dutch working life. No boring drills. No stuffy classrooms.

During the Dutch City Experiences, you explore Amsterdam with your group, use your Dutch where it actually happens and end with a drink in a bruin café. Think of it as a dress rehearsal for your first coffee break at a new job. And to keep the conversation going, join the free monthly taalcafé and practise your Dutch in a relaxed setting.

In a hurry or ready to immerse yourself? Amstel Dutch also offers intensive weeks that take you through a full level in one week (coffee included, sleep optional): A0 to A1 from 14 to 19 December and A1 to A2 from 11 to 16 January 2027. More dates follow throughout the year.

Not sure where to start? Book your free 20-minute intake: you’ll know your level, the level your next job asks for, and the quickest realistic route between the two. Your way into Dutch life starts here.

World.title: Dutch households turning down gas as global unrest stokes prices
World.content:
Dutch households are using less gas for heating and more electricity in response to the steep rise in energy prices, according to figures from energy supplier Essent.

The company said gas consumption dropped by 10% year-on-year at the start of November, despite the cold start to the month, while electricity use was up by 40%.

Essenty said there was a clear trend towards switching to electric heating systems such as infrared panels and air conditioning units, which can also be used for heating.

Households are still using gas as their main source of heating, but electric heaters are being used as a top-up supply, with a surge in demand in the early hours of the evening as people come home from work and school.

Most homes are still connected to the gas mains, but the Dutch government is committed to switching off the supply completely by 2050.

“Under normal temperatures we saw the same gas use as normal, but op November 3, when it was 1 degree below the normal temperature, we saw 4% less gas use,” Essent energy market specialist Denise van Zon told NOS.

Earlier surveys by Essent found that a quarter of households are planning to use electric heating devices as gas prices are expected to remain high through the winter because of the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, which is restricting global supplies.

“I think the unrest is the reason for the increase,” Van Zon said. “We’ve heard about the gas reserves, the conflict in Iran and we have seen another significant increase in prices.”

The average household gas price has risen by 35% since October last year and many energy companies are offering lower prices for multiple-year contracts in an attempt to encourage customers to fix their prices for the long term.

World.title: Dutch man who spent 42 years in US prison for murder dies
World.content:
A Dutch man who spent 42 years in prison in the US for murder has died of leukaemia, eight months after being repatriated to the Netherlands.

Jaitsen Singh, 81, spent his final months in Scheveningen after the appeal court in The Hague ordered the government to bring him home because of his age and ill health.

His death on Sunday was confirmed in an online post by his lawyer, Rachel Imamkhan, who represented him since 2011. He was the longest serving Dutch prisoner in foreign custody.

“Those who knew him will mainly remember the man behind the case,” she wrote.

In August the appeal court ordered him to be transferred from the US to the Netherlands, following years of campaigning by his family and lawyers.

He was born in Suriname when it was still a Dutch colony and held a Dutch passport, even after moving to the US in 1970. The Dutch attorney general opposed his repatriation, arguing he had insufficient ties to the country.

Denied guilt

Singh was jailed in 1986 for “56 years to life” for arranging the murder of his wife and stepdaughter, but he has always denied committing the crime.

Their bodies were found in the boot of their car in Los Angeles two years earlier. A key piece of evidence was a statement by a serving prisoner who was later found to have been bribed.

Imamkhan said his case was “seen by many as a miscarriage of justice in the United States and remained a subject of debate for years.”

But the family of his wife and stepdaughter said they believed he was responsible for their deaths and his “‘continued denial and lack of remorse have only deepened the family’s suffering”.

In a statement released through the family support organisation Namens de Familie, they said Singh was being portrayed as a victim “while two innocent lives that have been taken away are once again fading into the background.”

Last August the appeal court ordered the state to request Singh’s transfer from the US to a Dutch prison, following years of campaigning by his family and lawyers. He flew into the Netherlands in March this year.

He was born in Suriname when it was still a Dutch colony and held a Dutch passport, even after moving to the US in 1970. The Netherlands opposed his repatriation, arguing he had insufficient ties to the country.

World.title: US turtle invasion: exotic species spreading through NL
World.content:
An “invasive exotic species” in spreading through the Netherlands – the yellow-bellied slider turtle – which has been brought from the US and can now survive in an increasingly warm environment, according to radio programme Vroege Vogels.

The species has long been imported from America and sold as pets but until recently could not survive in the cold Dutch climate.

This has changed and last Spring someone spotted a group of young turtles by a pond in Zuid-Holland, and contacted Faunawatch, an organisation dedicated to abandoned turtles.

After inspecting the site, sixteen empty eggs and two young turtles were found, both of which have been taken to a rescue centre in Limburg.

Tim Huijsmans, a researcher from Faunawatch, told the radio programme that climate change is making it possible for these turtles to breed in the Netherlands for the first time.

“If it is too cold, the hatchlings die in the egg. So now, for the first time, young water turtles have been born. After hatching, they burrowed into the ground during the winter and went to the water in the spring,” he explained.

An estimated 200,000 freshwater turtles have been dumped in the Dutch wild, he said, and the government now needs to allocate funds to monitor their spread and the risks associated.

The Netherlands will become the latest country to purchase Poland’s Piorun man-portable air-defence systems, which have been increasingly in demand following their successful use during Ukraine’s defence against Russia. On Monday, their Polish manufacturer, Mesko, which is part of state-owned defence group PGZ, signed an agreement adding the Netherlands to a list of countries that will buy Pioruns with funds from the European Union’s SAFE mechanism for financing defence spending. 🇵🇱🇳🇱⚡ HOLANDIA DOŁĄCZA DO DRUŻYNY PIORUNA! W @PGZ_MESKO_SA w Skarżysku-Kamiennej podpisano aneks do umowy ramowej, umożliwiający Holandii dołączenie do wspólnych zamówień zestawów PIORUN. ✍️ Dokument podpisali gen. dyw. In 2022, Pioruns were among the large quantities of military equipment that Poland provided to Ukraine to help its eastern neighbour defend itself from Russia’s full-scale invasion. The systems have been successfully used to take down Russian aircraft. Since then, they have been in high demand, with Mesko receiving orders from the United States, Norway, Belgium and Sweden, as well as Ukraine itself. In August this year, Mesko signed an 8 billion zloty (€1.8 billion) agreement to supply further Piorun systems to Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia, with the deal financed through SAFE funds. Precise details were not revealed. However, the agreement was said to involve the supply of “several hundred” launchers and “several thousand” missiles, with over 80% of the equipment going to Poland’s own armed forces. Now Mesko has signed an addendum to that deal, adding the Netherlands to the list of countries that are jointly ordering Pioruns. Deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who has overseen Poland’s participation in the SAFE programme, said after attending Monday’s signing ceremony that the Netherlands would not be the last country to join the procurement of Pioruns. “We promised that the list of Mesko’s buyers from all over Europe would grow, and today we have living proof of that,” said Sobkowiak-Czarnecka. “And I can reveal a secret: it’s not over yet.” She noted that Mesko has stepped up its production volumes in response to demand. Last year, it could produce “several hundred” systems annually; that has now risen to 1,500, and is set to grow even further. Last week, PGZ and the state assets ministry signed an agreement to support Mesko’s expansion with around 370 million zloty from the state Capital Investment Fund (FIK). It will help bring production capacity to around 2,500 per year. 🗣️ "Obiecywaliśmy, że lista kupujących z całej Europy będzie się powiększać i mamy tego żywy dowód. The firm’s revenues of 2.3 billion zloty in 2025 were up 33% year-on-year. The EU’s SAFE programme is providing a total of €150 billion in loans at preferential rates for member states to use on defence-related spending. Poland, with around €44 billion, is the largest single recipient. While most SAFE purchases are conducted individually by member states, some are also carried out jointly. World.title: Public astronomical observatory opens in Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Warsaw’s first astronomical observatory open to the public and run by a local municipal institution launched on Sunday. Its organisers say the facility, with two telescopes allowing safe observation of the Sun and photography of the cosmos, is aimed at astronomy enthusiasts as well as children and young people, who will be able to watch the night sky and participate in recording data without needing their own equipment. The new observatory, which is located on the roof of the Gocław Culture Terminal in the Praga-South of Poland’s capital, was created in response to growing public interest in astronomy, science and new technologies, says city hall. “Under the three-metre-high dome, specialised equipment awaits, allowing for observation of the sky, including safe viewing of the Sun,” said mayor Rafał Trzaskowski, who visited the facility last week ahead of its official opening. “Anyone who is interested can come here and learn about space through observation, photographing the sky and hands-on activities,” he added. The observatory will be free to use but only accessible during organised events, owing to limited space and the expensive equipment it contains, reports newspaper Super Express. “The dome houses very expensive equipment. For most of the year, it will function as a broadcasting station, and images from the telescopes will be projected onto screens in the main hall of the terminal,” Jacek Białek, head of Gocław Culture Terminal, told the newspaper. “We will invite people inside the dome as part of programs, the dates of which will be published on the cultural centre’s website,” he added. Participants in workshops and events will also be able to help collect and analyse data, with Białek noting that the centre will be working closely with scientists from the University of Warsaw The new facility cost around 500,000 zloty (€111,000), most of which was covered from the district budget, with contributions from private donations as well as grants from the state-owned military optoelectronic equipment company PCO and the national lottery foundation. The core of the new facility is a 14″ DO-GSO (Ritchey-Chrétien) telescope with a mirror diameter of approximately 35 cm and a focal length of approximately 2,850 mm, placed on an EQ8-RH equatorial mount with automatic sky tracking. This setup, along with a QHY268M Pro monochrome camera, a filter wheel and an electronic focuser, will be used for astrophotography and targeted photometric measurements, producing images suited to Warsaw’s atmospheric conditions. The observatory also boasts a specialist Sky-Watcher Heliostar 100 H-Alpha telescope, which is used for safe and detailed observation and astrophotography of the Sun, allowing viewers to see structures in the solar atmosphere invisible through an ordinary telescope. The telescope allows solar prominences – large, bright features extending out from the Sun’s surface – to be observed and compared with images produced on other days. The telescope is protected by a three-metre dome that automatically opens and rotates. Warsaw has been chosen as the location for a new European Space Agency security centre, as Poland takes another step in its ambitions to become a bigger player in the space sector The facility will be the @esa's first outside its 11 founding member states https://t.co/WnHIbrW3ze — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 13, 2026 The observatory also features a computer coordinating its measurements, a camera showing almost the entire sky, and a weather monitoring system. Observations will depend on atmospheric conditions and visibility. “Examples of how this telescope might be used include photographing the cosmos and conducting simple research, such as measuring changes in the brightness of stars and producing graphs illustrating these changes,” explained Ewa Konarzewska from Gocław Culture Terminal. Poland has placed great emphasis on developing its space industry in recent years, with the aim of becoming a major European player in the sector. Last year, the country launched its first national military satellite. A Polish firm, Creotech Instruments, signed Poland’s largest-ever contract with the European Space Agency, a €52 million deal to build and launch a constellation of Earth observation satellites. Meanwhile, 2025 also saw astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski become the second-ever Pole to travel into space, as part of an ESA mission to the International Space Station. Earlier this year, Warsaw was chosen as the location for a new ESA centre focused on civil security and resilience, with the agency’s head declaring that “Poland has rapidly become one of the driving forces in Europe’s space sector”. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prosecutors investigating three objects that landed in Poland last Friday morning have confirmed that they were all Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. They added that preliminary findings indicate the missiles were recently manufactured at a plant in Dubna, Russia. The objects struck at three different locations in southeastern Poland – Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik and Mołodycz – not far from the Ukrainian border. The incidents took place amid large-scale Russian attacks on Ukraine. No injuries or damage to infrastructure was reported as a result of the strikes on Poland. Prokuratorzy wojskowi oraz Żandarmeria Wojskowa ustalili, że w Nowym Lipowcu, Rudniku i Mołodyczu spadły rosyjskie pociski manewrujące Ch-101. Wyprodukowano je w IV kwartale 2026 r. w zakładach w Dubnej pod Moskwą. W dwóch miejscach oględziny już się zakończyły. Dziś rano,… https://t.co/nNfkvx4FAq — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 23, 2026 Initially, on Friday, Poland’s defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, identified one of the objects as a Kh-101 cruise missile – the same type as one that entered Polish airspace and exploded in eastern Poland in July this year. He said another was also likely a missile while the third was probably a jet-powered drone. However, in a statement issued on Sunday, the district prosecutor’s office in Lublin, which is leading the investigation, confirmed that all three objects were Kh-101 cruise missiles. Analysis is still underway, but “preliminary findings indicate that all the missiles were manufactured in the fourth quarter of 2026 at a plant in Dubna (Moscow Oblast, Russian Federation)”, said the prosecutors. Dubna is home to MKB Raduga, the Russian aerospace firm that produces Kh-101 missiles. “Kremlin trolls will once again try to convince Poles that these are not Russian missiles,” wrote Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, “but the evidence nips those lies in the bud.” Ireneusz Nowak, the operational commander of the Polish armed forces, revealed on Friday that the three missiles were in Polish airspace for around three minutes before hitting the ground. Two Swedish Gripen fighter jets, which are helping patrol Polish skies as part of a NATO air policing mission, had attempted to intercept the missiles. They received authorisation from NATO’s Combined Air Operations Centre to fire upon the objects if certain conditions were met. However, the pilots were unable to confirm the identity of the objects in time, largely because of “extremely difficult weather conditions”, said Nowak, quoted by the Rzeczpospolita daily. World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. A consortium led by FedEx has completed its €7.8 billion (34.5 billion zloty) takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost. The deal will see InPost remain headquartered in Poland, with founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska staying at the helm. Friday’s announcement brings to a close a process that was first announced in February and received European Commission approval in August. InPost’s shares have now been delisted from the stock exchange. The takeover follows years of rapid growth for InPost, which pioneered the use of parcel delivery lockers in Poland before spreading rapidly in major western European markets, including France, Spain and the UK. A consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF has completed its takeover of Poland's InPost, which is now private. InPost has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Founder Rafał Brzoska stays on as CEO, and the company remains headquartered in Poland. pic.twitter.com/HWigKVPC3w — IPO Newsroom (@IPONewsroom_) November 20, 2026 Under the deal, FedEx and Advent, an American private equity firm, each hold 37% of InPost. A&R Investments, Brzoska’s own investment vehicle, has 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. PPF, A&R and Advent were previously already stakeholders. The consortium acquired InPost at a price of €15.60 per share, valuing the company at approximately €7.8 billion. In a statement published on Friday, Advent confirmed that InPost would retain its name, branding, Polish headquarters and operational independence following the takeover. Brzoska, who founded his business in 1999, will continue as CEO alongside the existing management team. “InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network,” said Advent. They added that the new consortium would now “accelerate investment” in InPost’s operations, helping the firm “extend its reach further”. FedEx and InPost would also “explore opportunities” to cooperate with one another. “InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment,” said FedEx’s CEO and president, Raj Subramaniam. “Connecting our global network…with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth.” Brzoska, who is one of Poland’s wealthiest individuals, said that the new partnership would “deliver the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler”. President Macron has thanked Polish delivery giant InPost for its latest investment in France The firm, which already operates over 9,000 parcel lockers in France through its subsidiary Mondial Relay, will now spend a further €500m to expand its presence https://t.co/caOGNQemfm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 InPost is the largest operator of parcel lockers in Europe, with around 70,000 across the continent. That includes roughly 30,000 in Poland and 16,000 in the UK, including in branches of the British Post Office, with over 23,000 more in the seven Eurozone countries where InPost operates. In the second quarter of 2026, InPost had revenue of 4.18 billion zloty (€970 million), up 18.2% year on year, while its number of parcels handled rose 16% to 380.9 million. The strongest revenue growth came in the eurozone, where sales increased 37.9%, followed by Poland, with 12.7% growth. Revenue in the UK and Ireland rose 9.8%. Poland recently managed to prevent a planned Russian “false-flag operation” at the border that, if it had not been stopped, could have “ended tragically”, says a retired general who acts as an advisor to the defence minister. His statement follows a report earlier this week by a leading newspaper, based on statements by unnamed senior officials, that Poland had foiled an attempt by Russia to carry out a major “provocation” on the border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Polish government figures, including Prime Minister Donald Tusk, have confirmed that a Russian operation at the border was prevented, though they have not provided further details. Generał Mieczysław Bieniek o próbie rosyjskiej prowokacji przy granicy z Polską !!! Polskie władze potwierdzają udaremnioną próbę rosyjskiej prowokacji przy granicy z obwodem królewieckim. – Udało się udaremnić, być może tragiczny w skutkach, incydent – przyznał w "Faktach po… pic.twitter.com/raQMfJ4uUp — Andrzej Mitura #Mocnytakżeosobno (@AndrzejekMitura) November 19, 2026 “The public isn’t informed about everything,” retired general Mieczysław Bieniek, who acts as an advisor to defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, told broadcaster TVN on Thursday. Bieniek then revealed that, “based on information we received from both our allies and our own intelligence services, we managed to thwart an incident with potentially tragic consequences, because the planned false-flag operation could have ended tragically”. “For example, if a group of people crossed the border and later dressed in uniforms, whether Ukrainian or Polish, but were Russian citizens disguised as others, and carried out an attack on their target, the side whose uniforms were worn would naturally be blamed,” continued the general. “Fortunately, nothing of the sort happened,” he added. “Certainly this preventative action [by Poland] forced the other side to desist from these acts.” Bieniek’s comments followed a report published on Wednesday by the Rzeczpospolita daily, which said it had learned of a planned Russian sabotage operation on the border between Poland and the Kaliningrad exclave. The newspaper, citing unnamed high-ranking figures from the uniformed services, said that the planned incident could have involved Russia mounting an attack on one of its own facilities but blaming it on Ukraine. Such actions are known as false-flag operations. “It was supposed to be reminiscent of the Gleiwitz incident,” said one unnamed source, referring to a false-flag attack in 1939 staged by Nazi Germany, in which German operatives dressed in Polish uniforms. It was one of a number of such staged incidents used to justify the invasion of Poland. 🔴 Operacja polskich służb oraz wojska na przełomie października i listopada zapobiegła rosyjskiej prowokacji na granicy z obwodem królewieckim – wynika z ustaleń @marek_kozubal https://t.co/EFWsdlZUHY — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 18, 2026 According to Rzeczpospolita, concerns over this planned Russian operation were what prompted Poland to bolster security in regions along the Kaliningrad border in late October. On 3 November, Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared that Poland had “managed to prevent a provocation” on the border after “individuals with flashlights” were spotted. However, he did not provide further details at the time. When Rzeczpospolita this week asked Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, if Russia had been planning a terrorist attack, he replied: “You’d have to ask the Russians. And they usually don’t admit to planning such actions. Even if we have such information, we don’t share it.” “If we took certain steps, it was because we recognised there was a real threat,” added Siemoniak. “Appropriate actions were taken by the border guard, the police and the military. I can’t go into details.” Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk claims that "individuals with flashlights" were observed at the Russian border last night. "We very quickly mobilised the appropriate forces and resources there, and managed to prevent a provocation," he added https://t.co/kD5OmpNagf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2026 On Wednesday afternoon, Kosiniak-Kamysz himself was asked about reports of a planned border provocation. “It didn’t happen, because we responded appropriately,” said the defence minister. “Russia is rapidly climbing the escalation ladder, moving from airspace violations, attempted train bombings, sabotage of arms factories, as well as cyberspace activity, [and] it can also provoke at the border,” he continued, referring to some of the actions Russia has already taken against Poland. However, Kosiniak-Kamysz did not comment on or provide any specific details of what kind of incident Poland may have prevented on the Kaliningrad border. Later on Wednesday, Tusk himself reiterated to journalists that “we received signals that some unacceptable events could occur near the Polish-Russian border” and that “it seems that the mobilisation of the border guard and police in this place blocked any plans or ideas to carry out any provocation”. However, he added that further details are “kept confidential for obvious reasons”. Two Russian missiles and what is likely to have been a jet-powered drone struck Poland last night during large-scale attacks on Ukraine, the defence minister has confirmed https://t.co/QM2t2hOwlg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 20, 2026 Poland’s government has for months been warning that Russia is planning escalatory provocations against eastern NATO states, which could involve border and airspace violations. In June, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski even announced that he was “expecting an attack on Russian territory under a false flag, to which Putin will ‘respond'”. Sikorski pointed to the Gleiwitz incident as an example of such an operation. On Friday morning, two Russian missiles and what is believed to be a drone entered Polish airspace and hit the ground in three locations. Tusk condemned the incident as a further “Russian escalation” and said that it was likely to have been “an intentional provocation”. World.title: Two Ukrainians charged with vandalising Polish monuments on behalf of Russia
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Two Ukrainians have been charged in Poland with working on behalf of Russia to paint slogans praising the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a nationalist formation responsible for massacring Poles during World War Two, on three monuments in the Polish city of Poznań. Polish prosecutors say that the operation was intended to fuel hostility between Poles and Ukrainians. The incidents in Poznań were part of a seemingly coordinated wave of similar graffiti on monuments in three other Polish cities. Ukraińcy malowali na pomnikach hasła „Sława UPA”. Działali na zlecenie wywiaduhttps://t.co/knLgZzo8ct — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 19, 2026 In early November, the words “Slava UPA” (“Glory to the UPA”) were painted in red on three monuments in Poznań commemorating World War Two soldiers. While the UPA is remembered by many in Ukraine for fighting for independence from Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is primarily associated with leading the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, were slaughtered as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. The history of those massacres, and the continued veneration of the UPA by some in Ukraine, has regularly stirred tension between Poland and Ukraine, who are otherwise close allies. On Thursday, the National Prosecutor’s Office confirmed to the Polish Press Agency (PAP) that two Ukrainians, who can be named only as Nikita S. and Dmytro Y. under Polish privacy law, had been detained and charged in relation to the vandalism. According to prosecutors, Nikita S., “acting on behalf of Russian intelligence and in order to obtain financial benefit of $500”, persuaded Dmytro Y. to “commit an act of sabotage by painting the slogans” with the aim of “publicly inciting hatred based on national differences between the Polish and Ukrainian peoples”. The suspects were identified by police and the Internal Security Agency (ABW), who had analysed surveillance footage of the perpetrator, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. Both were detained in Poznań, according to PAP. In the wake of the Poznań vandalism, Poland-based Belarusian news outlet MOST reported that, a few days before the graffiti appeared, an advert offering $500 for someone to paint pro-UPA slogans on monuments in the city had appeared on messaging service Telegram. When an undercover journalist from the outlet contacted the person offering the job, they were told that similar work was available in other Polish cities. Around the same time, almost identical graffiti praising the UPA appeared on further monuments in the cities of Gdańsk, Gdynia and Warsaw, including one dedicated to the heroes of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising. Around a dozen monuments in Poland, including one dedicated to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, have been defaced with graffiti glorifying the WWII Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Ukraine’s embassy in Warsaw has condemned the vandalism and blamed it on Russia https://t.co/iaZb2CyiPx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2026 Last week, local police in Gdańsk confirmed that they had detained a 17-year-old Ukrainian suspected of carrying out the graffiti there and in Gdynia. He has been charged with promoting fascist ideology, incitement to violence and hatred based on nationality, and desecration of monuments. The Ukrainian embassy in Poland has condemned the acts of vandalism, calling them a “disgraceful provocation” and “a manifestation of the hybrid war that Russia is attempting to wage by any means in European states”. Poland has been a primary target for Russia’s so-called hybrid actions in Europe, which have included acts of sabotage, espionage, disinformation and efforts to stir hostility towards Ukrainians. Such operations are rarely carried out by Russian operatives themselves. Instead, Russia often recruits people already on the ground, often members of Poland’s large Ukrainian and Belarusian migrant communities, as well as Poles themselves in some cases. In July this year, a Ukrainian teenager was indicted by Polish prosecutors on charges of painting dozens of pro-UPA slogans in public places, including on a monument to victims of the Volhynia massacres. Two Russian missiles and what is likely to have been a jet-powered drone struck Poland today amid large-scale attacks on Ukraine, the defence minister has confirmed. On Friday morning, an image published by Polish media outlet Wirtualna Polska showed a crater in the ground with a fire burning in the middle of it. The website reported that it had been caused by an object landing in a field in the village of Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland, around 60 kilometres from the Ukrainian border. 🔴Tu spadł niezidentyfikowany obiekt. Mamy zdjęcie Niezidentyfikowany obiekt spadł w piątek rano na pole w miejscowości Nowy Lipowiec w powiecie biłgorajskim. Stało się to kilkaset metrów od zabudowań. Nikomu nic się nie stało. Mamy zdjęcie z tego miejsca… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) November 20, 2026 At a press conference later on Friday morning, Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the object in Nowy Lipowiec was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile (the same type as one that entered Polish airspace and exploded in eastern Poland in July this year). The defence minister also revealed that another missile had fallen in the town of Rudnik nad Sanem and what is likely to be a jet-powered drone had struck in the village of Mołodycz. Both of those locations are also in southeastern Poland, not far from the Ukrainian border. He added that there were no reports of injuries or any damage to critical infrastructure as a result of the incidents in Poland, which he noted had taken place during “one of the largest Russian attacks on Ukraine since the beginning of the full-scale war”. Kosiniak-Kamysz also suggested that the fact that these incidents had taken place now was “no coincidence”, given that military exercises of the Coalition of the Willing – a group of countries supporting Ukraine – are taking place in Poland not far from where the missiles and drone struck. Addressing the media on Friday afternoon, Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared that Friday represented “another instalment in the Russian escalation”. He said that there was no doubt that the objects which had hit Poland were Russian. “I’m cautious in my wording, but it does seem that we’re dealing with an intentional provocation,” added the prime minister. NATO’s secretary general, Mark Rutte, announced that he had spoken with Tusk about “the grave violations of Polish airspace” and declared that the alliance “stands in solidarity with Poland and will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend”. Spoke with @donaldtusk about the grave violations of Polish airspace overnight. NATO jets were scrambled in response. We stand in solidarity with Poland and will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend. This incident is clearly dangerous – a consequence of… — Mark Rutte (@SecGenNATO) November 20, 2026 During the early hours of Friday, operational command of Poland’s armed forces reported that they had “activated the necessary forces in response to Russia’s strikes on targets in Ukraine”. Such communiques have become common in recent months, as Poland has had to scramble its forces in response to Russia’s increasing strikes on targets in western Ukraine, including a passenger train travelling between Kyiv and Warsaw that was hit by a jet-powered drone in September this year. In recent months, the Polish government has warned of intelligence suggesting the likelihood of “provocations” by Russia, including airspace and border violations. In September this year, a Russian helicopter briefly crossed the border from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Earlier this month, Poland claimed to have foiled a ground operation around the border with Kaliningrad. Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk claims that "individuals with flashlights" were observed at the Russian border last night. "We very quickly mobilised the appropriate forces and resources there, and managed to prevent a provocation," he added https://t.co/kD5OmpNagf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2026 In September 2025, around 20 Russian drones crossed Poland’s eastern borders in an unprecedented violation that prompted Poland to trigger NATO’s Article 4. Back in November 2022, during the early stages of Russia’s war in Ukraine, two people died in Poland after a missile crossed the Ukrainian border and struck the ground. It later transpired to have been a Ukrainian air-defence missile fired in response to Russian attacks. Poland’s consumer protection authority, UOKiK, has fined Allegro, one of Europe’s largest e-commerce platforms, 55 million zloty (€12.3 million) for misleading consumers over a campaign that promised to plant trees in exchange for collecting parcels through its delivery service. The case is one of a series of investigations into so-called “greenwashing” launched by the authority against companies operating in Poland. UOKiK found that two of the Polish e-commerce group’s practices relating to the tree-planting initiative had infringed consumers’ interests. The first involved promotional claims suggesting that collecting 10 parcels through Allegro’s delivery service would result in a tree being planted. In practice, however, Allegro calculated the number of trees to be planted using forecasts prepared the previous year, rather than linking plantings to individual consumers’ parcel collections. This meant that decisions on the number of trees had already been made before customers collected their parcels. 🌳 Greenwashing ma swoją cenę! Blisko 55 mln zł kary dla Allegro – ekologiczne obietnice miały zachęcać do odbioru paczek, ale rzeczywistość nie była tak zielona. Milionów deklarowanych drzew nigdy nie posadzono. ❌ Ekościema nie może się opłacać 🔎https://t.co/yPQznKz0H1 pic.twitter.com/UDcWXWq3LI — UOKiK (@UOKiKgovPL) November 18, 2026 The second breach concerned the conditions attached to the campaign, which Allegro failed to communicate clearly to consumers. According to UOKiK, Allegro’s promotional messages could have led customers to believe that collecting 10 parcels through their delivery was sufficient to trigger tree planting. In fact, customers had to do it within a single calendar year and, from January 2024, submit a dedication for the tree within a specified period. Without a dedication, collecting the required number of parcels did not result in a tree being planted or assigned to the customer. UOKiK also found that the option to submit a dedication was unavailable for extended periods. Between March and November 2024, the feature was disabled for a total of 264 days, the watchdog said. The prolonged interruptions could have led customers to forget about the requirement or abandon their attempts to submit a dedication, meaning they would not receive the promised tree. UOKiK imposed a fine of 29.9 million zloty for the first practice and 24.9 million zloty for the second. Its decision can still be appealed in court by Allegro, which has not yet commented on the decision. “Green claims must be truthful, specific and verifiable; otherwise, they may mislead consumers and constitute an example of greenwashing,” said UOKiK president Tomasz Chróstny. “If a consumer hears, ‘collect 10 parcels, and we will plant a tree,’ they have the right to interpret that literally,” Chróstny said, adding that “several million [trees] – more than half of the total number claimed by Allegro – were never planted at all”. When announcing its decision, UOKiK noted that, according to a 2025 consumer survey conducted by the European Union, 43% of Poles said that the environmental impact of a product or service influenced their choices. The Allegro case forms part of a broader crackdown on suspected greenwashing by companies operating in Poland. Alongside Allegro, UOKiK has brought charges against delivery companies DHL, DPD and InPost, mobility firm Bolt, retailers Tchibo and Zara, and cosmetics firm L’Oréal Polska.
