World.title: Ants Nõmper: How to legalize euthanasia in Estonia?
World.content:
I believe there are no credible arguments against holding a referendum on whether euthanasia should be permitted. Just as a competition is a celebration for athletes, a referendum is a celebration of democracy, writes Ants Nõmper.

The Riigikogu is considering a proposal by Eesti 200 to hold a referendum on euthanasia. As usual, there are differing opinions and criticisms.

Broadly speaking, the criticism directed at the proposal can be divided into three categories. The first consists of arguments based on the Constitution. Is it even permissible to put such an issue to a referendum? Can the referendum be held alongside parliamentary elections?

The second category covers criticism rooted in medical law. Is the question sufficiently clear? Is it asking about euthanasia, assisted suicide or limiting medical treatment?

The third category includes broader ethical and societal objections, such as whether Estonian society is ready. Are our other systems functioning well enough?

All these criticisms will have to be addressed individually in the Riigikogu. Let us assume that a referendum is held and the outcome is positive, meaning that the public supports legalizing euthanasia. How, then, should Estonia go about legalizing it?

What is euthanasia?

Before regulating something, we must understand what it is we are regulating — in other words, what constitutes euthanasia and what does not.

Euthanasia means the termination of a person's life by a physician on humanitarian grounds. Euthanasia is permitted in some countries and prohibited in others. Each country must decide for itself whether to allow euthanasia at all and, if so, under what conditions.

But what does not constitute euthanasia? A patient dying from complications of medical treatment is not euthanasia. For example, administering painkillers to a patient in doses that cause death as a side effect is not euthanasia, but rather the realization of a knowingly accepted risk. Every medication is a poison and potentially life-threatening, even when administered in accordance with treatment guidelines.

Nor is it euthanasia when a physician refrains from acting because there is an obstacle to providing treatment. One such obstacle may be the patient's wishes, meaning a situation in which treatment is not initiated or treatment already underway is discontinued at the patient's request.

Another obstacle may arise when a physician refuses to initiate treatment or discontinues treatment already underway for medical reasons. Thus, a physician may allow a patient to die because consent to treatment has not been given or to avoid providing futile treatment.

Neither situation constitutes euthanasia, which involves an act intended to bring about a patient's death at their request and out of compassion. Death does occur, but it is not the objective of the action; rather, it is an inevitable consequence. The patient is not killed but allowed to die. Medical care is provided during the dying process, not for the purpose of causing death. Providing medical care during the dying process is entirely lawful and requires no additional regulation.

Centuries-old debate

When is the right time to regulate a particular aspect of society? No one disputes that any regulation must be preceded by public debate. But how long, extensive, substantive and so on must that debate be? I know of no specific criteria for determining when there has been enough debate and when there has not. What I do know, however, are the statistics on the euthanasia debate.

According to DIGAR, a database that catalogs Estonian publications, the word "euthanasia" first appeared in the Estonian press in 1935. Even then, legalizing euthanasia in Estonia was considered to require legislation allowing people to make an advance declaration of their end-of-life wishes.

The newspaper even published the text of such a declaration:

"I am … years old and suffer very severe pain from … disease. As I have been informed, my illness is incurable and already at a very advanced stage. I have spoken with my relatives and put my affairs in order as far as I could. I have consulted my physician, Dr. …, and authorized him, in accordance with legal requirements, to grant me a quicker and more peaceful death. I know that in doing so I am shortening my life, but also my suffering. I authorize my physician to hasten my death."

In the first years following Estonia's restoration of independence, the debate over euthanasia was largely dormant. According to DIGAR, an average of six articles on euthanasia appeared annually during that period. A significant increase in press coverage came in the mid-1990s and by the end of the decade, nearly 50 articles on euthanasia were being published each year.

The peak year for coverage of euthanasia was 2013 when 119 articles appeared in the Estonian press. Interest subsequently waned somewhat, with an average of approximately 60 articles published annually. In total, the subject has been covered 1,758 times in the Estonian press. This figure excludes social media, television, radio and online media whose content has not been reproduced in print, including all coverage by Estonian Public Broadcasting.

In addition to the mainstream media, opinions have also been expressed in professional publications. Professor Jaan Sootak, the grand old man of Estonian criminal law, initiated a legal debate on euthanasia in the journal Juridica in 1995. Physician Dr. Rait Lobotkin brought the discussion to the medical journal Eesti Arst in 1998. The Estonian Council of Churches published its position in 2006 and the Estonian Bioethics Council organized a conference on euthanasia in 2010.

The journal Juridica subsequently brought all stakeholders, except patients, together again in 2017, organizing two roundtable discussions on euthanasia. Physicians, ethicists, lawyers and theologians participated in these discussions. Thus, all the relevant professionals have had an opportunity to express their views. Everyone except the public.

What do the people want?

The first attempt to gauge public opinion in Estonia was a survey conducted by Eesti Päevaleht in 1996. Asked whether euthanasia should be permitted when a person has no hope of recovery and can survive only in a hospital bed connected to life-support equipment, 60 percent of the 254 respondents answered yes, 27 percent said no and the remaining 13 percent had no opinion.

Since the issue of euthanasia frequently arises in connection with cancer patients, the views of this group were also examined. Asked whether a patient with incurable cancer should have the right to request medical assistance in ending their life with dignity, 5 percent of the 110 patients surveyed at Tartu University Hospital answered no, 58 percent said yes, 22 percent were undecided and 13 percent could not say.

The will of the people can also be expressed through citizens' initiatives. In fact, the bill introduced by Eesti 200 is not the first attempt to seek public input on euthanasia.

The first proposal, which collected 2,246 signatures, was submitted by the Estonian Greens in 2020. Reading the proposal, however, it is unclear what exactly its supporters were signing, as it conflated euthanasia with advance declarations of end-of-life wishes. The Riigikogu's Social Affairs Committee did not support the citizens' initiative, citing the need to first regulate advance declarations of end-of-life wishes and improve access to palliative care.

Is the time right now?

The current Riigikogu has successfully dealt with advance declarations of end-of-life wishes. Starting next year, adults with full legal capacity will be able to specify, either on paper or electronically, what healthcare professionals may or may not do to them. So half the job is done. But what about the other half — palliative care?

"Since 2020, hospice care has been included on the Estonian Health Insurance Fund's list of healthcare services, meaning it is publicly funded."

Palliative care, which includes hospice care, does not cure illness but alleviates symptoms and improves the well-being of patients with serious illnesses that diminish their quality of life. Access to palliative care in Estonia has improved significantly in recent years. Since 2020, hospice care has been included on the Estonian Health Insurance Fund's list of healthcare services, meaning it is publicly funded. A two-part clinical guideline on palliative care has also been in place since then.

There is no doubt that palliative care needs more funding, but isn't the same true of cancer treatment, cardiology, dental care, child psychiatry and most other areas of medicine? Limited treatment options are undoubtedly an important consideration when determining the substance of any regulation, but they are not a reason to avoid public debate. I would therefore argue that the other half of the job has also been done and the time is ripe for a substantive debate on regulating euthanasia in Estonia.

What needs regulating?

Looking at euthanasia regulations in different countries, the requirements can be summarized as follows: Anyone reading the law should be able to find answers to the following questions:

Who may request euthanasia? It would be advisable to restrict eligibility to Estonian residents who are adults and have legal capacity and decision-making capacity.

Under what circumstances should euthanasia be considered? It would be advisable to take both an objective approach based on diagnostic codes and a subjective approach that considers the severity of suffering. A decision must be made on whether eligibility should be based solely on physical illness or also include mental illness and how close a patient must be to the end of their life.

How should the patient's wishes be established? It would be advisable to require consultations with physicians, consideration of alternatives, repeated expression of the patient's wishes after a waiting period, written documentation, notification of family members and so on. Safeguards must be put in place to prevent undue influence by family members and inappropriate motives on the part of the patient, such as a desire to avoid becoming a financial burden.

What medical safeguards should be in place? A medical review by a panel of physicians should be required, a humane method of ending life must be agreed upon, physicians must be guaranteed the right not to participate in euthanasia and documentation requirements must be established.

What oversight should be in place? Euthanasia should not be available at every medical facility and law enforcement authorities should be notified when a patient requests euthanasia. It may also be reasonable to establish a role for an ethics committee and create a registry to analyze the effects on society.

Lawful act or lack of prosecution?

If Estonia decides to introduce legislation regulating euthanasia, the main legal question will be whether euthanasia is a lawful act or remains an unlawful act for which no one is nevertheless convicted.

Estonian criminal law recognizes several circumstances that exclude the unlawfulness of an act. These include self-defense, necessity, conflicts of duties and so on. Euthanasia could be added to this list, thereby establishing that euthanasia is a lawful termination of life. However, countries generally do not choose this approach.

Instead, they usually take a second approach based on procedural law. In a state governed by the rule of law, only a court can convict someone of a crime. A court can hear a case only if prosecutors bring it before the court. Prosecutors, in turn, receive cases from the police. However, if the police or prosecutors are authorized under certain conditions to discontinue an investigation or refrain from bringing charges, the result is a situation in which no one is convicted in court for ending a person's life.

The conditions that must be met would constitute the substance of euthanasia regulations. If a physician deviates from these conditions, they risk criminal liability for intentional homicide. There is therefore no reason to assume that physicians would engage in euthanasia lightly, since the risk of criminal liability would always remain.

In place of a summary

I believe there are no credible arguments against holding a referendum on whether euthanasia should be permitted. Just as a competition is a celebration for athletes, a referendum is a celebration of democracy. We have not had too many such occasions.

If the public rejects the proposal, the issue should be off the table for about 10 years. If the public supports regulating euthanasia, it could still take another 10 years for the legislation to finally take effect, as the points of contention are virtually endless.

Of course, we can continue to bury our heads in the sand and avoid dealing with the issue. That is what happened with assisted suicide until one individual came along and demonstrated that assisted suicide is legal in Estonia even without specific legislation.

I believe a similar situation could arise with euthanasia. Even now, it is possible to interpret existing laws in such a way that a physician who ends a patient's life at their request to relieve their suffering in a hopeless medical situation could be acquitted in court. However, the law should be made by the legislative branch, not the judiciary. Hopefully, lawmakers will have the sense of responsibility to address the issue.

World.title: Babar Azam shines in DP World ILT20 debut, powering Desert Vipers to first win of Season 5
World.content:
SHARJAH: Defending champions Desert Vipers registered their first win of DP World ILT20 Season 5, beating Sharjah Warriorz by six wickets at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Monday.

Making his DP World ILT20 debut, Babar Azam anchored the chase of 167 with an impressive 86 off 51 balls ¬— including a league record of 13 fours — as the Vipers got over the line in 17.3 overs.

Paul Walter’s 75 off 43 had given the Warriorz a strong platform, but Shadab Khan (3/18) and Khuzaima Tanveer (3/31) led a disciplined bowling effort to bowl them out for 166. Babar’s 86 and a crucial stand with Joe Clarke (35 off 27) then set the Vipers on the path to victory — and their seventh consecutive win over the Warriorz.

The Vipers made a fast start, but Junaid Siddique broke the deadlock in the fourth over, with the wicket of Fakhar Zaman (15 off 10). Waqar Salamkheil struck with his very first ball of the match to bowl Andries Gous (13 off 5) in the seventh over, leaving the Vipers on 70/2 as they looked for a way back into the game.

Babar completed his 50 off just 31 balls in the 10th over. He and Clarke then put on 82 runs for the third wicket, taking the Vipers close to the target.

Adam Milne struck twice in the 16th over with the scalps of Clarke and then Babar. But it was too late for the Warriorz as Shimron Hetmyer (4*) and skipper Shadab Khan (8* off 5) saw the Vipers home with 15 balls to spare.

Earlier, Tom Curran gave the Vipers an early breakthrough in the third over, dismissing Tim Seifert (17 off 9) to leave the Warriorz on 34/1. Walter then took charge, reaching his 50 off 30 balls with a six off Mujeeb Ur Rahman in the 10th over. He and James Vince added 68 runs in 48 balls before Shadab broke the stand in the 11th over, with Vince (23 off 22) caught by Hetmyer.

Shadab struck again in the 13th over, bowling Brandon McMullen (2 off 6) to leave the Warriorz on 122/3. Two balls later he got skipper Sikandar Raza (0 off 2) as well, as the Vipers took control of the innings. Naseem Shah then dismissed the dangerous Walter in the 14th over, making it 128/5.

Tanveer joined the wicket-takers in the 16th over with the wicket of Mohammad Nabi (3 off 8). He claimed his second wicket in the 18th over, and his third in the final over, to ensure that the Warriorz were bowled out for 166.

Player of the Match Azam said: “It’s my first match and the team’s first win. We planned the first six overs, played cricketing shots and stayed positive, and then we built partnerships and the innings. The way our fast bowlers pulled things back was fantastic.”

Warriorz skipper Sikandar Raza said: “We lost momentum in the first half and couldn’t get it back. Our top three were nice to watch, but one spell from Shadab changed the game. The middle order hasn’t fired in this game or the last, so we’re missing runs from the middle and lower order. We thought we’d get the momentum back with the ball, but they had such a brilliant start that by the time we did, it was too late.”

World.title: Oil prices near three-month lows as rising supply offsets Hormuz threat
World.content:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices extended their falls into a second day on Tuesday to trade near three-month lows on signs of rising crude ​supply and a potential market surplus, though risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz ‌persisted.

Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.7 percent, to $88.71 a barrel by 06:10 a.m. Saudi time, after posting their lowest close since Aug. 31 on Monday. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 60 cents, or 0.8 percent, to $79.57 a barrel, after hitting their lowest level since Aug. 26 ​earlier in the session.

“Brent has largely lost any upward impetus in recent days as supply conditions ​remain benign despite the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and the ⁠market weighs the possibility of a future supply glut against persistent Middle East tensions and shipping disruptions,” ​said Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS Bank.

“However, risk of prices going up again cannot be ruled out as ​nothing has moved in US-Iran talks and both parties could move at some point to test the other's resolve in blockading the strait.”

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards navy said three “violating” oil tankers had caught fire after hitting naval mines in the strait on Monday, Iran’s Press ​TV reported.

The US is also investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy ​tankers, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials and others familiar with the matter.

Libya’s Sharara oil pipeline has reopened after ‌an “unlawful ⁠group” had closed a valve on the pipeline, and oil has begun to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the chairperson of the National Oil Corp. told Reuters on Monday.

While better supply is weighing on prices, analysts said the market remained fragile.

“Despite some improvement in inventories and product availability, the ​oil market remains under ​severe strain,” Daniel Hynes, ⁠senior commodity strategist at ANZ, said in a client note.

“Oil prices, time spreads, refining margins and investor positioning increasingly suggest the market expects conditions to normalise. Yet logistics ​remain constrained and inventory buffers are thin. The oil system therefore appears to ​be moving ⁠from acute scarcity towards persistent vulnerability, rather than returning to normal.”

Deutsche Bank said that global observed liquids inventory rose 52 million barrels in October, implying an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels each day. Evidence is accumulating that ⁠the global ​market is rebalancing and turning into surplus, although setbacks could ​delay progress, the bank said in a research report.

US crude oil and product inventories likely rose last week, a preliminary Reuters poll ​showed.

World.title: UAE: 11 Dead in collision between bus and truck in Ras Al Khaimah
World.content:
The UAE Ministry of Interior reported today, Tuesday, that 11 people died in a collision between a passenger bus and a truck in the Emirate of Ras Al Khaimah.

The ministry added in a statement published on the X platform that “upon receiving the report, specialized teams moved to the accident site and began, in cooperation with ambulance and civil defense teams and relevant authorities, rescue and medical operations, in addition to securing the site and organizing traffic.”

The ministry did not specify the identities of the deceased or mention whether there were any other injuries. It added that authorities are investigating to determine the causes of the accident, and the results of the investigations will be announced upon completion.

World.title: Iran carries out flogging of singer and her team, Iranian website says
World.content:
DUBAI: An Iranian ‌singer and four members of her production team have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for “offending public decency by producing and publishing obscene and immoral content online,” an Iranian news website said on Monday.

Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and ‌travel, the Emtedad website ‌quoted lawyer Mostafa Nili ‌as saying. The case followed the release of a video on YouTube in December 2024 showing Ahmadi performing without the mandatory hijab alongside male musicians in Qom, south of the capital Tehran, Norway-based human rights group Hengaw said. Western governments and human rights ‌groups have ‌criticized flogging as torture and a violation of ‌international law. Iran rejects accusations over its ‌human rights record, saying Western countries should focus on their own human rights problems. Iranian authorities did not immediately respond to ‌a request for comment by Reuters.

Rules requiring women to wear the hijab were a flashpoint during protests in 2022 after the death in custody of Kurdish Iranian woman Mahsa Amini, who was arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.

The rules have increasingly been flouted on the streets of Tehran and beyond, and enforcement of the rules has also become more selective.

Emtedad did not specify whether Nili had represented the five defendants.

World.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on December 16 on state carrier
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on December 16, the anniversary of the end of her country’s 1971 liberation war with Pakistan, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday.

It is the first time Hasina has set a specific date for her return, potentially raising political and legal tensions in a country where her party is banned and where violence ‌has risen since she ‌sought a new passport and ‌other documents earlier this month.

In addition to seeking the paperwork, canceled months after she fled to Delhi following a deadly uprising against her, Hasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines.

“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon ‌the government to arrange for ‌her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesperson, ‌Syed Mozammel Ali, said in a statement. “Having exiled ‌her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on December 16th.”

A Bangladeshi ‌government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina, who faces a death sentence, would be arrested and jailed on return, and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back.

The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power. Bangladesh’s war crimes court sentenced her to death in November last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising, though she has denied the charges from exile.

World.title: Singapore investigating Nvidia-linked Megaspeed after US blacklisting
World.content:
SYDNEY: Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Tuesday that his country would continue to investigate cloud company Megaspeed, an Nvidia-linked firm alleged by US authorities to have diverted advanced AI chips to China.

The US Commerce Department on Monday added Singapore-based Megaspeed to its trade blacklist, following criticism from US lawmakers and Trump administration officials.

“If there are companies that are caught breaching our laws, we will certainly take very firm enforcement actions. So it’s on that basis that we were investigating Megaspeed,” ‌Wong said at ‌a press conference in Canberra, where he is ‌on an official visit. “These investigations into Megaspeed are ongoing on American side, on the Singapore side we are focusing on whether Megaspeed might have breached any Singapore laws,” he said, adding Singapore was continuing discussions with US authorities on the issue.

US and Singaporean law enforcement conducted an “on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed” in June 2025 and interviewed Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman and former CEO of Megaspeed who is accused of ‌having ties with Beijing, the Commerce ‌and Justice departments said earlier this month. Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that has ‌been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether ‌it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the US Commerce Department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.

Singapore had previously investigated Alice Huang, but found no basis for prosecution, Wong said.

“We ‌took her in, we investigated her, but we eventually released her because there was no basis for further prosecution,” he said.

Reuters has been unable to determine Alice Huang’s whereabouts to seek comment. Megaspeed did not immediately return a request for comment. A week ago, the company issued a statement saying it conducts legitimate and lawful business, including complying with US export controls.

Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, a stunning reversal following his resignation over allegations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang.

Wong was speaking at a joint press conference with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, where the two nations signed an agreement to expand cooperation on securing “essential supplies,” including food, pharmaceuticals, medical products and agricultural inputs.

World.title: Brentford hit Everton for four to soar into Premier League top six
World.content:
LONDON: Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League’s top six on Monday.

Lewis-Potter’s luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match.

Vitaly Janelt’s stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday.

“It’ll probably go a bit under the radar because of the sending off but 11 versus 11 we were outstanding,” said Brentford boss Keith Andrews.

“I’m really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue.

“Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we’re really looking forward to it.”

David Moyes’s record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table.

“With two shots, both deflected in and took the goalkeeper the wrong way, and the third goal was a worldie outside the box. We could use them as excuses but there’s no excuses tonight,” said Moyes.

“The performance was way below the standards we’ve set and the way we’ve been playing recently.”

A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford.

Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally.

The winger’s first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself toward the ball.

Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin.

Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday’s Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool.

Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago.

Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt’s strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half.

The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time.

Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute.

Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils.

United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years.

World.title: Russian cargo ship under tow after being hit by drones arrives in St Petersburg
World.content:
A ‌Russian cargo ship under tow after being struck by drones in the ​Gulf of Finland arrived in St Petersburg on Monday, the regional governor said.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of Leningrad Region, wrote on Telegram that both the Sparta II ‌ship and its ‌16-member crew ​had arrived ‌in ⁠the ​port.

The crew ⁠had been evacuated, first onto lifeboats, then to a nearby Russian ship, after the vessel was hit by drones on Saturday and caught ⁠fire. Drozdenko said there ‌were ‌no injuries.

The Finnish military ​has said ‌the strike on the ‌Sparta II was likely carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters.

In ‌a rare instance of cross-border collaboration, out of ⁠the seven ⁠vessels helping to fight the fire, two were Russian, two were Estonian and the rest were Finnish.

Ukraine has made no official comment on the incident.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv's forces had sunk a Russian naval ​corvette ​at the Libyan port of Benghazi using maritime drones on Sunday.

World.title: Baghdad welcomes Arab leaders as Al Zaidi wraps up Cairo talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government formally opened Baghdad’s doors to Arab heads of state and representatives of pan-Arab organizations on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, just hours after Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi concluded his visit to the League of Arab States headquarters in Cairo.

In statements to the official newspaper, Government Spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi revealed that Al-Zaidi’s talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi focused heavily on coordinating bilateral efforts to ward off economic risks and mitigate the fallout inflicted on regional economies by the ongoing war.

Al-Aboudi also confirmed that the Prime Minister extended a direct invitation to the Grand Imam of Al-Azhar to visit Baghdad to foster deeper institutional communication and promote a moderate religious discourse between Iraq and Egypt.

Characterizing Cairo as a pivotal stop in Baghdad’s broader foreign policy of balanced international engagement, Al-Aboudi noted that Al-Zaidi’s diplomatic outreach has previously spanned Washington, Paris, Berlin, and several Arab and Gulf capitals.

He emphasized that Iraq’s diplomacy prioritizes Arab economic integration and the activation of joint Arab action mechanisms to safeguard regional sovereignty and resources.

Addressing Al-Zaidi’s appearance at the Arab League headquarters and meetings with member-state representatives, Al-Aboudi stated that Iraq’s historical founding role in the institution motivated the visit, underscoring Baghdad’s determination to strengthen its Arab presence and help confront shared regional threats.

Welcoming Arab leaders, prominent figures, and active regional organizations to convene in Baghdad, Al-Aboudi concluded that the Cairo summit reflects Iraq’s commitment to consolidating Arab ties and expanding joint cooperation in support of regional stability.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt agree to lift entry visa requirements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Egypt have reached an agreement to cancel entry visa requirements between the two countries.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced the decision on Monday during a joint press conference with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi at Ittihadiya Palace in the Egyptian capital, Cairo.

The visa waiver aims to facilitate the movement of citizens and boost tourism, trade, and political ties between both countries.

The announcement came alongside the fourth session of the Iraq-Egypt Higher Joint Committee, where officials discussed agreements covering energy, oil supplies, transportation, investment, and regional security.

While the agreement has been officially announced by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), it is still unclear when the exemption will go into effect, how long visitors may stay, and whether security checks would still be required.

Travelers should check with their respective foreign ministries or airlines before booking immediate visa-free travel.

World.title: Iraqi Airways to sell two 1982 Boeing 747s parked in Tunisia since 1991
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Airways published on Wednesday an official direct-sale notice for two 1982 Boeing 747 aircraft that have been parked at Nefta International Airport in Tozeur, Tunisia, since January 1991.

Both airplanes were built in 1982. One is originally configured as a VIP government transport used during Saddam Hussein’s rule, and the other is a convertible passenger-and-cargo airliner.

The two aircraft are equipped with Pratt & Whitney JT9D-7F engines.

Each aircraft is valued at $900,000, or $1.8 million for the pair, an 82 percent increase over an unsuccessful 2023 auction attempt priced at $494,000 per jet.

Shortlisted bidders must provide a 20 percent deposit per aircraft. The buyer must also pay a two percent service fee,  publication costs, ownership transfer, customs clearance, transport, taxes, and any parking fees accumulated after handover.

Both planes are sold strictly “as is” on the ramp in Tozeur with no technical warranty or guarantee of airworthiness.

Companies or individuals can submit offers for one or both aircraft to a sales committee at the Iraqi Embassy in Tunisia between December 21, 2026, and January 5, 2027. Selected buyers have five days to pay the full balance, and any final sale requires the approval of the Iraqi minister of transport.

The two jets were flown to southern Tunisia in January 1991 to shield them from coalition airstrikes ahead of the Gulf War.

International sanctions, legal disputes, and decades of unpaid storage fees kept them grounded.

Iraq previously settled roughly $5.4 million in accumulated parking debts with Tunisian authorities in 2020, and unlike the 2023 sale attempt, the current notice removes earlier restrictions that required the airplanes to be scrapped or barred political use.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Egyptian president co-chair expanded meeting in Cairo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi co-chaired an expanded meeting between the delegations of the two countries on Monday at the Ittihadiya Palace in Cairo.

The two sides discussed mechanisms to strengthen and develop bilateral relations, particularly in the economic, trade, and investment areas to fulfill the aspirations of the people in both countries.

The two leaders also addressed coordination on regional and international issues of mutual concern, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Egyptian president and Iraqi prime minister held a joint press conference where al-Zaidi highlighted the distinguished economic relations between the two countries and the mutual commitment to promote these ties in different sectors.

According to al-Zaidi, a series of measures have been adopted to bolster cooperation between Iraq and Egypt.

Iraq is open to the Arab world, seeking strong relations that are based on cooperation and mutual interests, according to the Iraqi prime minister.

Al-Zaidi underlined that Iraq and Egypt have similar political positions and a shared strategy for creating regional security, reducing tensions, and resolving conflicts through communication to maintain regional and international stability.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Egypt coincides with the fourth session of the Joint Higher Committee between the two countries.

The Egyptian president commended Iraq’s positions that support peace, as well as its efforts to prioritize dialogue and avoid escalation to achieve stability in the region.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Egyptian president discuss bilateral ties, regional issues
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi met at Cairo’s al-Ittihadiya Palace on Monday to expand economic cooperation and coordinate diplomatic efforts on regional security.

The discussions coincide with the fourth session of the joint higher committee, which al-Zaidi is co-chairing alongside Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly.

The trip marks al-Zaidi’s first official visit to Egypt since taking office in May 2026.

Baghdad and Cairo are negotiating a potential supply of 10 million barrels of Iraqi crude to Egypt, alongside alternative export paths that bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

In addition to discussions for establishing an Iraqi Rafidain Bank branch in Cairo, the two countries are negotiating new agreements pertaining to commerce, transportation, and finance.

In 2024, the volume of trade exchange between Iraq and Egypt totaled $1.1 billion.

While both parties talked about increasing the participation of Egyptian companies in Iraq’s infrastructure development, al-Zaidi proposed additional initiatives to attract investment.

To handle wider regional issues, such as security risks involving Iran, Yemen, and Red Sea commerce routes, al-Zaidi and el-Sisi emphasized the importance of dialogue.

Al-Zaidi is expected to meet with Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy while in Cairo and speak to representatives of member states to promote joint Arab action.

World.title: Ninth Erbil International Food, Packaging, and Plastics Exhibition opens with 286 companies
World.content:
Erbil (IrraqiNews.com) – The ninth edition of the Erbil International Food, Packaging, and Plastics Exhibition opened on Monday, November 23, 2026, bringing together 286 local and international companies from 20 countries.

Speaking at the opening ceremony attended by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Erbil Governor Omed Khoshnaw stated that the Erbil International Fair serves as a premier hub for showcasing domestic goods and attracting foreign enterprises, ranking first among trade exhibitions across Iraq.

Khoshnaw noted that strong domestic and international corporate participation reflects ongoing stability and economic growth in Erbil and the broader Kurdistan Region, emphasizing that supporting local manufacturing remains a central pillar of the Kurdistan Regional Government’s strategic agenda alongside steady annual growth in registered production firms coordinated with the Investment Board and relevant ministries.

Exhibition spokesperson Hoshmand Mohammed told INA that the ninth edition features broad international representation across specialized food processing, packaging, and plastics sectors.

He added that the event provides a vital commercial platform to introduce Iraqi-made products to global firms while giving domestic businesses and citizens direct access to the latest international food technologies and product lines, noting that the exhibition opens daily to visitors from across all Iraqi governorates starting at 11:00 AM.

World.title: Iraq considers exporting 10 million barrels of oil to Egypt
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is currently studying a proposal to supply Egypt with approximately 10 million barrels of crude oil.

The potential shipment is a primary topic during Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s official visit to Cairo, which coincides with the fourth session of the Iraqi-Egyptian Joint Higher Committee.

According to Iraqi Deputy Minister of Trade Sattar al-Jabiri, the 10-million-barrel supply is still being considered. There have been no confirmed or declared delivery dates, shipment timetables, or payment arrangements.

Finding other export routes to avoid the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping has experienced increased security hazards, is one of the important topics of the discussions taking place in Cairo.

In addition to oil, al-Zaidi and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi are overseeing bilateral memoranda of understanding (MoUs) pertaining to commerce, transportation, and the possible reactivation of Iraq’s Rafidain Bank branch in Cairo.

The fourth session of the Joint Higher Committee aims to build on cooperation agreements signed previously, while both nations continue advancing regional integration through the Egypt-Iraq-Jordan trilateral cooperation mechanism.

Additionally, al-Zaidi’s official trip to Egypt aims to promote bilateral ties and expand Egyptian corporate participation in Iraqi infrastructure.

World.title: Iraqi Atomic Energy Commission outlines 10-year roadmap for peaceful nuclear reactor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Atomic Energy Commission announced on Monday, November 23, 2026, that constructing a peaceful nuclear reactor will take roughly seven to ten years, confirming that authorities are preparing to launch immediate preparatory steps—including specialized workforce training, laboratory construction, and radiopharmaceutical projects—ahead of full-scale reactor operations.

In statements to the official newspaper, Murtadha Adhab, Iraq’s National Liaison Officer with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), emphasized that peaceful nuclear applications span agriculture, industry, education, and broader sectoral development.

He highlighted the practical role of radioactive materials in sterilizing medical supplies and preserving agricultural seeds over extended storage periods to prevent spoilage.

Rather than delaying progress until a reactor is fully built, Adhab explained that the commission is actively coordinating with relevant state institutions to bring near-term strategic projects into execution.

Foremost among these is a radiopharmacy initiative focused on producing medical radioisotopes. Under the commission’s phased roadmap, initial efforts will prioritize qualifying technical personnel, establishing specialized laboratories, and initiating radioisotope fractionation processes before transitioning to full domestic isotope production once the reactor comes online.

Adhab underscored that Iraq’s nuclear reactor and all associated atomic energy programs are strictly dedicated to peaceful purposes. He noted that this commitment is firmly enshrined in the Iraqi Constitution and governed by domestic legislation as well as the international treaties and IAEA safeguards agreements ratified by Baghdad.

World.content:
With the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections approaching,

(SP) president

is set to release the party's election manifesto on Thursday, coinciding with

. Titled the 'Jan-Man Manifesto' (Manifesto of the People), the document will be presented as the party's 'PDA Pranpatra', with a focus on constitutional protection, democracy, reservation and social justice.

The manifesto, reportedly prepared under the supervision of former Uttar Pradesh chief secretary Alok Ranjan, is expected to outline the party's commitments on employment, education, reservation and welfare measures for women, young people and marginalised communities. The party is also planning separate region-specific and district-level manifestos to take its proposals to voters at the grassroots level.



The PDA, a political formulation promoted by Yadav, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities). The SP has indicated that releasing its manifesto months before the polls will allow it to take its proposals to the public ahead of the election campaign.

He added that the 'Jan-Man Manifesto' would be released on the "democratic and sacred occasion" of Constitution Day.

The manifesto announcement comes amid a series of attacks by Yadav on the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over governance and election preparedness.
