NEW DELHI: Chemical contaminants detected in a batch of packaged drinking water manufactured by Bisleri at its Goa facility has raised concerns over potential health risks, including kidney damage and cancer.Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) reportedly declared the sample unsafe after tests flagged bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Bisleri, however, has disputed the findings, maintaining that its water is safe for consumption.Dr Tanmay Pandya, HoD and director, Nephrology and Renal Transplantation, Sarvodaya Hospital, Faridabad, said prolonged exposure to certain chemical contaminants could affect kidney function, depending on their concentration and duration of exposure. "Bromate is a chemical of concern because of its potential carcinogenic properties," he said, adding that certain heavy metals and industrial chemicals could also interfere with kidney function.In a statement issued Monday, Bisleri said FSSAI collected six samples from its Goa manufacturing facility on Sept 30, 2025.While five met the applicable standards, the sixth recorded bromate at 12 micrograms per litre against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre, the company said in a statement.Following an appeal, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory in Nov 2025. Bisleri said the laboratory found bromate within the prescribed limit but separately flagged PAHs. The company subsequently got the sample tested at an FSSAI-approved independent laboratory, which also found bromate within the prescribed limit.Bisleri said it submitted the independent laboratory results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office on Feb 2, 2026, but received no further communication. It also claimed it had not received the reported notice by email or in hard copy.The company said it follows a 10-stage purification process, conducts over 90 quality tests and will cooperate with FSSAI.Explaining the contamination concerns, Dr Saurabh Arora, MD of Auriga Research, said packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are regulated under separate standards. Bromate can form during water treatment, while PAHs may enter through packaging or contamination during bottling.

World.title: Bangladeshi court orders interim curbs on social media access for children under 16
World.content:
The court issued the directives Sunday while passing an order on a writ petition

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

DHAKA: Bangladeshi court has directed the authorities to frame mandatory interim guidelines to prevent children below 16 years of age from accessing social media platforms and ordered the formation of an independent expert committee to examine the impact of algorithm-driven content feeds on minors.The High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh issued the directives on Sunday while passing an order on a writ petition that questioned the government's failure to formulate a national policy regulating social media access for children under 16, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.The bench comprising Justices Sikder Mahmudur Razi and Fatema Anwar directed the Secretary of the Posts and Telecommunications Division and the Chairman of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission, among other respondents, to take necessary steps.It also ordered the immediate formation of a committee comprising cybersecurity specialists, child psychologists, paediatricians and legal experts to assess the structural impact of algorithm-controlled feeds on children.The move comes amid growing international concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health, physical well-being and development, with governments across the globe increasingly considering age-based restrictions and stricter safeguards against potentially harmful online content.The committee will examine how algorithm-based recommendation systems influence children's behaviour, exposure to online content and overall development, and submit its assessment to help shape regulatory measures.The writ petition was filed earlier this month by Supreme Court lawyer Mohammad Faisal Dastagir, who appeared before the court in person.The absence of a regulatory framework had left children below 16 exposed to unrestricted social media use, potentially affecting their mental and physical development, Dastagir was quoted as saying by Prothom Alo.Citing research highlighting health concerns, including impaired eyesight, among children exposed to excessive screen time, he argued that a national policy was necessary to regulate their access to social media.The court also directed the authorities to explain why their failure to establish an independent committee to assess the structural impact of algorithm-controlled feeds on minors and formulate a national policy restricting social media access for children under 16 should not be declared illegal and beyond their lawful authority, the report said.Several countries across the world are tightening regulations governing children's access to social media.Australia became the first country to enforce a minimum age of 16 for accounts on major social media platforms in December 2025, requiring platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent under-16s from creating or retaining accounts.Indonesia banned children under 16 from having accounts on "high-risk" social media and online platforms starting on March 28, 2026, making it the first country in Southeast Asia to introduce such restrictions.Malaysia, too, began enforcing age-verification requirements in June 2026, barring children below 16 from opening social media accounts and requiring existing users to verify their age.The UK plans to ban children under 16 from major social media platforms starting in spring 2027, with initial regulations expected to be laid before Parliament by December 2026. It is also considering overnight curfews for teens aged 16 and 17 and blocking infinite-scroll mechanisms for kids.Canada introduced a bill in parliament in June, proposing a minimum age of 16 for holding social media accounts. The proposed legislation is yet to become law.Brazil enacted rules in 2026 requiring age verification and parental account linking for users under 16.The European Commission has proposed the EU KIDS Act in September to ban children under 13 from social media and set 15 as the minimum age for independent accounts.Countries such as France, Greece, Turkey, Spain, Poland, New Zealand, Denmark, and Slovenia have drafted restrictions aimed primarily at under-15s, while Austria has proposed an under-14 ban.

World.title: Detail grounds for cancelling UK journalist's OCI card: HC to govt
World.content:
Justice Amit Mahajan passed the order on Wilsonâs plea challenging Centreâs 2023 decision to cancel her OCI card

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has said the Centre's showcause notice and order cancelling the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card of UK-based journalist Amrit Wilson did not specify her anti-India activities. It directed authorities to issue a fresh notice on the grounds.Justice Amit Mahajan passed the order on Wilson's plea challenging Centre's 2023 decision to cancel her OCI card. On Nov 19, HC directed authorities to issue a fresh showcause notice with specific details within a week and allowed Wilson another week to respond. Authorities would then pass an order.It clarified that the existing cancellation order would remain in operation for four weeks or until a fresh order was passed, whichever was earlier.It observed that the lack of specific details had denied Wilson an opportunity to explain her position, and even Centre's reply lacked specific reasons. The court said the notice and order did not detail the alleged anti-India activities, adding that principles of natural justice had not been followed.If the authorities could not spell out specific reasons in the fresh notice, they should provide Wilson with the "gist of the material" while redacting sensitive information or allow her to inspect it, the court said.Centre cancelled Wilson's OCI card in 2023, alleging that she had engaged in "detrimental propaganda against govt". Wilson contended the cancellation order was arbitrary.

World.title: PM Modi is Asia's second-most effective leader after Xi, says Lowy Institute's power index
World.content:
According to the index, âdiplomatic influenceâ was Indiaâs strongest measure

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi climbed three places to rank as Asia's second-most effective leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to the 2026 Asia Power Index released by Lowy Institute.According to the index, 'diplomatic influence' was India's strongest measure and held steady in a year when most countries faltered. One of the notable findings of the latest index was the improvement in the assessment of Modi's regional leadership.The Lowy Institute's expert survey rated Modi more highly for his effectiveness in advancing India's diplomatic interests in Asia. The assessment comes despite a relatively subdued Indian diplomatic profile during the Gulf conflict, which the report said weighed on perceptions of his global leadership and strategic ambition.The 2026 findings point to a more prominent Indian role in an increasingly competitive Asian strategic landscape, even as the US and China continue to dominate the regional power structure.India's gains have been driven by a combination of diplomatic engagement, regional security cooperation, investment attractiveness, cultural influence and demographic prospects. Its ability to maintain economic relationships even as regional conditions weakened also helped support its overall position.India's membership in diplomatic forums was up two places to joint second. India was represented in 17 of the summits, diplomatic clubs and regional inter-governmental organisations Lowy tracks, level with Indonesia and Thailand and only one behind China.

World.title: 22 lakh pleas to include names in West Bengal rolls top priority: SC to EC
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Monday said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll, and sought the state govt's response to allegations that voters deleted during SIR are being denied ration and benefits under various social welfare schemes.

The court also said even among the 22 lakh, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation should be heard ahead of others, keeping in view the upcoming civic elections.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the Calcutta HC chief justice in consultation with

must increase the number of tribunals - currently 19 - to deal with the 38 lakh appeals, filed on deletion of 90 lakh voters declared absent, shifted, duplicate or dead, or flagged for 'logical discrepancy', related to mapping.



The bench also asked Election Commission to requisition additional space for housing the tribunals at various places to facilitate easy access to appellants.

SC's direction came after advocate Prashant Bhushan told SC that of the 1.4 lakh appeals decided so far by tribunals, which were appointed to adjudicate a large number of appeals filed after SIR, more than 90% have been allowed leading to restoration of their names in the electoral roll.





This is a strong indicator based on a large sample size to persuade the top court to direct that those who have filed appeals against deletion of their names should be allowed to vote in the coming elections, Bhushan said.

Supreme Court said this was the reason for it to ask for prioritisation of appeals for restoration of names relating to various wards in KMC.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Bhushan, supported by senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan, told the apex court that even though the court had categorically clarified that deletion of names from electoral roll would not have any consequence, including with regard to citizenship, beyond the chance to vote, state govt has been denying the deleted voters ration through public distribution system (PDS) and benefits under social welfare schemes, including Annapurna Yojna.

Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said these are bald assertions and alleged that the petitioners have not cited a single example to substantiate their claims.

However, the CJI-led bench asked state govt to file response to the allegations.

In a related issue, SC postponed to Wednesday hearing on state govt's appeal challenging an interim order of a division bench of Calcutta HC restraining the state EC from announcing schedule for KMC polls, in which the number of wards were increased from 144 to 209 by an amending Act. Mehta said the high court mistakenly concluded that state govt lacked the jurisdiction to carry out the exercise of increasing the number of wards and resultant adjustment of ward boundaries.

World.title: FDA suspends licences of British Brewing Company, NSCI; fines Mumbai University canteen ₹1 lakh over hygiene violations
World.content:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food licences of several prominent establishments, including British Brewing Company in Lower Parel and the National Sports Club of India (NSCI) in Worli, and fined the University of Mumbai’s Fort campus canteen ₹1 lakh for food safety violations.

Also Read: Food and Drug Administration seizes 20,085 litres of oil in Pune over violations of standards

The action was part of a statewide enforcement drive, during which licences and registration certificates of 27 food establishments were suspended, banned food products worth ₹34.56 lakh were seized, and four FIRs were registered, the FDA said on Monday (November 23, 2026).

Of the 27 establishments facing suspension, six are located in Mumbai and 21 in the Pune division. Inspections revealed serious violations of hygiene and sanitation norms, including pest infestations, improper food storage, inadequate waste disposal and failure to maintain mandatory food safety records.

At British Brewing Company in Lower Parel, FDA inspectors found live flies in a bag of flour and a large number of cockroaches near a drain clogged with food waste. Vegetables and other food items were stored improperly in refrigerators, several products lacked expiry labels, and rusted utensils were found on the premises. The restaurant’s food licence was suspended with immediate effect on November 21.

Also Read: FDA suspends 105 licences, cancels 7 across Maharashtra after pre-Deepavali checks

Similarly, an inspection at the NSCI in Worli revealed flies in the main kitchen, cockroaches near washbasins, accumulated food waste and improper storage of raw materials. Inspectors also found open dustbins near food preparation areas, deteriorating walls and ceilings, and food handlers working without gloves. Its food licence was suspended on November 23.

The FDA also imposed and recovered a fine of ₹1 lakh from the vendor operating the University of Mumbai’s Fort campus canteen after finding multiple food safety violations. The canteen was found operating without a valid food business licence or registration.

According to the department, food was stored improperly in refrigerators, creating a risk of cross-contamination, while overflowing dustbins were kept near food storage areas. Inspectors also found utensils placed directly on the floor, inadequate segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, damaged kitchen flooring and open drains. Mandatory records relating to food purchases, staff training, medical examinations and pest control were unavailable.

Among the other Mumbai establishments facing suspension were Curefoods India Limited’s Crusto’s — Cheese Burst Pizza by Olio outlet in Prabhadevi — Velvet Fine Chocolates and Shane-Ilahi Bakery and Store in Govandi, and Maratha Chicken Suppliers in Borivali East.

At the Crusto’s outlet, inspectors found accumulated food waste, improper drainage and inadequate segregation of raw and cooked food. Cockroaches were found in the manufacturing area of Velvet Fine Chocolates, where a toilet was also located within the production area. At Maratha Chicken Suppliers, inspectors found inadequate refrigeration facilities, unhygienic storage conditions and deficiencies in waste disposal.

In Pune division, the FDA suspended licences and registrations of 21 establishments for serious violations of hygiene norms. These included Metro Restaurant, Grand Delhi Darbar Hospitality, The Burger Barn Cafe, Chaitanya Parathas and an Instamart establishment operated by Rajdhi Retail Pvt. Ltd., among other restaurants and food outlets across Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad.

Separately, the FDA conducted raids against the sale, storage and transportation of banned food products, including gutkha, pan masala and scented tobacco, across Mumbai, Amravati and Nashik divisions.

The largest seizure was reported from Amravati division, where banned food products worth ₹34.53 lakh were confiscated. One person was arrested, two establishments were sealed and a vehicle valued at ₹21 lakh was seized.

In Mumbai, two FIRs were registered following seizures of banned food products worth ₹2,616 in Antop Hill and ₹2,750 in Tilaknagar. Another FIR was registered in Kalwan in Nashik district, where banned products worth ₹651 were seized. The fourth FIR was registered in Amravati division.

In Thane district, FDA officials seized expired and spoiled food products worth approximately ₹39,862 from M.K. Traders in Bhiwandi. Suspected substandard areca nut (supari) was also seized in a separate operation.

FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said the administration would continue taking strict action against establishments violating food safety regulations.

“Playing with public health will not be tolerated at all. Access to pure food is the right of every citizen,” Mr. Mundhe said, adding that enforcement against food adulteration and banned substances would continue.

The FDA urged citizens to report suspected food adulteration and quality violations through its toll-free helpline, 1800222365, or its online grievance portal.

World.title: Thirupparankundram row LIVE: Tamil Nadu town on high alert on Karthigai Deepam day
World.content:
A Supreme Court Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi had ordered the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the ‘Deepathoon’ on Thiruparankundram Hill on November 24, 2026, coinciding with Karthigai Deepam. The court described the direction as a “temporary, one-time arrangement.” The interim order addressed the State’s plea to stay the January 6 judgment. The ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon is slated for 6 p.m.

Also read | Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement

The Madurai City Police tightened security across the hill on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The police declared areas around Thiruparankundram a “red zone”, banning the use of drones and unmanned aerial vehicles on. Hundreds of personnel have been deployed around the hill, which houses the Subramaniya Swamy Temple, to prevent unauthorised access to the hilltop where the Deepathoon is located.

Also read | Deepathoon row: Tamil Nadu files a review plea in Supreme Court against Thirupparankundram order

At the foothills of Thiruparankundram Hill stands the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Murugan, while the summit is home to the Sikandar Badusha Dargah, a Muslim shrine. The Deepathoon is located around 50 metres from the dargah. The dispute centres on whether the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp should also be lit at this pillar.

World.title: BJP hits out at Rahul Gandhi, says person filled with hatred towards country won't be accepted by people
World.content:
The BJP on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks against the Indian economy and electoral system during foreign visits, saying he may try to relaunch his political career from foreign soil but would never be accepted by the people of the country.

As several BJP leaders offered prayers at gurudwaras and performed community service on the occasion of Parkash Purab, they also pledged to work towards making the country, particularly Punjab, drug-free and hit out at opposition parties for allegedly failing to do enough to tackle the menace.

The birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev is being observed on November 24.

After offering prayers along with other BJP leaders at a gurudwara here, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari told reporters that this pious occasion should also be used to pledge to make Punjab and the entire country free of drugs.

He further said the Lowy Institute's Asia Power Index had stated that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership, India had emerged as one of Asia's leading powers.

"Goldman Sachs and the IMF have also described India as the fastest-growing major economy," he said.

Taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, Mr. Bhandari said, "He may make every effort to relaunch his political career from foreign soil, but a person whose every fibre is filled with hatred towards the country will never be accepted by its people."

"That is why the people of India will not accept Rahul Gandhi," he added.

India improved its score by 0.5, reaching 40.5, which marks the narrowest gap since 2018 between its score and China's, which stands at 73.6, as per the Lowy Institute metric.

The report said India has consolidated its position as the third-most powerful country and a "major powerhouse" in Asia, with Prime Minister Modi rated as the second-most effective regional leader.

According to the Index, the U.S. and China are "superpowers in Asia for 2026", with the U.S.' score being the highest, at 78.9.

Mr. Gandhi had triggered a political row with his remarks on India's economy during an address at Columbia University in the U.S.

India is sitting on an "economic disaster" with massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep-rooted problems in its education system, Mr. Gandhi said, warning that the country risks getting into serious trouble if it continues on the current economic path.

Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University last week, Mr. Gandhi said India's economic model "stopped giving results almost a decade ago" and criticised the Government's initiatives such as 'Make in India' and 'Start-up India', claiming they had failed to revive the country's "broken" economic backbone.

World.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
World.content:
Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.

U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.”

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement.

Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO: 6 other CEOs who reclaimed their top positions

The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”

Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart".

Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused.

Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.

U.S. intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.

Board chair Harvey Jones said on Monday (November 23, 2026) that directors now believe Mr. Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers.

Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO.

Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Mr. Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said.

World.title: President Murmu to inaugurate Bali Jatra in Cuttack during two-day Odisha visit
World.content:
President Droupadi Murmu will arrive in Odisha on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon on a two-day visit, during which she will inaugurate the Bali Jatra festival in Cuttack and attend a national convention on homoeopathy in Bhubaneswar, officials said.

After arriving at the Biju Patnaik International Airport in Bhubaneswar, Ms. Murmu will proceed to Lok Bhavan before travelling to Cuttack to inaugurate the annual trade fair this evening, they said.

She will stay overnight at Lok Bhavan and attend the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday (November 25).

Security has been tightened in the twin cities of Bhubaneswar and Cuttack ahead of the President's visit.

DGP Vinaytosh Mishra reviewed security arrangements at the Bali Jatra ground in Cuttack on Monday (November 23).

Around 70 platoons of police personnel will be deployed to manage security and crowd movement, he said.

Police have also set up 38 watchtowers and installed 1,400 CCTV cameras at the venue, another official said.

In Bhubaneswar, arrangements have been made to ensure smooth traffic movement. Traffic restrictions will be imposed for brief periods to facilitate the movement of the President's convoy, he said.

World.title: Customs seize 11 dismantled air rifles at Kochi airport
World.content:
The Customs have seized 11 air rifles of different models in dismantled condition, along with accessories, from two passengers at the Cochin International Airport in Keralam.

The items were recovered from Ramesh Machat and Sijoy Sasi, who arrived from Dubai. The rifles were taken for technical examination.

The rifles, which were allegedly being smuggled into India, had been dismantled into different parts and concealed in the passengers’ luggage.

World.title: Punjab Assembly polls: BJP-SAD to hold joint presser today
World.content:
As the political climate heats up ahead of next year’s Assembly polls in Punjab, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are set to hold a joint press conference in New Delhi today (November 24, 2026).

Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal will address the meeting at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi at 1 p.m.

While no further information is available on the subject of the presser, it is widely anticipated that the two parties will provide details on the alliance for the Punjab Assembly polls. Negotiations on seat-sharing between the BJP and the SAD for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls have been underway.

The SAD had snapped its 24-year-old alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the now-scrapped three farm laws.

Earlier, Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal was also part of the Modi government as a Minister with Cabinet rank.

Last month in Delhi, Shah had predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027. When he came to Chandigarh on November 1, he again said an NDA government will be formed in the border State.

The statement reignited the buzz about a possible SAD-BJP alliance.

On November 2, when SAD president Badal was asked about the possibility of a re-alliance, he gave a guarded response to speculation, saying, "You will come to know in a few days as to what will happen".

He reiterated that, except for the Congress and the AAP, he is open to an alliance with other parties which accept his party's philosophy.

In the 2022 Assembly polls, the BJP won two seats, and the SAD could register victories in three Assembly segments out of a total of 117.

Prior to the end of the electoral alliance, both the Akalis and the BJP used to contest together. As per the previous pact in the Assembly polls, the BJP used to contest 23 seats and the SAD 94 Assembly seats.

In parliamentary polls, the SAD used to fight for 10 seats and the BJP the remaining three.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from woman IAS officer over Kallakurichi TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told
World.content:
State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh of misbehaving with her, as widely reported in the media over the past few days.

Also read: Collector files complaint against Kallakurichi TVK MLA

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer.

When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case.

“Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?”

The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.”

On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.”

‘Won’t interfere if there’s no plaint’

Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.”

After taking note of the SPP’s submission that the State was willing to file an affidavit before the court making it clear that neither the police nor the Chief Secretary had received any complaint from the woman IAS officer, the judge asked Mr. Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any complaint.

World.title: Hema Malini remembers ‘backbone’ Dharmendra on first death anniversary: ‘He was my existence’
World.content:
Veteran actor Dharmendra died on November 24 last year, two weeks before his 90th birthday. On his first death anniversary today, his wife, actor-politician Hema Malini shared an emotional post on social media. In the post, Hema called Dharmendra her ‘backbone’, and opened up about the grief that hasn’t lost its intensity. Along with the heartfelt note, the actor also shared a few unseen pictures with the late icon.



Taking to her Instagram handle, Hema Malini posted a carousel of beautiful photos of herself with Dharmendra. Along with the post, she penned a moving caption, in which she called the late actor her ‘existence’. “A whole year has sped by but my grief has not lost its intensity I grieve over the tremendous and irreparable loss of a man who was not just my husband – he was my everything – my friend, philosopher and guide who was my backbone and in short, was my very existence,” it read.

World.title: Calcutta High Court upholds SBI employee’s dismissal for mishandling customer accounts
World.content:
Observing that even when the bank suffers no financial loss, a bank employee can’t escape disciplinary action simply by refunding the money involved in misconduct, the Calcutta High Court recently upheld the dismissal of a State Bank of India (SBI) employee accused of repeatedly mishandling customers’ accounts.

Justice Partha Sarathi Chatterjee was hearing a plea filed by a bank employee challenging the bank’s decision to remove him from service after he was held guilty of irregularities in handling customers’ accounts and transactions in a departmental enquiry.

“The obligation of a bank employee to maintain integrity and adhere to prescribed norms does not depend upon whether the bank has ultimately suffered any monetary loss. The safeguards governing the operation of customers’ accounts are intended to protect not only the bank’s interests but also the money entrusted to it by its customers. A subsequent refund or adjustment cannot retrospectively legitimise an unauthorised transaction,” the November 20 order read.



The high court also said that the “real test” was whether the man had done his duties with “the degree of integrity, care and diligence” expected from an employee responsible for the handling of customers’ money.

The man claimed that he was working at an SBI branch as a Customer Assistant and was accused of committing several “irregularities”, which included double-debiting Rs 1,000 from a customer’s account, transferring Rs 7,000 from his father’s account without proper authorisation, paying Rs 6,000 without verifying a customer’s signature, transferring Rs 60,000 without the required authorisation, and failing to credit a customer’s deposit of Rs 6,000.

The man stated that the transactions were either genuine mistakes or carried out with proper instructions and that the customers were eventually refunded. The man alleged that the bank sought explanations from him and, without properly considering the explanation, suspended him in January 2015.

In April 2015, the bank issued a chargesheet containing six allegations of major misconduct, and the man challenged the proceedings, claiming the chargesheet was vague and didn’t initially include the required documents and witness lists.



During the departmental enquiry, the man denied the allegations and explained the circumstances behind each transaction but was eventually found guilty of five of the six charges. In December 2015, the Disciplinary Authority removed him from service, and his appeal against his removal was also rejected in March 2016.

The man then approached the high court, arguing that the enquiry was unfair, his explanations had not been properly considered, and that the punishment was excessive.

‘Disciplinary proceedings’

Senior advocate Sardar Amjad Ali and advocate Arun Kr Das, appearing for the man, argued that the bank could not impose a major punishment when the chargesheet they had filed against the man mentioned a provision dealing with minor misconduct.

The counsel stated that the proceedings were legally incorrect because the chargesheet did not have lists of documents and witnesses, and the authorities had also failed to provide certain relevant documents despite the man’s written request, because of which he was not able to properly defend himself.



Advocates S K Sinha and Sanchita Dey Pal Chaudhury, appearing for the bank, argued that returning the money of the customers did not correct the misconduct of the man. The counsel stated that the mention of minor misconduct instead of major misconduct was just an error, and the allegations in the chargesheet were clearly described as major misconduct.

The counsel contended that the man had not shown how any alleged irregularity had actually affected his defence and that only pointing out a defect in the proceedings was not enough; the man had to establish that the defect deprived him of “a fair opportunity” to defend himself.

Noting that the chargesheet had clearly described the allegations as major misconduct and mentioned the dates, amounts and details of the transactions. The high court stated that the disciplinary proceedings could not be held wrong only because an incorrect clause was given in the chargesheet.

The high court rejected the man’s claim that relevant documents had not been provided to him because he had failed to state which essential document had been withheld or explain how its absence affected his defence.



The high court observed that the allegations against the man were not about a single incident but involved repeated irregularities and that such behaviour was a serious breach of the trust placed in a bank employee. The bench further stated that subsequent refunds could not erase the misconduct of the man because “a bank employee is expected to adhere to the prescribed procedures at the time of undertaking financial transactions”.

World.title: NCERT issues advisory, says supplied books can be rejected if printing not up to mark
World.content:
The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has issued an advisory to all its empanelled printing presses, directing them to strictly follow prescribed quality standards while printing and supplying textbooks. The council has warned that books failing to meet the required standards can be rejected, while printing presses responsible for substandard supplies may face penalties, cancellation of allotted work and even blacklisting.

In a statement, NCERT said it had received several complaints from different parts of the country about the poor printing quality of its textbooks and other publications available in the market. The complaints include concerns over inferior printing, which the council said affects the overall quality and acceptability of its publications and undermines its reputation and credibility.

The advisory directs all empanelled printing presses to exercise greater care and ensure quality checks at every stage of printing and book production. They have been asked to maintain prescribed standards in printing, colour reproduction, registration, finishing, binding and overall workmanship. The council has also stressed that presses must use appropriate machinery, skilled manpower and adequate quality-control mechanisms to ensure defect-free production and timely delivery.

In its statement, NCERT said:

“Any deviation from the prescribed specifications, negligence in maintaining quality standards or supply of substandard books shall be viewed seriously.” 

The council has also made it clear that action will be taken against printing presses found violating the prescribed standards. Depending on the nature of the violation, this could include financial penalties, rejection of supplied books, cancellation of allotted work, termination of contracts and revocation of empanelment. In serious cases, presses may also be debarred or blacklisted, as permitted under the applicable tender conditions and contractual provisions.

Why has NCERT issued the advisory?

The latest advisory follows complaints about the quality of printing in NCERT textbooks, particularly reports of blurred and unclear text in some school books. The issue gained attention after Vineet Jindal, a Supreme Court lawyer, raised concerns about the printing quality of a Class 10 NCERT textbook in a post on X.

Jindal said the text in his son’s textbook was extremely small, blurred and poorly printed, making it difficult for students to read comfortably. He also flagged concerns about the possible discomfort caused to children while reading books with unclear printing.

Taking cognisance of the complaints, NCERT had earlier said it was examining the matter on priority and that strict action would be initiated against any printer found responsible. The council reiterated its commitment to providing clear and readable textbooks for schoolchildren.



The latest advisory formalises the quality requirements expected from printing presses working with the council and warns that failure to meet them could have contractual consequences.

NCERT is responsible for developing and publishing school textbooks and other educational resources used across the country. Its textbooks are prescribed in several schools affiliated with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and are also used by other educational institutions. The quality of printing is therefore important to ensure that students can read and use the prescribed learning material without difficulty.

World.title: Man travelling on Srinagar-Delhi flight loses checked-in bag, airline told to pay Rs 28,000
World.content:
The Srinagar consumer commission has directed an airline to pay Rs 28,000 as compensation to a passenger whose checked-in cabin bag went missing during a flight from Srinagar to Delhi. The commission found that the airline had accepted the bag at Srinagar airport but failed to deliver it at the destination, and could not provide a satisfactory explanation for its disappearance.

Commission president Farah Deeba and member Shabnum Munshi were hearing a complaint filed by a 33-year-old man who was travelling with his mother in 2022.

“The loss of an entire bag during air travel, followed by repeated unsuccessful enquiries, an inconclusive investigation and failure to pay even the amount offered, would undoubtedly cause inconvenience and distress to a passenger,” the November 3 order read.



Airline asked to check-in luggage

The man claimed that he and his mother travelled from Srinagar to Delhi on December 21, 2022, on the airline. He carried a laptop bag and a brown cabin bag (stroller), while his mother had a blue stroller bag. According to the man, while checking in at the airport, he asked the airline staff at the check-in counter whether he could carry his bags in his hands, but the staff declined and asked him to deliver them at the check-in counter. He accordingly did so.

After landing in Delhi, the man claimed that after waiting for more than an hour, he received only one blue stroller bag. He approached the airline and got to know from the staff at the airport that his brown stroller was missing, which led to the filing of a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) by the airline staff. He added that despite repeatedly enquiring about the status of the missing bag from the airline, he got no satisfactory response.

Later, after 20 days, the airline allegedly mailed the complainant that they could not trace the baggage and, as such, the same had been declared lost, and further offered a meagre amount of Rs 1,800 for the lost baggage. However, the man claimed that his lost baggage contained some valuable items like jeans, jacket, shirts, sweater, pants, etc and he had to buy new clothes in Delhi, incurring an additional expenditure of Rs 3,000.

He then provided his bank details for transfer of Rs 1,800 without any prejudice to his rights. However, it was alleged that the airline did not even transfer the said meagre amount to him. Aggrieved, he moved the commission alleging immense pain, agony, harassment and financial loss due to their deficient service. He was represented through advocate Syed Manzoor.



Airline’s defence

The airline, through advocate Syed Falsal Qadri, argued that hand baggage not exceeding 7 kg can be taken on the flight and any baggage exceeding 7 kg in weight has to be checked in as per the procedure.

It was submitted that the airline has consistently provided timely and appropriate responses to the complainant about the investigation being carried out regarding the missing bag. The airline claimed that they have made every effort to trace the missing bag and even checked the CCTV footage to identify the lost baggage. However, it added that, due to the poor quality of the footage, they could not identify the bag.

It was argued that the airline offered Rs 1,800 as compensation, but the complainant had an intention to proceed with the instant complaint even after receiving the compensation.

‘Airline liable’

The commission highlighted that the fact that the complainant was travelling with his mother, who is stated to have a knee ailment, is relevant in assessing the inconvenience caused to him. It also pointed out that once the airline accepted the bag at its counter as checked-in baggage, it assumed responsibility for its safe carriage and delivery at the destination.



“The question whether the bag could originally have been carried in the cabin is, therefore, not decisive after its acceptance as checked-in baggage by the airline,” it added.

It added that the airline’s own witness admitted that the bag was last recorded at Srinagar and did not reach Delhi. “The relevant system report and statement of the check-in staff were not produced; the CCTV investigation was inconclusive; and even the amount offered by the airline was not paid,” it added.

The commission clarified that the authorities relied upon by the airline do not absolve it of its obligation to account for the baggage accepted by it. “The mere assertion that an investigation was conducted cannot substitute proof of proper handling and delivery of the baggage,” it held.

The commission directed the airline to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation to the complainant on account of loss of baggage. It also directed the airline to pay a sum of Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs.



Takeaway

The ruling reiterates that an airline assumes responsibility for the safe carriage and delivery of baggage once it accepts it as checked-in luggage.

For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states (Jammu and Kashmir: 1800 180 7114) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
